bio_parts_en.value: Liu Hong was the son of the marquis Chang of Xieduting.

died without issue, and Empress Dowager Dou with Dou Wu raised the twelve-year-old Hong as Emperor Ling — the curtain rises on the last act of Eastern Han.

In the very first year of his reign, Dou Wu and Chen Fan's plot against the eunuchs failed and cost them their lives; the eunuchs struck back, the second proscription began, and six or seven hundred famous men of the realm were barred from office. For the next twenty years the eunuchs and the consorts took turns at power while the emperor turned his attention elsewhere: in the first Guanghe year he opened office sales at the West Garden, with set prices for dukes, ministers, and provincial governors — even the Three Dukes could be bought; in the same year he founded the Hongdu Academy, choosing scholars for calligraphy and letters against the classicists of the Grand Academy; in the second Zhongping year he built the Hall of Ten Thousand Gold to hoard money at the West Garden. Four hundred years of the Han inheritance had become, in Ling's hands, goods with a price tag.

In the first Zhongping year Zhang Jiao of Julu gathered followers through the Way of Great Peace, and the Yellow Turban revolt erupted — "eight provinces rose together, and the realm answered." Ling lifted the proscription to rally the scholars, and Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun suppressed the revolt; but the power of provincial governors grew from that war, and the regional strongmen each held troops of their own. The realm of Han was already coming apart. In the fifth Zhongping year he created the Eight Colonels of the West Garden, among them Yuan Shao and Cao Cao — this imperial guard would become the roster of the coming warlord age.

In the sixth Zhongping year Ling died at thirty-four, leaving an empire in tatters: eunuchs and scholars at each other's throats, Yellow Turban remnants across the provinces, and frontier warlords closing in.

was deposed by Dong Zhuo within months, and Eastern Han entered its last age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 8 (Benji of Emperor Ling), and the biographies of the Proscribed Partisans, Chen Fan, and Huangfu Song; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). # 汉少帝辩 · 主要事迹

刘辩是[[e-han-ling|灵帝]]之子，何皇后所生。中平六年灵帝崩，辩即位，何太后临朝，大将军何进秉政。东汉的最后一场宫廷剧，就在这几个月内演完。

何进欲诛宦官，却迟疑不决，反召四方兵将入京示威——包括并州牧董卓。事泄，宦官张让等先发制人，杀何进；袁绍等率兵入宫，尽诛宦官二千余人，「十常侍乱」的结局，是宦官与外戚同归于尽。随后入京的董卓成了唯一的赢家：九月，董卓废少帝辩为弘农王，立陈留王刘协，即[[e-han-xian|献帝]]。

辩在位不足半年，被废后幽于阁上。初平元年正月，董卓遣郎中令李儒进鸩，辩临终与妻唐姬作诀别歌，时年十四。他一生没有做过任何决策，却亲身见证了东汉皇权最后的崩塌：在他之前，皇帝尚是外戚与宦官争夺的猎物；在他之后，皇帝成了军阀手里的印玺。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷008《孝灵帝纪》、卷009《孝献帝纪》、《董卓传》、《何进传》，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Bian was the son of

by Empress He. When Ling died in the sixth Zhongping year, Bian took the throne with Empress Dowager He in the regency and General-in-Chief He Jin in power. The last court drama of Eastern Han was played out in these few months.

He Jin meant to destroy the eunuchs, but hesitated and instead summoned troops from the provinces to overawe the court — including Dong Zhuo, governor of Bingzhou. The plot leaked; the eunuchs led by Zhang Rang struck first and slew He Jin; Yuan Shao and others stormed the palace and slaughtered more than two thousand eunuchs. The "chaos of the Ten Attendants" ended with eunuchs and consorts destroying each other. Dong Zhuo, arriving on cue, was the sole victor: in the ninth month he deposed Bian as Prince of Hongnong and raised the prince of Chenliu, Xie, as

.

Bian had reigned under half a year. Deposed, he was shut up in a tower; in the first month of the first Chuping year Dong Zhuo sent Li Ru with poisoned wine. Bian sang a farewell to his wife Tang Ji as he drank, and died at fourteen. He never made a single decision of his own, yet he witnessed the final collapse of Han sovereignty: before him the emperor had been the prize fought over by consorts and eunuchs; after him, the emperor became a seal in the hands of warlords.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 8 (Benji of Emperor Ling), ch. 9 (Benji of Emperor Xian), and the biographies of Dong Zhuo and He Jin; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). emperors.bio_md:
# 汉献帝 · 主要事迹

刘协是[[e-han-ling|灵帝]]次子。中平六年，董卓废[[e-han-shao-bian|少帝辩]]，立年九岁的刘协，是为献帝——汉家四百年天下的最后一位皇帝，从此开始了他作为「流动的玉玺」的三十一年。

初平元年，董卓逼迁长安，焚洛阳宫室，东汉中枢第一次流离失所；初平三年，王允与吕布诛董卓，旋为李傕、郭汜所败，长安再乱。兴平二年，献帝出长安东归，一路为乱兵所劫，食枣栗度日，流离曹阳、弘农之间。建安元年，曹操迎帝都许，「奉天子以令不臣」——献帝终于有了一个固定的都城，也终于有了一个不可摆脱的主人。

都许之后的二十四年，是曹操父子经营天下的二十四年，也是献帝作为禅让道具的二十四年：建安五年官渡之战、十三年赤壁之战，皆在许都的名义下进行；建安十九年，曹操杀伏皇后，献帝只能默然；二十五年（延康元年），曹丕受禅，献帝逊位，封山阳公，东汉正式灭亡。他做了三十一年皇帝，从未有过一天的实权，却以「建安」年号为名，见证了整个三国格局的形成。

逊位后的献帝在山阳做了十四年公，于魏明帝青龙二年薨，年五十四，以汉天子礼葬。史评「得位屯蹇，版荡云海」，正是他一生最贴切的注脚：汉祚四百年，始于[[e-han-guangwu|光武]]之中兴，终于献帝之禅代。

> 本地参考：点校本《后汉书》卷009《孝献帝纪》、《董卓传》，《三国志》武帝纪、文帝纪，谭图第 2 册（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Xie was the second son of
. In the sixth Zhongping year, Dong Zhuo deposed

and raised the nine-year-old Xie as Emperor Xian — the last emperor of the four-hundred-year Han, beginning his thirty-one years as a "movable imperial seal."

In the first Chuping year Dong Zhuo forced the court to Chang'an, burning the palaces of Luoyang: the Eastern Han center was uprooted for the first time. In the third Chuping year Wang Yun and Lü Bu killed Dong Zhuo, only to be overthrown by Li Jue and Guo Si; Chang'an fell into chaos again. In the second Xingping year the emperor left Chang'an and fled east, robbed by the soldiery on the road, living on dates and chestnuts, drifting through Caoyang and Hongnong. In the first Jian'an year Cao Cao received the emperor and settled the court at Xu — "supporting the Son of Heaven to command the disobedient." Xian at last had a fixed capital, and at last a master he could never shake.

The twenty-four years at Xu were the years of the Cao house's conquest of the realm, and of Xian's role as the prop of an abdication: the Guandu campaign of Jian'an 5 and the Red Cliffs of Jian'an 13 were fought under his name; in Jian'an 19 Cao Cao slew Empress Fu, and Xian could only be silent; in the first Yankang year (220) Cao Pi received the abdication, and Xian was enfeoffed Duke of Shanyang. Eastern Han was formally finished. He had been emperor for thirty-one years without a single day of real power, yet under his "Jian'an" era name the whole Three Kingdoms pattern took shape.

As Duke of Shanyang he lived another fourteen years, dying in the second Qinglong year of Wei at fifty-four, buried with the rites of a Han emperor. The historians' verdict — "he got the throne in hardship and drifting, tossed on the waves of the age" — fits him exactly: the Han mandate, opened by

's restoration, closed with Xian's abdication.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 9 (Benji of Emperor Xian) and the biography of Dong Zhuo; the *Sanguozhi*, biographies of Emperor Wu (Cao Cao) and Emperor Wen (Cao Pi); Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

timeline.summary: 幸广陵故城，临江观兵，见江涛汹涌而退。

timeline.title: 再幸广陵

emperors.bio_md:
# 魏文帝 · 主要事迹

曹丕字子桓，曹操次子，母卞氏。少有逸才，好文学，善骑射，与父及曹植同列建安文坛。建安二十二年，曹操立为魏太子，与曹植争储历十年而终定。延康元年（220）正月曹操崩，丕继魏王位；同年十月，汉献帝禅位，丕即皇帝位于繁阳，改元黄初，国号魏，都洛阳——汉祚四百载至此而绝，魏晋禅代之局由此开启。

文帝在位七年，立制多于用武：改正朔、定服色、行郊祀，重建开国礼仪；用陈群议，立九品官人法，开魏晋南北朝门阀之端；又贬抑宗室诸王为县侯，防藩镇之祸。用武则三路伐吴无大功，两幸广陵临江而不得渡，终未越长江一步。性刻急，杀鲍勋等谏臣，史有微辞。

黄初七年五月，崩于洛阳嘉福殿，年四十，明帝叡即位。陈寿评曰「天资文藻，下笔成章」，惜乎「若加之旷大之度，励以公平之诚，迈志存道，岂不闲哉」。其所著《典论·论文》开中国文学批评之先河，「文章经国之大业，不朽之盛事」一语传诵至今；建安风骨与魏制新典，皆以文帝为承转之人。

> 本地参考：点校本《三国志》卷002《文帝纪》、卷012《鲍勋传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Cao Pi, styled Zihuan, was Cao Cao's second son by Lady Bian. Gifted early in letters, fond of literature, and skilled at riding and archery, he stood with his father and Cao Zhi at the heart of the Jian'an literary circle. In the 22nd year of Jian'an (217) Cao Cao made him heir of Wei, ending the decade-long rivalry with Cao Zhi. In the first month of Yankang 1 (220) Cao Cao died and Pi inherited the kingship; that October Emperor Xian abdicated, Pi took the throne at Fanyang, changed the era to Huangchu, styled the realm Wei, and made Luoyang his capital — the four-hundred-year Han line was cut, and the Wei–Jin cycle of abdications began.

His seven years were richer in institutions than in arms: he fixed the calendar, vestments, and sacrifices, rebuilding the rites of a founding dynasty; on Chen Qun's counsel he established the nine-rank method of appointing officials, opening the era of the great clans; and he reduced the imperial princes to county marquises to guard against feudatory danger. In arms, the three-pronged campaign against Wu gained nothing, and twice he toured Guangling without ever crossing the Yangzi. His temper was harsh: Bao Xun and other remonstrants were put to death, drawing the historians' censure.

In the fifth month of Huangchu 7 he died in the Jiafu Hall at Luoyang, aged forty, and Emperor Ming (Cao Rui) succeeded. Chen Shou judged him "gifted of literary talent, writing at the brush's touch," while regretting the want of magnanimity. His *Dianlun: On Literature* founded Chinese literary criticism; "literary composition is the great enterprise of statecraft, the glorious work of the imperishable" still echoes — in both letters and institutions, Wen of Wei stands as the hinge of his age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Sanguozhi*, ch. 2 ("Benji of Emperor Wen"), ch. 12 (biography of Bao Xun) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

timeline.summary_en: He raised the Luoyang Palace, the Zhaoyang and Taiji halls, driving tens of thousands to labor, and put many remonstrants to death.

timeline.title: 明帝崩托孤

timeline.summary_en: Mortally ill, he made his adopted son, Cao Fang of Qi, heir and entrusted him to Cao Shuang and Sima Yi, then died.

emperors.bio_md:
# 魏明帝 · 主要事迹

曹叡字元仲，文帝子，母甄氏，幼有岐嶷之姿。黄初七年文帝崩，叡即皇帝位，年二十二。其治之要，在拒敌于西陲、平乱于辽东：太和二年诸葛亮首出祁山，张郃破马谡于街亭；其后亮屡出无功，青龙二年屯五丈原，与司马懿相持百馀日，病卒军中——蜀之北伐，至此而衰。景初二年司马懿率军四万攻辽东，破襄平，斩公孙渊，魏境遂至朝鲜边界。

明帝之失，在大营宫室：起洛阳宫、昭阳殿、太极殿，役民数万，群臣谏者多遭诛戮。改元景初、亲定历法，亦见其好断自任。陈寿评其「沈毅好断，任意不恤下人，故能奋其威明」，然「不能尽礼于太后，慎终追远」之讥，亦不可免。

景初三年正月，明帝疾笃，急召司马懿于辽东，执其手立养子曹芳为嗣，托孤于曹爽、司马懿，寻崩，年三十六。十年之后，高平陵之变起，曹氏之权尽归司马氏——明帝之托孤，实为曹魏存亡之枢机：任懿以平辽拒蜀，则功在社稷；托孤于懿，则祸胎后嗣。功过相权，后世论者每致慨焉。

> 本地参考：点校本《三国志》卷003《明帝纪》、卷035《诸葛亮传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Cao Rui, styled Yuanzhong, son of Emperor Wen by Lady Zhen, showed unusual promise from childhood. On Emperor Wen's death in the 7th year of Huangchu he took the throne at twenty-two. His reign was defined by holding the west and pacifying the northeast: in the 2nd year of Taihe (228), in Zhuge Liang's first northern expedition, Zhang He broke Ma Su at Jieting; the later expeditions gained nothing, and in the 2nd year of Qinglong Liang camped on the Wuzhang Plain, faced Sima Yi for over a hundred days, and died of illness in camp — the Shu offensive never recovered. In the 2nd year of Jingchu Sima Yi marched forty thousand men on Liaodong, stormed Xiangping, beheaded Gongsun Yuan, and carried Wei's border to the Korean frontier.

Ming's failing was the great palace works: the Luoyang Palace and the Zhaoyang and Taiji halls rose on tens of thousands of laborers while remonstrants were put to death. His changes of era and calendar showed the same self-willed decisiveness. Chen Shou's verdict — "resolute and self-assured, heedless of those beneath him, able to display his stern brilliance" — concedes his power while noting his want of duty to the empress dowager.

In the first month of the 3rd year of Jingchu, mortally ill, he summoned Sima Yi from Liaodong, took his hand, named his adopted son Cao Fang heir, and entrusted him to Cao Shuang and Sima Yi; he died at thirty-six. Ten years later came the Gaopingling incident, and Wei's power passed wholly to the Simas. His regency trust was the hinge of Wei's fate: Sima Yi, the man who won Liaodong and held Zhuge Liang at bay, was the same man whose house would take the realm.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Sanguozhi*, ch. 3 ("Benji of Emperor Ming"), ch. 35 (biography of Zhuge Liang) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.summary_en: Adopted heir of Emperor Ming, he came to the throne at eight, power resting with Cao Shuang and Sima Yi; after the Gaopingling incident Sima's house ruled alone, and in the 6th year of Jiaping he was deposed as Prince of Qi.

emperors.bio_md:
# 齐王芳 · 主要事迹

曹芳字兰卿，明帝养子，一说任城王曹楷之子。景初三年正月，明帝疾笃，立为皇太子，寻即帝位，年八岁，改元正始，曹爽、司马懿并受遗诏辅政。正始十年正月，帝与曹爽兄弟谒高平陵，司马懿以太后诏勒兵，收其兵权，诛曹爽三族——史称高平陵之变。自此魏之政柄尽归司马氏，帝徒居大位而已。

其后王凌谋立楚王彪，事泄自杀；李丰、张缉等欲除司马师，亦被族诛。帝自即位至废，正始、嘉平两朝，凡十五年间，外朝之变皆系司马家之兴替，帝无一语得与。嘉平六年，司马师以帝「荒淫无度」奏废，芳出为齐王，迁居河内。

正元元年，高贵乡公曹髦即位，芳以齐王终其身。晋泰始十年薨，晋以王礼葬。史家论齐王芳：以冲龄践祚，本无可为，而「曹爽之诛，实启司马之篡」——高平陵一役，不独废一人、易一君，乃曹魏国祚之所系。芳之见废，史称其自取，然冲主何罪，权臣之欲而已。

> 本地参考：点校本《三国志》卷004《三少帝纪》、卷009《曹爽传》、卷044《司马懿传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Cao Fang, styled Lanqing, was Emperor Ming's adopted son, said to be a son of Cao Kai of Rencheng. In the first month of the 3rd year of Jingchu, in Ming's last illness, he was named crown prince and at once took the throne at eight, changing the era to Zhengshi, with Cao Shuang and Sima Yi as co-regents by the late edict. In the first month of the 10th year of Zhengshi, while the emperor and Shuang paid homage at the Gaopingling tombs, Sima Yi seized the armies on forged decrees and exterminated Shuang's kin — the Gaopingling incident. From that day Wei's government lay with the Simas, and the emperor sat on the throne without a voice.

Wang Ling's plot to set up Prince Biao of Chu failed, and Ling took his own life; Li Feng and Zhang Ji, plotting against Sima Shi, were executed with their kin. Through Zhengshi and Jiaping, fifteen years, every turn of court affairs was the rise and fall of Sima's house, and the emperor had not one word in it. In the 6th year of Jiaping, Sima Shi petitioned the empress dowager to depose Fang for "dissolute excess"; Fang was set aside as Prince of Qi and moved to Henei.

The Duke of Gaogui District succeeded him, and Fang lived out his days as Prince of Qi, dying in the 10th year of Jin Taishi. The historians' judgment: a child sovereign could do nothing, yet the slaying of Cao Shuang began the Sima usurpation — the Gaopingling incident deposed more than one man; it was the fate of the Wei dynasty. Fang's fall was blamed on himself by the official historians, but a child emperor's "fault" was only the strong minister's will.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Sanguozhi*, ch. 4 ("Annals of the Three Young Sovereigns"), ch. 9 (biography of Cao Shuang), ch. 44 (biography of Sima Yi) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.summary_en: Called to the throne after Cao Fang's deposition, he was a scholar-emperor set on rooting out the Simas; in the 5th year of Ganlu he led his guards against Sima Zhao and was slain beneath the southern gate, aged twenty.

timeline.summary_en: With Cao Fang deposed, Sima Shi summoned the duke of Gaogui District to the throne; the era was changed to Zhengyuan.

timeline.summary_en: The Yangzhou commander Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rose against Sima Shi; Shi campaigned in person, Jian died, and Qin fled to Wu.

timeline.title: 诸葛诞反
timeline.summary: 征东大将军诸葛诞据寿春反，司马昭围城年馀，诞败死。
timeline.summary_en: The general Zhuge Dan rose from Shouchun; Sima Zhao besieged the city for over a year until Dan fell and died.

timeline.title: 讨司马昭被弑

timeline.summary_en: The emperor sallied forth with his palace guards, and Jia Chong of Sima Zhao's party ordered Cheng Ji to slay him beneath the southern gate — as the Han–Jin Annals, quoted by Pei Songzhi, records.

timeline.title: 立常道乡公

timeline.summary_en: After the slaying, Sima Zhao installed Cao Huan, marquis of Changdao District, who became the last Wei emperor.

emperors.bio_md:
# 高贵乡公 · 主要事迹

曹髦字彦士，文帝孙，东海定王曹霖之子，封高贵乡公。嘉平六年，齐王芳被废，司马师迎立髦，年十三，改元正元。髦好学有成人之量，即位后屡与诸儒论经于朝堂，有「帝王之学」之誉；然政柄在司马氏，正元二年毌丘俭、文钦起兵讨师，甘露二年诸葛诞据寿春反昭，皆不平而败。

甘露五年五月，帝以司马昭弑君之心日显，召侍中王沈、尚书王经等密议，曰：「司马昭之心，路人所知也。吾不能坐受废辱，今日当与卿等自出讨之。」遂率殿中宿卫苍头官僮鼓噪而出，自讨司马昭。昭之党羽贾充命成济抽戈犯跸，帝崩于南阙之下，年二十。以天子之尊，冲锋蹈刃，亘古未有，事见《汉晋春秋》裴注。

帝既弑，司马昭以太后令罪帝「悖逆不道」，废为庶人，迎立常道乡公曹奂。后世论曹髦：以英锐之资，处必亡之势，明知不济而为之，其节可哀，其志可敬。三国之君，自汉献帝以下，皆苟且图存，独高贵乡公以死殉社稷——「司马昭之心」成语流传千古，正是民心所向的定评。

> 本地参考：点校本《三国志》卷004《三少帝纪》及裴注引《汉晋春秋》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Cao Mao, styled Yanshi, was a grandson of Emperor Wen, son of Cao Lin, Prince Ding of Donghai, enfeoffed Duke of Gaogui District. In the 6th year of Jiaping, after Cao Fang's deposition, Sima Shi installed Mao at thirteen, changing the era to Zhengyuan. He was a student with an adult's gravity, debating the classics with the scholars at court, earning the name of a philosopher-sovereign; but the government lay with the Simas. In the 2nd year of Zhengyuan Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rose against Shi; in the 2nd year of Ganlu Zhuge Dan rose from Shouchun against Sima Zhao — both rose and both fell without result.

In the fifth month of the 5th year of Ganlu, with Sima Zhao's ambition plain, the emperor summoned Wang Shen, Wang Jing, and the others and said: "Sima Zhao's heart is known to every man on the road. I cannot sit and await disgrace — today I shall go out against him myself." He sallied forth with his palace guards, servants, and lads against Sima Zhao. Jia Chong of Zhao's party ordered Cheng Ji to strike; the emperor was slain beneath the southern gate, aged twenty. That an emperor should charge the spears in person was unheard of — the deed is recorded in the *Han–Jin Annals*, preserved in Pei Songzhi's commentary.

After the slaying, Sima Zhao blamed the emperor by the empress dowager's edict, degraded him to commoner, and installed Cao Huan, marquis of Changdao District. Posterity judges Cao Mao: of sharp spirit in a doomed position, he acted knowing he could not win — his constancy is pitiable, his resolve admirable. Of the Three Kingdoms' emperors, from Emperor Xian on, all clung to life; only the Duke of Gaogui District died for his altars. "Sima Zhao's heart" has passed into the language as the verdict of the people.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Sanguozhi*, ch. 4 ("Annals of the Three Young Sovereigns") and the commentary citing the *Han–Jin Annals* (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 魏元帝 · 主要事迹

曹奂字景明，武帝孙，燕王曹宇之子，封常道乡公。甘露五年，高贵乡公被弑，司马昭迎立奂，改元景元。奂即位时年十五，明知前车之鉴，遂恭顺为君，惟命是从：景元四年，诏钟会、邓艾伐蜀，蜀亡；景元五年，钟会据蜀谋反，兵变被杀，邓艾亦为卫瓘所杀。灭蜀之功尽归司马氏，而帝不过画诺而已。

咸熙二年八月司马昭卒，其子司马炎袭晋王位。十二月，炎受禅，奂逊位，封陈留王，魏之社稷凡四十五年而终。泰安元年，奂薨于洛阳，年五十七，晋以王礼葬于邺，谥曰元。

曹魏之亡，与其说亡于元帝，不如说亡于高平陵一役后司马氏之渐积：自芳、髦至于奂，三帝皆坐受废立之柄，史称「魏之失政，始于文、明之托，成于高平之变」。奂以让国之君终，与其先辈禅汉之事相映——汉献帝禅于曹，曹奂禅于司马，天道循环，史家或引为讥讽：文帝受禅于繁阳之坛，其子孙终亦面北而称臣。

> 本地参考：点校本《三国志》卷004《三少帝纪》、卷003《明帝纪》及晋书卷003《武帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Cao Huan, styled Jingming, was a grandson of Emperor Wu, son of Cao Yu, prince of Yan, enfeoffed Marquis of Changdao District. After the slaying of the Duke of Gaogui District, Sima Zhao installed Huan at fifteen, changing the era to Jingyuan. Mindful of his predecessor's fate, Huan kept a compliant silence, assenting to everything: in the 4th year of Jingyuan, on his edict, Zhong Hui and Deng Ai invaded and destroyed Shu; in the 5th year, Zhong Hui rebelled from Shu and was killed in a mutiny, and Deng Ai was put to death by Wei Guan. The conquest of Shu redounded wholly to the Simas; the emperor only nodded.

In the eighth month of the 2nd year of Xianxi Sima Zhao died, and his son Yan succeeded to the kingship of Jin. That December Yan received the abdication; Huan stepped down, was enfeoffed Duke of Chenliu, and the Wei altars, after forty-five years, came to an end. In the 1st year of Tai'an he died at Luoyang at fifty-seven, and Jin buried him with princely rites at Ye, posthumously styled Yuan.

Wei did not fall to its last emperor but to the long drift that began at Gaopingling: from Fang to Mao to Huan, three sovereigns sat at the mercy of deposition. The historians write that Wei's loss of government began with Wen and Ming's regency trust and was completed at Gaopingling. Huan's abdication mirrors his house's own act — Emperor Xian had abdicated to Cao, and Cao Huan abdicated to the Simas: the wheel turned, and the historians mark the irony that Wen of Wei, who took the throne on the Fanyang altar, saw his descendants bow to the south as vassals.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Sanguozhi*, ch. 4 ("Annals of the Three Young Sovereigns"), ch. 3 ("Benji of Emperor Ming"), and the *Jinshu*, ch. 3 ("Benji of Emperor Wu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

timeline.title: 生涿郡
timeline.summary: 汉景帝子中山靖王胜之后，家贫，与母贩履织席为业。
timeline.summary_en: A descendant of Liu Sheng, Prince Jing of Zhongshan, son of Emperor Jing of Han, he grew up poor, selling straw shoes and mats with his mother.

timeline.title: 与黄巾战
timeline.summary: 黄巾起，备率徒众从军征讨，以功除安喜尉。
timeline.summary_en: When the Yellow Turbans rose, Bei led his followers into the army, earning by merit the post of commandant of Anxi.

timeline.title: 归曹操又叛
timeline.summary: 失徐州依曹操，操厚待之；寻与董承谋泄，走归袁绍。
timeline.summary_en: Losing Xuzhou he took refuge with Cao Cao, who treated him generously; but the plot with Dong Cheng leaked, and he fled to Yuan Shao.

timeline.title: 赤壁联合抗曹
timeline.summary: 曹操南下，诸葛亮说孙权，孙刘联军大破曹军于赤壁。
timeline.summary_en: Cao Cao came south; Zhuge Liang persuaded Sun Quan, and the Sun–Liu allies shattered the Cao army at the Red Cliffs.

timeline.title: 得益州
timeline.summary: 刘璋迎备入蜀，备反攻取成都，得益州，自领益州牧。
timeline.summary_en: Liu Zhang invited Bei into Shu; Bei turned on him, took Chengdu, won Yizhou, and styled himself its governor.

timeline.title: 汉中称王
timeline.summary: 与曹操争汉中，大胜，遂于沔阳进位汉中王。
timeline.summary_en: Vying with Cao Cao for Hanzhong, he won decisively and took the title King of Hanzhong at Mianyang.

timeline.title: 关羽失荆州
timeline.summary: 关羽北伐襄樊，吕蒙袭取江陵，羽败被杀，荆州归吴。
timeline.summary_en: While Guan Yu campaigned north to Xiangfan, Lü Meng seized Jiangling behind him; Yu fell and was slain, and Jingzhou passed to Wu.

timeline.title: 即皇帝位
timeline.summary: 闻汉献帝被害（讹传），于成都即皇帝位，国号汉，以续汉统。
timeline.summary_en: On the rumored death of Emperor Xian, he took the throne at Chengdu, styling his realm Han in continuation of the Han line.

timeline.title: 伐吴
timeline.summary: 为关羽复仇，亲率大军伐吴；赵云、诸葛亮等谏不听。
timeline.summary_en: To avenge Guan Yu he led the host against Wu in person, deaf to the remonstrances of Zhao Yun and Zhuge Liang.

timeline.title: 夷陵之败
timeline.summary: 陆逊火烧连营，备大败，退保白帝城，仅以身免。
timeline.summary_en: Lu Xun burned the linked camps; Bei was routed, fled to White Emperor City, and escaped with his life alone.

timeline.title: 崩于永安
timeline.summary: 病笃，托孤于诸葛亮，崩于永安宫，年六十三，后主禅即位。
timeline.summary_en: Mortally ill, he entrusted his heir to Zhuge Liang and died in the Yong'an Palace, aged sixty-three; Liu Shan, the Later Sovereign, succeeded.

timeline.title: 先主总评
timeline.summary: 陈寿评其弘毅宽厚、知人待士，有高祖之风、英雄之器，惜机权干略不逮。
timeline.summary_en: Chen Shou praised his magnanimity, his discernment of men, and his treatment of officers — the manner of Gaozu and the bearing of a hero — while regretting that his cunning and resource fell short.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉昭烈帝 · 主要事迹

刘备字玄德，涿郡涿县人，汉景帝子中山靖王刘胜之后。少孤，与母贩履织席为业；然有大志，「好交结豪侠，年少争附之」。中平元年黄巾起，备率徒众从军征讨，以功除安喜尉，自此投身乱世三十馀年：辗转公孙瓒、陶谦、吕布、曹操、袁绍、刘表之间，败多胜少，然「信义著于四海」，士人多归之。

建安十二年，诸葛亮隆中对策，为备画三分之策；建安十三年赤壁，孙刘联军破曹操，备据荆州四郡。建安十九年得益州，二十四年争汉中，大破曹军，遂于沔阳进位汉中王——「汉中之战」定三分之局。同年关羽失荆州，身死江陵，蜀吴联盟破裂。

章武元年，备闻献帝被害（实为讹传），于成都即皇帝位，国号汉，续汉家正统。为报关羽之仇，七月亲率大军伐吴；赵云、诸葛亮等力谏不听。章武二年，陆逊于夷陵火烧连营，备大败，仅以身免，退保白帝城，次年崩于永安宫，年六十三，临终托孤于诸葛亮，曰：「若嗣子可辅，辅之；如其不才，君可自取。」

陈寿评先主「弘毅宽厚，知人待士，盖有高祖之风，英雄之器焉」，惜「机权干略，不逮魏武」。然以贩履之身起家，数败不馁，终成鼎足之业，其「勿以恶小而为之，勿以善小而不为」之遗训，仁德之名，流传千古，为三国君主中最得民心者。

> 本地参考：点校本《三国志》卷032《先主传》、卷035《诸葛亮传》、卷047《吴主传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

Liu Bei, styled Xuande, was a native of Zhuoxian, Zhuojun, a descendant of Liu Sheng, Prince Jing of Zhongshan, son of Emperor Jing of Han. Orphaned young, he sold straw shoes and mats with his mother; yet he was ambitious, "delighting in company with heroes, so that the young flocked to him." In the 1st year of Zhongping the Yellow Turbans rose, and Bei led his followers into the army, earning by merit the commandancy of Anxi. Then began more than thirty years of drift through the realm — under Gongsun Zan, Tao Qian, Lü Bu, Cao Cao, Yuan Shao, Liu Biao — more defeats than victories, yet his "good faith was renowned within the four seas," and men of worth came to him.

In the 12th year of Jian'an, Zhuge Liang laid out the tripartite plan at Longzhong; in the 13th, at the Red Cliffs, the Sun–Liu allies broke Cao Cao, and Bei took the four commanderies of Jingzhou. In the 19th year he won Yizhou, and in the 24th, after the great struggle for Hanzhong, he routed the Cao army and took the title King of Hanzhong at Mianyang — the Hanzhong campaign fixed the tripartite balance. That same year Guan Yu lost Jingzhou and died at Jiangling, and the Shu–Wu alliance cracked.

In the 1st year of Zhangwu, on the rumored death of Emperor Xian, Bei took the throne at Chengdu, styling his realm Han in continuation of the Han line. To avenge Guan Yu he led the host against Wu in person that July, deaf to Zhao Yun and Zhuge Liang. In the 2nd year of Zhangwu, Lu Xun burned the linked camps at Yiling; Bei was shattered, escaped with his life alone, and fell back to White Emperor City. He died in the Yong'an Palace the next year at sixty-three, entrusting his heir to Zhuge Liang: "If the heir can be aided, aid him; if he is unworthy, take the throne yourself."

Chen Shou's verdict: "magnanimous, resolute, and generous, discerning in men and generous to officers — the manner of Gaozu and the bearing of a hero," yet "his cunning and resource fell short of the martial Wei." A shoemaker who never despaired through defeat after defeat, he yet built a corner of the tripartite realm; his last charge — "do no evil because it is small, omit no good because it is small" — and his name for benevolence outlived him, making him the most beloved of the Three Kingdoms' sovereigns.

emperors.summary_en: Succeeding the First Sovereign, he governed well while trusting Zhuge Liang; after Liang's death he heeded Huang Hao and the northern wars failed, until Deng Ai entered Shu in the 6th year of Jingyao and he surrendered with the seal in his mouth, enfeoffed Duke of Anle — his "happier here than in Shu" staying a byword.

emperors.bio_md:
# 蜀后主 · 主要事迹

刘禅字公嗣，先主子，母甘夫人。建安十二年生于荆州，长坂之役赖赵云单骑护持得免。章武三年先主崩，禅即位于成都，年十七，改元建兴，诸葛亮受遗诏辅政，政事无巨细皆决于亮。建兴三年亮南征，七擒孟获，南中平定；五年亮出师北伐，上《出师表》，屯汉中，连年攻魏。亮治国「科教严明，赏罚必信」，蜀汉之治于斯为盛——史称后主任贤则治。

建兴十二年，诸葛亮病卒五丈原，蒋琬、费祎相继执政，皆守成之器，蜀汉得以休息。延熙十六年费祎遇刺，姜维掌军，连年出陇西，多无大功，国力日耗；后主又信用中常侍黄皓，政事日坏，姜维避祸屯田沓中，不敢还成都。

景耀六年，魏军三路大举，邓艾出阴平、越摩天岭，破诸葛瞻于绵竹，兵临成都。谯周力主投降，后主从之，舆榇出降，蜀汉历二主四十三年而亡。后主举家迁洛阳，魏封安乐公；司马昭宴之，问曰：「颇思蜀否？」后主答：「此间乐，不思蜀。」「乐不思蜀」遂成后世笑谈。

史评曰：后主任贤相则为循理之君，惑阉竖则为昏暗之后，政之得失系于得人。其所以维持蜀汉四十馀年者，实赖诸葛亮、蒋琬、费祎之经营；而黄皓用事、姜维耗国、援兵失期，终致亡国。然以「此间乐」三字全身远祸，亦不失为乱世自全之智。

> 本地参考：点校本《三国志》卷033《后主传》、卷035《诸葛亮传》、卷044《姜维传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Shan, styled Gongsi, was the Former Sovereign's son by Lady Gan. Born in Jingzhou in the 12th year of Jian'an, he was saved at the Changban disaster by Zhao Yun's single-handed ride. On the Former Sovereign's death in the 3rd year of Zhangwu, Shan took the throne at Chengdu at seventeen, changing the era to Jianxing, with Zhuge Liang as regent by the late will; nothing in government was decided without Liang. In the 3rd year of Jianxing Liang pacified the south, capturing Meng Huo seven times; in the 5th he memorialized the *Chu Shi Biao*, garrisoned Hanzhong, and campaigned north against Wei year after year. Liang's rule — "laws and education strict and clear, rewards and punishments sure" — made Shu's government the finest of its age: the histories say that with worthy ministers the Later Sovereign ruled aright.

In the 12th year of Jianxing Liang died at the Wuzhang Plain; Jiang Wan and Fei Yi governed in turn, keepers of the established order, and Shu rested. In the 16th year of Yanxi Fei Yi was assassinated, and Jiang Wei took the armies, campaigning into Longxi year after year with little gain while the state's strength ebbed; the sovereign took the eunuch Huang Hao into his confidence, government decayed daily, and Jiang Wei, to escape the eunuch's malice, went to farm at Tazhong.

In the 6th year of Jingyao Wei invaded on three roads; Deng Ai came by the Yinping track over impossible ground, broke Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu, and reached the gates of Chengdu. On Qiao Zhou's counsel the sovereign surrendered with the coffin in his cart — Shu Han, through two sovereigns and forty-three years, was no more. Brought with his house to Luoyang, he was made Duke of Anle by Wei. At a banquet Sima Zhao asked whether he thought of Shu; he answered, "I am happy here and do not think of Shu" — "happier here than in Shu" passing into the language as a byword.

The historians' judgment: with worthy ministers he was a right-reasoning sovereign, beguiled by eunuchs a darkened one — the state's fate turned on the men he chose. That Shu held forty years was the work of Zhuge Liang, Jiang Wan, and Fei Yi; that it fell was the work of Huang Hao's power, Jiang Wei's exhausting wars, and the failure of relief. Yet "happier here" kept him alive in an age of slaughter — the self-preservation of a weakling, and perhaps a kind of wisdom.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Sanguozhi*, ch. 33 ("Biography of the Later Sovereign"), ch. 35 (biography of Zhuge Liang), ch. 44 (biography of Jiang Wei) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.summary: 继兄业据江东，赤壁破曹、袭取荆州、夷陵败备，黄龙元年称帝建业，为吴国开基之主；晚年二宫之争，立嗣两误。
emperors.summary_en: He took up his brother's enterprise in Jiangdong, broke Cao at the Red Cliffs, seized Jingzhou, defeated Bei at Yiling, and in the 1st year of Huanglong took the throne at Jianye as founder of Wu; in old age the two-palace feud wrecked the succession.

portrait.appearance_basis: 三国志载「方颐大口，目有精光」。画像宜表现任才尚计的雄主之态，衣冠从孙吴初制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary: 孙坚次子，母吴氏；兄策统事江东时已随军。
timeline.summary_en: Second son of Sun Jian by Lady Wu; he followed the armies in his elder brother Ce's conquest of Jiangdong.

timeline.title: 统事
timeline.summary: 孙策遇刺卒，权继统江东，张昭、周瑜辅之。
timeline.summary_en: Sun Ce died by an assassin's knife; Quan took command of Jiangdong with Zhang Zhao and Zhou Yu to support him.

timeline.title: 赤壁破曹
timeline.title_en: Breaking Cao at the Red Cliffs
timeline.summary: 联合刘备，周瑜火攻，大破曹军于赤壁，天下三分之势遂定。
timeline.summary_en: Allied with Liu Bei, Zhou Yu's fire attack broke the Cao army at the Red Cliffs, fixing the tripartite division of the realm.

timeline.title: 袭取荆州
timeline.summary: 吕蒙白衣渡江袭江陵，关羽败亡，吴据有荆州。
timeline.summary_en: Lü Meng's covert crossing took Jiangling, Guan Yu fell, and Wu held Jingzhou.

timeline.title: 夷陵破备
timeline.summary: 陆逊于夷陵火攻大破刘备，吴转守为攻。
timeline.summary_en: Lu Xun's fire attack at Yiling shattered Liu Bei, turning Wu from defense to offense.

timeline.title: 称帝建业
timeline.summary: 孙权于武昌即皇帝位，旋还都建业，国号吴。
timeline.summary_en: Sun Quan took the imperial throne at Wuchang and at once moved the capital back to Jianye, styling the realm Wu.

timeline.title: 辽东通使
timeline.summary: 遣使泛海通辽东公孙渊，欲结外援；渊后杀使背约。
timeline.summary_en: He sent envoys by sea to Gongsun Yuan of Liaodong seeking an ally; Yuan later slew the envoys and broke the pact.

timeline.title: 合肥新城
timeline.summary: 亲率大军攻合肥新城，久攻不下，闻魏援至而还。
timeline.summary_en: He led the host in person against the new city of Hefei, could not take it after long siege, and withdrew on word of Wei relief.

timeline.title: 太子登卒
timeline.title_en: Death of the Crown Prince Deng
timeline.summary: 皇太子孙登病卒，立嗣问题自此始。
timeline.summary_en: Crown Prince Sun Deng died of illness, and the succession question began.

timeline.title: 废太子和
timeline.summary: 二宫之争，权废太子和，赐鲁王霸死，陆逊忧愤卒。
timeline.summary_en: In the two-palace feud Quan deposed the crown prince He, ordered Prince Ba of Lu to die, and Lu Xun died of grief and rage.

timeline.title: 权崩
timeline.summary: 立少子孙亮为太子，寻崩，年七十一；亮即位，诸葛恪辅政。
timeline.summary_en: He named his youngest son, Sun Liang, heir and died, aged seventy-one; Liang took the throne with Zhuge Ke as regent.

timeline.title: 吴主总评
timeline.summary: 陈寿评其任才尚计、有勾践之奇英，而性多嫌忌、果于杀戮，立嗣再误，吴之亡萌于斯。
timeline.summary_en: Chen Shou praised his use of talent and his stratagems — the rare heroism of a Goujian — while noting his jealousy and readiness to kill; the succession erred twice, and Wu's ruin sprouted here.

emperors.bio_md:
# 吴大帝 · 主要事迹

孙权字仲谋，孙坚次子，母吴氏。建安五年孙策遇刺卒，权年十九，继统江东，张昭、周瑜辅之——「举贤任能，各尽其心」，江东基业自此而固。建安十三年，曹操南下，权纳周瑜、鲁肃之议，联刘备于赤壁火攻破曹，三分之势遂定。建安二十四年，吕蒙白衣渡江袭荆州，关羽败亡，吴据有荆襄。黄武元年，陆逊于夷陵火攻大破刘备，吴转守为攻，疆域遂定。

黄龙元年，权于武昌即皇帝位，国号吴，旋还都建业——历曹操、曹丕、刘备三强并世，而权「任才尚计，有勾践之奇英」，始终为鼎足之一。称帝后数十年间，通使辽东公孙渊、攻合肥新城皆无果，而治国以宽，江东之民乐业，四十年无大战。

权之晚节，坏于立嗣：赤乌四年太子孙登卒，其后二宫之争起，群臣各附鲁王霸、太子和，权废和赐霸死，陆逊亦忧愤而卒——「阋墙之祸」自此始，吴之衰象已萌。太元二年，权立少子孙亮为太子，寻崩，年七十一，谥大皇帝。

陈寿评曰：「孙权屈身忍辱，任才尚计，有勾践之奇英，人之杰也。故能自擅江表，成鼎峙之业。然性多嫌忌，果于杀戮，暨臻末年，弥以滋甚。」「生子当如孙仲谋」之誉传于后世；然二宫之误，实为吴亡之远因，可叹权一世英雄，不悟齐家之道。

> 本地参考：点校本《三国志》卷047《吴主传》、卷054《周瑜传》、卷058《陆逊传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sun Quan, styled Zhongmou, was Sun Jian's second son by Lady Wu. In the 5th year of Jian'an, Sun Ce died by an assassin's knife, and Quan, at nineteen, took command of Jiangdong with Zhang Zhao and Zhou Yu at his side — "raising the worthy and employing the able, each giving his utmost," and the Jiangdong foundations were secured. In the 13th year of Jian'an, as Cao Cao came south, Quan took the counsel of Zhou Yu and Lu Su, allied with Liu Bei, and broke the Cao army by fire at the Red Cliffs — the tripartite balance was fixed. In the 24th year Lü Meng's covert crossing seized Jingzhou, Guan Yu fell, and Wu held the Jing province. In the 1st year of Huangwu Lu Xun's fire attack at Yiling shattered Liu Bei, and Wu turned from defense to offense, its borders set.

In the 1st year of Huanglong Quan took the imperial throne at Wuchang, styling the realm Wu, and at once returned the capital to Jianye. Through the great ages of Cao Cao, Cao Pi, and Liu Bei, "employing talent and valuing stratagems, with the rare heroism of a Goujian," he held one leg of the tripod. In the decades of his empire he sent envoys to Gongsun Yuan in Liaodong and besieged the new city of Hefei, both fruitless, while governing Jiangdong gently — the people prospered, and for forty years there was no great war.

His late years were wrecked by the succession: in the 4th year of Chiwu the crown prince Deng died, and the two-palace feud followed; the court split between Prince Ba of Lu and the crown prince He, Quan deposed He, ordered Ba to die, and Lu Xun himself died of grief and rage — the "strife within the walls" began, and Wu's decline was already visible. In the 2nd year of Taiyuan he named his youngest son, Sun Liang, heir, and died, aged seventy-one, posthumously styled Da.

Chen Shou's verdict: "Sun Quan, bending himself and swallowing humiliation, employing talent and valuing stratagems, had the rare heroism of a Goujian — a man of eminence. So he could hold the south of the river and complete the tripod's reign. But his nature was jealous and suspicious, quick to kill, and in his last years it grew worse." "A son should be born like Sun Zhongmou" passed into the people's praise; yet the succession's double error was the distant cause of Wu's fall — a pity that a lifetime's hero could not keep his own house.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Sanguozhi*, ch. 47 ("Biography of the Wu Sovereign"), ch. 54 (biography of Zhou Yu), ch. 58 (biography of Lu Xun) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 会稽王 · 主要事迹

孙亮字子明，孙权少子，母潘皇后，孙权晚年最钟爱。太元二年，孙权以七十一岁高龄立亮为太子，寻崩，亮即位，年九岁，改元建兴，诸葛恪辅政。建兴二年，诸葛恪兴师二十万围合肥新城，士卒疫病大败而归；孙峻设宴伏兵杀恪，自为大将军，专权日甚。五凤二年，孙峻又杀张悌等大臣，威福自恣。

太平元年孙峻病卒，其从弟孙綝继秉国政，骄横尤甚。亮虽年幼而聪慧，尝亲政事，见綝「专权自恣」，遂与全公主、刘承等谋诛綝。太平三年，亮密诏刘承等围綝第，谋泄，綝先发制人，废亮为会稽王，迎立琅琊王孙休。亮被废后居会稽，永安三年，孙休使人逼之，亮自杀，年十八。

亮之为人，史称「童幼而聪慧」，观其亲断政事、能识孙綝之奸，非昏主可比；然以九岁冲主当权臣迭兴之局，身不由己，终以废死终。吴自孙权崩后，十年之间三易其君（亮、休、皓），皆系权臣迎立之柄——孙亮之废，实开吴中后期「君权旁落、废立由人」之先例。

> 本地参考：点校本《三国志》卷048《三嗣主传》、卷064《诸葛恪传》《孙綝传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sun Liang, styled Ziming, was Sun Quan's youngest son by Empress Pan, the favorite of Quan's old age. In the 2nd year of Taiyuan, at seventy-one, Quan named Liang heir and died; Liang took the throne at nine, changing the era to Jianxing, with Zhuge Ke as regent. In the 2nd year of Jianxing Ke raised 200,000 men to besiege the new city of Hefei; plague struck and the host came back ruined, and Sun Jun, ambushing him at a banquet, slew Ke and made himself grand general, his power growing daily. In the 2nd year of Wufeng Jun put Zhang Ti and other ministers to death, acting as he pleased.

In the 1st year of Taiping Jun died of illness, and his cousin Sun Chen took the government, more overbearing still. Liang, young but sharp, had begun to attend to government himself; seeing Chen's "monopoly and arrogance," he plotted with Princess Quan and Liu Cheng to slay him. In the 3rd year of Taiping, Liang's secret order to surround Chen's mansion leaked; Chen struck first, deposed Liang as Prince of Kuajji, and brought in the Prince of Langya, Sun Xiu. In exile at Kuajji, pressed by Xiu's men in the 3rd year of Yong'an, Liang took his own life at eighteen.

The histories call Liang "sharp-witted though a child"; his own judgments of court affairs and his recognition of Sun Chen's villainy show no dullard. But a nine-year-old sovereign amid a succession of strong ministers was at the mercy of the age, and he ended deposed and dead. After Sun Quan's death Wu changed sovereigns three times in ten years — Liang, Xiu, Hao — each change by the strong ministers' will: the deposition of Sun Liang opened the era in which Wu's throne passed by coup.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Sanguozhi*, ch. 48 ("Biographies of the Three Successors"), ch. 64 (biographies of Zhuge Ke and Sun Chen) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.summary_en: Installed after Sun Liang's deposition, he and Zhang Bu and Ding Feng laid the plot that slew Sun Chen; governing himself, he founded schools and chairs of learning, and died in the 6th year of Yong'an, aged thirty.

emperors.bio_md:
# 吴景帝 · 主要事迹

孙休字子烈，孙权第六子，封琅琊王，居虎林。太平三年，孙綝废孙亮，迎立休，改元永安。休知綝之奸，即位后厚礼以安其心，暗中与老臣张布、丁奉密谋：永安元年十二月，借腊祭朝会之机，殿前设伏，一举诛孙綝，夷三族——吴之权柄，自诸葛恪、孙峻、孙綝三执政以来，复归君主。

休亲政后励精图治：诏立五经博士，置学官，大兴教育；减赋税、赈灾民、察吏治，颇有可观。然其为人「好刑名」，用刑过当：张布以功自负，休疑之，寻杀布——诛权臣之智与诛功臣之刻，集于一身。陈寿评其「虽有过失，而能补过」，不失为吴之中兴之主。

永安六年，蜀汉亡，魏军陈兵边境，吴人心浮动；休病笃，太子年幼，乃托孤于丞相濮阳兴。七月崩，年三十，谥景皇帝。休崩后，濮阳兴等以太子幼弱，违先帝遗命，迎立乌程侯孙皓——以「主幼国危」为由易君，实开吴末迎立之祸；吴之亡，自此启端。孙休在位六年，诛綝、立学、亲政，皆中主之善，惜其寿不永，吴不得其福。

> 本地参考：点校本《三国志》卷048《三嗣主传》、卷064《孙綝传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sun Xiu, styled Zilie, was Sun Quan's sixth son, enfeoffed Prince of Langya, dwelling at Hulin. In the 3rd year of Taiping, Sun Chen deposed Sun Liang and brought in Xiu, changing the era to Yong'an. Xiu knew Chen's treachery: on accession he honored Chen with gifts to put him at ease, while secretly plotting with the old ministers Zhang Bu and Ding Feng. In the twelfth month of the 1st year of Yong'an, at the winter festival court, the trap closed and Sun Chen was slain before the hall, his kin exterminated — for the first time since Zhuge Ke, Sun Jun, and Sun Chen, Wu's government returned to the sovereign.

In person rule Xiu governed diligently: he decreed chairs of the Five Classics, established academies, and fostered learning; he lightened taxes, relieved the stricken, and examined the officials — much that was admirable. But he "delighted in law and punishment," and used them too far: Zhang Bu, presuming on his merit, fell under suspicion and was slain — the cunning that slew a usurper and the harshness that slew a supporter met in one man. Chen Shou judged him "not without fault, yet able to repair his faults": in the middle of Wu's decline, a restorer in the making.

In the 6th year of Yong'an, with Shu fallen and the Wei armies massed on the border, Xiu fell ill; the crown prince was a child, and he entrusted the heir to the chancellor Puru Yangxing. He died that July at thirty, posthumously styled Jing. After his death Yangxing and the others, deeming the child heir too weak for the hour, set aside the late sovereign's will and brought in Sun Hao, marquis of Wucheng — the precedent of enthronement by coup that undid Wu. Six years of slaying Sun Chen, founding schools, and ruling in person were the good deeds of a competent sovereign; his early death was Wu's misfortune.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Sanguozhi*, ch. 48 ("Biographies of the Three Successors"), ch. 64 (biography of Sun Chen) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.summary: 孙休崩后迎立，初有善政，旋以暴虐著称：杀张尚、任何定、改元无度；天纪四年晋六路伐吴，面缚出降，吴亡，封归命侯。
emperors.summary_en: Installed after Sun Xiu's death, he governed well at first, then grew notorious for cruelty: slaying Zhang Shang, favoring He Ding, changing eras without count; in the 4th year of Tianji, with Jin invading on six roads, he surrendered bound and bare, ending Wu, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Guiming.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载「皓之为人，心性凶悖」。画像宜表现骄盈暴戾的末代君主之态，衣冠从孙吴末制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary: 孙权孙，太子和之子，封乌程侯。
timeline.summary_en: Grandson of Sun Quan, son of the crown prince He, enfeoffed Marquis of Wucheng.

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 孙休崩，群臣迎立乌程侯皓，改元元兴；初有令誉，旋露凶暴。
timeline.summary_en: On Sun Xiu's death the court brought in the Marquis of Wucheng; after a good start his savagery showed itself.

timeline.title: 诛濮阳兴张布
timeline.title_en: Puru Yangxing and Zhang Bu Slain
timeline.summary: 迎立功臣濮阳兴、张布以谏被诛，凶虐之端自此。
timeline.summary_en: The ministers who brought him in, Puru Yangxing and Zhang Bu, were slain for remonstrance — the first marks of his tyranny.

timeline.title: 迁都武昌旋还
timeline.title_en: The Capital Moved to Wuchang and Back
timeline.summary: 迁都武昌，民怨「宁饮建业水，不食武昌鱼」，寻还建业。
timeline.summary_en: He moved the capital to Wuchang; the people grumbled "rather drink Jianye's water than eat Wuchang's fish," and he soon returned.

timeline.title: 陆抗守西陵
timeline.summary: 步阐降晋，陆抗率军收复西陵，晋援不克。
timeline.summary_en: Bu Chan defected to Jin; Lu Kang retook Xiling, and the Jin relief failed.

timeline.title: 何定弄权
timeline.summary: 佞臣何定用事，典兵擅权，众皆侧目。
timeline.summary_en: The flatterer He Ding came to power, commanded troops, and overreached, drawing every eye against him.

timeline.title: 杀张尚等
timeline.summary: 侍中张尚以言语忤旨被诛，谏诤之路遂绝。
timeline.summary_en: The attendant Zhang Shang was put to death for words that offended, and the road of remonstrance closed.

timeline.title: 改元频繁
timeline.summary: 数年间频改元以应符瑞，朝纲愈乱。
timeline.summary_en: Year after year he changed the era to match portents, and the government fell further into disorder.

timeline.title: 晋六路伐吴
timeline.summary: 晋武帝命王濬、杜预等六路伐吴，建业震动。
timeline.summary_en: Emperor Wu of Jin sent Wang Jun, Du Yu, and others against Wu on six roads, shaking Jianye itself.

timeline.title: 孙皓降
timeline.summary: 皓面缚舆榇，出降于王濬军前，吴亡，封归命侯。
timeline.summary_en: Bound bare with the coffin at his cart, Hao surrendered before Wang Jun's army; Wu perished, and he was made Marquis of Guiming.

timeline.title: 薨于洛阳
timeline.summary: 举家迁洛阳，年四十二卒于洛阳。
timeline.summary_en: Brought with his house to Luoyang, he died there at forty-two.

timeline.title: 粗暴骄盈
timeline.summary: 史评称皓凶顽骄暴，虐杀朝臣，亲昵小人，吴之亡实由其自取。
timeline.summary_en: The histories call Hao brutal and arrogant, slaying his courtiers, clinging to petty men — Wu's ruin self-inflicted.

emperors.bio_md:
# 吴末帝 · 主要事迹

孙皓字元宗，孙权孙，废太子孙和之子，封乌程侯。永安六年孙休崩，丞相濮阳兴、左将军张布以太子年幼，迎立皓，改元元兴。皓初立，发优诏、恤士民、开仓廪，虚誉满朝野；然未及数月，凶暴之性毕露——元兴元年，即诛迎立功臣濮阳兴、张布，自此「滥杀之端」大开。

皓之暴政，史不绝书：性嗜酒，强臣下灌醉以伺其过；好杀人，剥面凿眼，酷刑备至；宠佞臣何定，杀侍中张尚，谏诤之路遂绝。甘露元年迁都武昌，民怨沸腾，谣曰「宁饮建业水，不食武昌鱼；宁还建业死，不止武昌居」，寻还建业。数年间频改元以应符瑞，天册、天玺之号纷至，朝纲日乱。

天纪四年，晋武帝六路伐吴，王濬楼船下益州，杜预、王浑等并进；陆抗已前卒，吴无良将。三月，王濬兵临建业，皓面缚舆榇，出降于军门——吴自孙权称帝至此凡五十二年而亡，三分归晋，天下复统。

皓举家迁洛阳，晋封归命侯，太康四年薨，年四十二。史家评曰：皓「凶顽骄暴，虐杀无度」，吴之亡非亡于晋之强，而亡于皓之暴——「既失民心，又失天命」，亡国之君，无有甚于皓者。然观其初立之善政，可见其非无才者，暴虐之性一朝得志，遂不可制，可为专制之戒。

> 本地参考：点校本《三国志》卷048《三嗣主传》、卷058《陆抗传》及晋书卷003《武帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sun Hao, styled Yuanzong, was a grandson of Sun Quan, son of the deposed crown prince He, enfeoffed Marquis of Wucheng. In the 6th year of Yong'an, after Sun Xiu's death, the chancellor Puru Yangxing and General Zhang Bu, deeming the child heir too weak, installed Hao, changing the era to Yuanxing. At first he issued kind decrees, relieved the people, and opened the granaries, winning a fine reputation throughout the court; within months his savagery showed itself — in the 1st year of Yuanxing he slew Puru Yangxing and Zhang Bu, the very men who had enthroned him, and the age of reckless killing opened.

His tyranny fills the histories: a lover of wine who forced his ministers drunk to catch their slips; a killer who used flaying and eye-gouging among his torments; he favored the flatterer He Ding, slew the attendant Zhang Shang, and closed the road of remonstrance. In the 1st year of Ganlu he moved the capital to Wuchang until the people's cry — "rather drink Jianye's water than eat Wuchang's fish; rather die back in Jianye than dwell in Wuchang" — forced his return. Era followed era to match portents — Tiance, Tianxi — and the government fell into chaos.

In the 4th year of Tianji Emperor Wu of Jin invaded on six roads: Wang Jun's fleet came down from Yizhou, Du Yu and Wang Hun pressed from every side; Lu Kang was dead, and Wu had no great general left. In the third month Wang Jun reached Jianye, and Hao, bound bare with the coffin in his cart, surrendered at the army gate — Wu, fifty-two years from Sun Quan's imperial title, was no more, and the realm was reunified under Jin.

Brought with his house to Luoyang, he was made Marquis of Guiming by Jin, and died there in the 4th year of Taikang at forty-two. The historians' verdict: "brutal, stubborn, arrogant, cruel beyond measure" — Wu fell not to the strength of Jin but to his own tyranny: "he had lost the people's hearts and Heaven's mandate alike." No fallen sovereign surpasses him in infamy. Yet his opening reforms show a man of some ability; the tyrant in him, once loosed, could not be checked — a lesson for unchecked power.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Sanguozhi*, ch. 48 ("Biographies of the Three Successors"), ch. 58 (biography of Lu Kang), and the *Jinshu*, ch. 3 ("Benji of Emperor Wu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary: 司马昭长子，母王氏。
timeline.summary_en: Eldest son of Sima Zhao by Lady Wang.

timeline.title: 受禅即位
timeline.summary: 魏元帝禅位，炎即皇帝位，改元泰始，国号晋，都洛阳。
timeline.summary_en: Emperor Yuan of Wei abdicated; Yan took the throne, changed the era to Taishi, styled the realm Jin, and made Luoyang his capital.

timeline.title: 郊祀建制
timeline.summary: 定郊庙之礼，建晋朝礼制框架。
timeline.summary_en: He fixed the suburban and ancestral rites, framing the ceremonial order of Jin.

timeline.title: 班五条诏书
timeline.summary: 颁守令五条，整饬吏治。
timeline.summary_en: He issued the five articles for local officials, tightening governance.

timeline.title: 选公卿女充后宫
timeline.summary: 大采公卿之女充后宫，禁天下嫁娶，史称荒淫之渐。
timeline.summary_en: He swept the daughters of the great houses into his harem and forbade all marriages in the realm — the beginnings, the histories say, of his debauchery.

timeline.title: 马隆平凉州
timeline.summary: 马隆率众击斩秃发树机能，凉州平。
timeline.summary_en: Ma Long struck down Tufa Shujineng and pacified Liangzhou.

timeline.title: 平吴统一
timeline.summary: 命贾充为大都督，王濬、王浑等六路下吴，孙皓降，天下一统。
timeline.summary_en: With Jia Chong grand commander, Wang Jun, Wang Hun, and others came down on Wu from six roads; Sun Hao surrendered and the realm was one.

timeline.title: 罢州郡兵
timeline.summary: 大郡置武吏百人，州郡武备削弱，史家谓八王之乱之背景。
timeline.summary_en: The great commanderies kept but a hundred armed clerks; the provincial defenses were cut away — the historians see here the background of the War of the Eight Princes.

timeline.title: 诏州郡中正
timeline.summary: 诏州郡各置中正，门阀选举体系延续。
timeline.summary_en: He ordered rectifiers appointed in every province and commandery, carrying on the aristocratic system of selection.

timeline.title: 封宗室强藩
timeline.summary: 大封同姓诸王，出御四方，藩镇渐强。
timeline.summary_en: He enfeoffed the imperial princes on a grand scale and sent them out to govern the four quarters, and the feudatories grew strong.

timeline.title: 武帝崩
timeline.summary: 崩，惠帝衷即位，杨骏辅政。
timeline.summary_en: He died; Emperor Hui (Sima Zhong) succeeded with Yang Jun as regent.

timeline.title: 武皇总评
timeline.summary: 晋书史臣评其宇量弘厚、明达善谋；平吴之后耽于游宴，宠爱后党，请谒公行，治道浸衰。
timeline.summary_en: The Jin historians credit his broad bearing and shrewd counsel, yet after the Wu conquest he gave himself to feasting and hunting, favored his wives' kin, and let petitions flow by favor — the way of government decayed.

emperors.bio_md:
# 晋武帝 · 主要事迹

司马炎字安世，司马昭长子。咸熙二年十二月，受魏元帝禅让即皇帝位，改元泰始，国号晋，都洛阳——汉末以来六十年的分裂，在他手上走向终结。即位之初颇思有为：定郊庙之礼以正名分，颁五条诏书以整吏治，泰始九年广采公卿之女充后宫，开其后奢靡之端。咸宁五年马隆击斩树机能，凉州平。

太康元年，命贾充为大都督，王濬、王浑等六路伐吴；王濬楼船下益州，孙皓面缚出降，三国归晋，天下一统。平吴之后，武帝志满意骄：罢州郡兵，大郡仅置武吏百人；大封同姓诸王出御四方，宗室渐强；后宫妃嫔近万，乘羊车随其所至而寝，史称「羊车望幸」。九品中正之制沿续，门阀世族坐大。

太熙元年四月，武帝崩，年五十五。惠帝以愚钝继位，八王之乱随之而起。史臣评武帝「宇量弘厚，明达善谋」，平吴之业足称雄主；然罢州郡兵、封宗室、宠后党三失，使「雍凉之兵不复天下」，「宗室之藩」反成祸源——太康之治二十余年，而祸根已伏于其间。西晋之亡，武帝实难辞其咎。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷003《武帝纪》、卷042《王濬传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Yan, styled Anshi, was the eldest son of Sima Zhao. In the twelfth month of the 2nd year of Xianxi he received the abdication of Wei and took the throne, changing the era to Taishi, styling the realm Jin, and making Luoyang his capital — the sixty-year division since the end of Han was on its way to an end. He began with purpose: he fixed the suburban and ancestral rites, issued the five articles to discipline local government, and in the 9th year of Taishi swept the daughters of the great houses into his harem — the beginnings of his luxury. In the 5th year of Xianning Ma Long struck down Tufa Shujineng, and Liangzhou was pacified.

In the 1st year of Taikang, with Jia Chong grand commander, Wang Jun, Wang Hun, and others came down on Wu from six roads; Wang Jun's fleet descended from Yizhou, Sun Hao surrendered bound and bare, and the Three Kingdoms were one under Jin. After the conquest he grew complacent: he disbanded the provincial armies, keeping a hundred armed clerks in the great commanderies; he enfeoffed the imperial princes on a grand scale to govern the four quarters, and the feudatories grew strong; his harem held nearly ten thousand ladies, and he rode a sheep-cart to let it choose where he slept — "the sheep-cart's favor." The nine-rank system continued, and the great clans waxed.

In the fourth month of the 1st year of Taixi the emperor died at fifty-five, and his dull-witted heir brought on the War of the Eight Princes. The historians credit him as "broad of bearing and shrewd in counsel," a sovereign worthy of the unification; but the three errors — disbanding the armies, enfeoffing the princes, favoring his wives' kin — sowed the ruin while the Taikang recovery flourished. Western Jin's fall, the historians agree, was prepared in his own reign.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 3 ("Benji of Emperor Wu"), ch. 42 (biography of Wang Jun) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.summary: 武帝子，性愚钝，在位十六年而八王之乱起，天下大乱；「何不食肉糜」为史所讥，光熙元年还洛后崩，或云被毒杀。
emperors.summary_en: Son of Emperor Wu, dull-witted, he sat sixteen years while the War of the Eight Princes tore the realm apart; his "why not eat minced meat?" became a byword for his folly, and in the 1st year of Guangxi he died after returning to Luoyang — by poison, some say.

timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary: 武帝子，母杨皇后；史称其愚钝，闻蛙鸣而问为官为私。
timeline.summary_en: Son of Emperor Wu by Empress Yang; the histories call him dull — hearing frogs croak, he asked whether they croaked for office or for private gain.

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 武帝崩，衷即位，杨骏辅政，贾后干政渐起。
timeline.summary_en: On Emperor Wu's death Zhong took the throne with Yang Jun as regent; Empress Jia's meddling in government began.

timeline.title: 诛杨骏
timeline.summary: 贾后杀杨骏，汝南王亮、卫瓘辅政旋亦死，贾氏专政。
timeline.summary_en: Empress Jia slew Yang Jun; the Princes of Runan, Sima Liang, and Wei Guan, who then governed, died in turn, and the Jia clan ruled.

timeline.title: 八王之乱开端
timeline.title_en: The War of the Eight Princes Begins
timeline.summary: 诸王同姓相屠自此始，延十余年，为永嘉之祸张本。
timeline.summary_en: The princes' mutual slaughter began here, running over ten years and preparing the disaster of Yongjia.

timeline.title: 杀太子遹
timeline.summary: 贾后诬太子司马遹谋反杀之，赵王伦等起兵讨贾。
timeline.summary_en: Empress Jia charged the heir Sima Yu with revolt and slew him; the Prince of Zhao, Sima Lun, and others rose against her.

timeline.title: 赵王伦篡
timeline.summary: 赵王伦废帝自立，改元建始；齐王冏等三王讨伦。
timeline.summary_en: The Prince of Zhao deposed the emperor and took the throne himself, changing the era to Jianshi; the Prince of Qi and two others marched against Lun.

timeline.title: 帝反正
timeline.summary: 齐王冏等诛伦，迎帝还宫复辟。
timeline.summary_en: The Prince of Qi and the others slew Lun and brought the emperor back to the palace.

timeline.title: 长沙王乂杀冏
timeline.summary: 长沙王乂杀齐王冏，诸王相攻不止。
timeline.summary_en: The Prince of Changsha, Sima Ai, slew the Prince of Qi, and the princes' wars went on.

timeline.title: 帝迁长安
timeline.summary: 张方劫帝入长安，河间、成都诸王交兵。
timeline.summary_en: Zhang Fang seized the emperor and carried him to Chang'an while the Princes of Hejian and Chengdu fought.

timeline.title: 李雄刘渊起
timeline.title_en: Li Xiong and Liu Yuan Rise
timeline.summary: 李雄据蜀称帝，刘渊据离石称汉王，五胡乱华前奏。
timeline.summary_en: Li Xiong took Shu, and Liu Yuan styled himself king of Han — the prelude to the Five Barbarian invasions.

timeline.title: 还洛崩
timeline.summary: 东海王越迎帝还洛阳，帝寻崩，或云为越毒杀。
timeline.summary_en: The Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue, brought the emperor back to Luoyang, where he died — poisoned by Yue, some say.

timeline.title: 肉糜
timeline.summary: 天下荒乱百姓饿死，帝曰「何不食肉糜」，史以为愚暗之证。
timeline.summary_en: In the great famine, told that the people were starving to death, he asked, "Why do they not eat minced meat?" — the historians' proof of his darkness.

emperors.bio_md:
# 晋惠帝 · 主要事迹

司马衷字正度，武帝第二子。其愚为天下所知：在华林园闻蛤蟆鸣，问左右「此鸣者为官乎，私乎」；天下荒乱，百姓饿死，曰「何不食肉糜」。武帝晚年虑其不慧，然经杨后、贾充之党劝进，终立为太子——为西晋埋下亡国之机。

太熙元年武帝崩，衷即位，年三十二。贾后专权，永平元年杀杨骏，又杀汝南王亮、卫瓘，专擅朝政；元康九年诬杀太子司马遹，赵王伦起兵讨贾，八王之乱自此爆发。其后十年，诸王迭相废立：赵王伦篡位、齐王冏反正、长沙王乂杀冏、河间王颙与成都王颖相攻，张方劫帝迁长安，东海王越迎帝还洛阳。光熙元年，帝崩，或云为越毒杀。

惠帝在位十六年，身在乱中而不自知，屡为诸王挟持播迁，「天下之势」尽坏于此：八王之乱耗尽晋之元气，李雄据蜀、刘渊称汉相继而起，五胡乱华之局已成。史家论惠帝之愚，不在其人之罪；然以如此之主承太康之业，武帝托付非人，西晋之祸实自兹始。「何不食肉糜」一语，遂成千古笑柄，亦千古殷鉴。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷004《惠帝纪》、卷031《后妃传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

太熙元年武帝崩，衷即位，年三十二。贾后专权，永平元年杀杨骏，又杀汝南王亮、卫瓘，专擅朝政；元康九年诬杀太子司马遹，赵王伦起兵讨贾，八王之乱自此爆发。其后十年，诸王迭相废立：赵王伦篡位、齐王冏反正、长沙王乂杀冏、河间王颙与成都王颖相攻，张方劫帝迁长安，东海王越迎帝还洛阳。光熙元年，帝崩，或云为越毒杀。

惠帝在位十六年，身在乱中而不自知，屡为诸王挟持播迁，「天下之势」尽坏于此：八王之乱耗尽晋之元气，李雄据蜀、刘渊称汉相继而起，五胡乱华之局已成。史家论惠帝之愚，不在其人之罪；然以如此之主承太康之业，武帝托付非人，西晋之祸实自兹始。「何不食肉糜」一语，遂成千古笑柄，亦千古殷鉴。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷004《惠帝纪》、卷031《后妃传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Zhong, styled Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu, and his dullness was known to all: in the Huayuan park, hearing frogs croak, he asked whether they croaked "for office or for private gain"; in the great famine, told the people were starving, he asked, "Why do they not eat minced meat?" Emperor Wu himself doubted him, but Empress Yang and Jia Chong's party pressed for his appointment as heir — planting the ruin of Western Jin.

In the 1st year of Taixi Wu died and Zhong took the throne at thirty-two. Empress Jia ruled: in the 1st year of Yuankang she slew Yang Jun, then the Prince of Runan and Wei Guan, governing at will; in the 9th year of Yuankang she had the heir Sima Yu falsely charged and slain, and the Prince of Zhao rose against her — the War of the Eight Princes broke out. For ten years the princes deposed and restored him: Lun usurped, the Prince of Qi restored, the Prince of Changsha slew the Prince of Qi, the Princes of Hejian and Chengdu fought, Zhang Fang carried the emperor to Chang'an, and the Prince of Donghai brought him back to Luoyang, where he died in the 1st year of Guangxi — poisoned by Yue, some say.

Sixteen years on the throne, he never knew he was in a storm, carried about by this prince and that. The war exhausted Jin's strength; Li Xiong took Shu and Liu Yuan styled himself king of Han — the Five Barbarian invasions had begun. The historians do not blame Zhong himself; they blame Wu's choice of heir. "Why not eat minced meat?" passed into the language as the eternal byword of a fool, and of a dynasty that entrusted its realm to one.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 4 ("Benji of Emperor Hui"), ch. 31 (biographies of the empresses) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 晋怀帝 · 主要事迹

司马炽字丰度，武帝第二十五子。好学博综，永嘉之乱前以「冲素好文」著称，封豫章王。光熙元年惠帝崩，东海王越迎立炽即位，改元永嘉。帝即位后颇欲振作，然八王之乱方息，匈奴之祸已兴：东海王越专权辅政，帝拱手而已；越领兵出镇，忧惧交加，病卒于项。

永嘉四年，刘渊卒，刘聪继立，遣刘曜、石勒等寇逼洛阳；洛阳饥困，城中人相食。永嘉五年六月，刘曜、王弥等破洛阳，纵兵焚掠，百官士民死者三万余人，帝蒙尘被俘，先送至平阳，刘聪以「青衣行酒」辱之，建兴前遇害，年三十。西晋之首都洛阳，自此丘墟。

怀帝在位六年，非无志之主，然承八王之乱之弊，当胡骑叩关之势，中兴之业，无可措手。永嘉之乱与「衣冠南渡」并称，为西晋灭亡之标志：洛阳倾覆之后，中原板荡，晋室南迁，中国历史自此转入东晋南朝与五胡十六国并立之局。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷005《怀帝纪》、卷102《刘聪载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Chi, styled Fengdu, was the twenty-fifth son of Emperor Wu, a student of wide learning known for his quiet love of letters, enfeoffed Prince of Yuzhang. In the 1st year of Guangxi, on Emperor Hui's death, the Prince of Donghai brought him to the throne; the era was changed to Yongjia. He wished to act, but the War of the Eight Princes had barely ended and the Xiongnu storm was rising: the Prince of Donghai governed alone and the emperor folded his hands; Yue, marching out with the armies, died of worry at Xiang.

In the 4th year of Yongjia Liu Yuan died and Liu Cong succeeded, sending Liu Yao and Shi Le against Luoyang; the city starved until men ate men. In the sixth month of the 5th year, Liu Yao and Wang Mi broke in, burned and looted, and slew over thirty thousand officials and people; the emperor was carried off to Pingyang, where Liu Cong made him serve wine in servant's dress before putting him to death, aged thirty. The capital of Western Jin lay in ruins.

Six years on the throne, Chi was no man without spirit, but he inherited the wreck of the princes' war with the barbarian cavalry at the gate; there was no room for recovery. The Yongjia disaster and the "crossing of the caps and gowns south" mark the fall of Western Jin: with Luoyang in ashes and the Central Plains lost, the Jin house fled south, and the age of the Eastern Jin and the Five Barbarian Sixteen States began.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 5 ("Benji of Emperor Huai"), ch. 102 (records of Liu Cong) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 晋愍帝 · 主要事迹

司马邺字彦旗，吴孝王晏之子，出继秦王司马柬。怀帝遇害，凶问传至长安，时邺年十四，即皇帝位于长安，改元建兴。然关中残破，饥疫相仍：刘曜连年攻围，城中粮尽，米斗金二两，人相食，死者大半。

建兴四年十一月，刘曜陷长安，帝乘羊车、肉袒衔璧、舆榇出降——西晋传四帝五十二年而亡。帝被送至平阳，刘聪以「行酒洗爵」之辱加之，建武元年遇害，年十八。同年三月，琅邪王司马睿在建康称晋王，翌年即帝位，东晋始立。

愍帝在位三年，非有失德，实无可为：关中之地，方数十里；兵马之数，不过数千。史家论西晋之亡，「非亡于愍帝之世，而亡于武帝之置宗室、惠帝之生乱」——愍帝不过承其祸而已。以冲龄之君，当板荡之运，其遭遇之惨，与怀帝相类，故史书并称「怀愍」，为两晋南渡之痛史开篇。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷005《愍帝纪》、卷103《刘曜载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Ye, styled Yanqi, was the son of Sima Yan, Prince Xiao of Wu, adopted into the line of Sima Jian, Prince of Qin. When word of Emperor Huai's murder reached Chang'an he took the throne there at fourteen, changing the era to Jianxing. But Guanzhong lay waste, famine and plague alternating: Liu Yao besieged the city year after year, the grain ran out, a bushel of rice cost two jin of gold, and men ate men; the people died by the half.

In the eleventh month of the 4th year of Jianxing Liu Yao took the city, and the emperor, bare-armed with the seal in his mouth and the coffin in his cart, surrendered — Western Jin, through four sovereigns and fifty-two years, was no more. Brought to Pingyang, he was made to serve wine and wash the cups for Liu Cong, and in the 1st year of Jianwu was put to death at eighteen. That same year Sima Rui styled himself King of Jin at Jiankang and took the throne the next year: Eastern Jin began.

Three years on the throne, Min committed no fault; he simply had nothing to work with — a few dozen li of territory, a few thousand men. The historians write that Western Jin fell not in Min's reign but in Wu's enfeoffment of the princes and Hui's accession; Min only inherited the disaster. A child sovereign in a realm in ruins, his fate matched Huai's, and the two are joined in history as "the Huai–Min tragedy," the opening wound of the southern Jin.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 5 ("Benji of Emperor Min"), ch. 103 (records of Liu Yao) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 晋元帝 · 主要事迹

司马睿字景文，琅邪恭王觐之子，武帝从子。八王之乱中，受东海王越之命镇守下邳，永嘉元年用王导计，南渡镇建邺，都督扬州诸军事。睿至江南，吴人未附，王导、王敦兄弟倾心推奉，三吴士族遂归心——「王与马，共天下」之局，自此而始。

建武元年，愍帝凶问未确，睿称晋王；太兴元年愍帝遇害之讯至，即皇帝位，都建康。即位后广辟掾属，多江南人望；命祖逖北伐，中流击楫，收复黄河以南。然元帝「恭俭之德有余，雄武之量不足」：以王敦坐镇荆州、都督诸州军事，兵权在外；又亲刘隗、刁协以制王氏，遂激王敦之变。永昌元年，王敦举兵武昌，攻入建康，杀刁协等，帝忧愤成疾，闰月崩，年四十七。

元帝以晋室疏属南渡称帝，保全衣冠、再造晋祚，其功在社稷；然南渡士族与侨姓共治之局，使皇权旁落、门阀坐大，东晋一朝「政在王氏」之祸，亦自此启。司马氏之天下，实与琅琊王氏共之——「王与马共天下」，遂成两晋南北朝门阀政治之标志。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Rui, styled Jingwen, was the son of Sima Jin, Prince Gong of Langya, and a nephew of Emperor Wu. In the War of the Eight Princes he was sent to garrison Xiapi, and in the 1st year of Yongjia, on Wang Dao's counsel, crossed south to govern Jianye with command of Yangzhou's armies. The southern houses would not at first submit; but Wang Dao and his brother Dun pushed him forward with all their hearts, and the notables of the three Wu commanderies came over — the arrangement of "Wang and Sima sharing the realm" began here.

In the 1st year of Jianwu, with Emperor Min's fate unconfirmed, Rui styled himself King of Jin; in the 1st year of Taixing, on word of Min's death, he took the throne with his capital at Jiankang. He gathered officers widely, most of them the leading men of the south, and sent Zu Ti north — striking the oars midstream, Zu recovered the lands south of the Yellow River. But Yuan's "frugality and reverence were more than sufficient, his heroic measure wanting": he let Wang Dun command Jingzhou and the surrounding provinces with the armies outside the capital, then raised Liu Kui and Diao Xie against the Wangs — and provoked Dun's revolt. In the 1st year of Yongchang Dun rose from Wuchang, forced his way into Jiankang, slew Diao Xie and others, and the emperor, falling ill of grief and rage, died in the intercalary month, aged forty-seven.

A distant kinsman of the imperial house, Yuan crossed south and saved the caps and gowns, re-founding the Jin line — a service to the altars. But the co-rule of the crossed clans and the local houses pushed the throne aside and the great clans up; the age of aristocratic politics, and of "Wang and Sima sharing the realm," had begun.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 6 ("Benji of Emperor Yuan"), ch. 65 (biography of Wang Dao) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 晋明帝 · 主要事迹

司马绍字道畿，元帝长子，母荀氏。幼而聪哲，元帝尝置膝前，问「日与长安孰远」，答「日近」，明日又问，答「日远」，曰「举头见日，不见长安」——童稚之间，已见其敏。永昌元年元帝崩，绍即位，年二十四，改元太宁。

明帝即位之时，王敦拥兵坐镇武昌，跋扈已甚。帝素有谋略：太宁元年以王导辅政，示安王氏；密察敦营，微服至其营垒视之。太宁二年，王敦病笃，帝亲征，遣温峤、庾亮等讨破其党，敦败死，江东复安——剪平大憝，朝纲为之一振。

太宁三年闰月，帝崩，年二十七。史称明帝「性至孝，有文武才略」，以弱年天子亲平权臣之乱，在东晋诸帝中最称英主；惜享年不永，遗孤成帝年仅五岁，庾太后临朝，庾亮执政，遂启苏峻之乱。明帝之英明与短祚，正成东晋「主少国疑、权臣迭起」之局的反照——其若在位稍久，东晋政局或当改观。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷006《明帝纪》、卷098《王敦传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Shao, styled Daoji, was the eldest son of Emperor Yuan by Lady Xun, and sharp from childhood. Emperor Yuan once set him on his knee and asked whether the sun or Chang'an was farther; "the sun," he answered. Asked again the next day he reversed himself: "the sun is farther — I can lift my head and see the sun, but not Chang'an." In the 1st year of Yongchang Yuan died and Shao took the throne at twenty-four, changing the era to Taining.

His reign opened with Wang Dun holding Wuchang, overbearing to the last degree. Ming had strategy: in the 1st year of Taining he made Wang Dao regent to reassure the Wangs; he himself, in disguise, rode out and viewed Dun's camps. In the 2nd year of Taining, with Dun dying of illness, the emperor campaigned in person, and Wen Qiao, Yu Liang, and the others broke Dun's party; Dun died as his army collapsed, and Jiangdong was at peace — the great villain cut down and the court's authority restored.

In the intercalary month of the 3rd year of Taining he died at twenty-seven. The histories call him "devoted to his parents, gifted in arms and letters," the strongest of the Eastern Jin sovereigns, a young emperor who put down a rebel minister in person. His early death left a five-year-old heir, Empress Yu's regency, and Yu Liang's government — and the Su Jun revolt. His brilliance and his brevity together shaped the pattern of Eastern Jin: a child on the throne, strong ministers rising.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 6 ("Benji of Emperor Ming"), ch. 98 (biography of Wang Dun) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 晋成帝 · 主要事迹

司马衍字世根，明帝长子，母庾皇后。太宁三年明帝崩，衍即位，年五岁，庾太后临朝，庾亮执政。成帝幼而聪敏，有成人之量，然国政操于庾氏：庾亮谋夺苏峻、祖约兵权，激成事变——咸和二年苏峻、祖约起兵，次年攻陷台城，帝蒙尘，赖温峤、陶侃等起兵勤王，咸和四年讨平苏峻，帝还宫。

苏峻乱后，东晋中枢元气大伤：成帝以冲龄之君，委政大臣，庾亮兄弟相继执政，兵权外重。咸康年间，后赵石虎南寇历阳，江淮戒严；慕容皝称燕王，辽东坐大。帝诏实编户，土断之议渐起，然政未见大效。

咸康八年六月，成帝崩，年二十二。帝临崩，庾冰以「国有强敌，宜立长君」，劝立弟岳，遂有康帝之立——东晋「兄终弟及」之先例，自此而开。史臣评成帝「少即大位，委政大臣」，谦恭而已；其朝苏峻之乱，为东晋建国以来最大之动荡，赖陶侃等名臣匡复，然门阀秉政之格局愈固，后患愈深。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷007《成帝纪》、卷073《庾亮传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Yan, styled Shigen, was the eldest son of Emperor Ming by Empress Yu. On Ming's death in the 3rd year of Taining he took the throne at five, with Empress Yu holding court and Yu Liang the government. Sharp and mature beyond his years, he nonetheless sat under the Yu clan's rule: Yu Liang's move to strip Su Jun and Zu Yue of their troops set off the storm — in the 2nd year of Xianhe the two rose, and in the 3rd stormed the palace, the emperor carried off, until Wen Qiao and Tao Kan raised the loyal armies and in the 4th year of Xianhe Su Jun was destroyed and the emperor returned.

After the Su Jun revolt the center was spent: the child emperor left government to his ministers, the Yu brothers governing in turn with the armies outside the capital. In the Xiankang years Shi Hu of Later Zhao raided Liyang and the Jiang-Huai went on alert; Murong Huang styled himself King of Yan and Liaodong grew strong. The emperor ordered the household registers filled, and the talk of local registration began — but no great reform came of it.

In the sixth month of the 8th year of Xiankang he died at twenty-two. On his deathbed, Yu Bing — "with strong enemies abroad, a grown sovereign should be raised" — had his younger brother Yue brought in, opening the Eastern Jin practice of brother succeeding brother. The historians judge Cheng a modest sovereign who left government to his ministers; his reign saw the greatest upheaval since the founding, the Su Jun revolt, restored by Tao Kan and the great officers — and the great clans' grip on government only tightened.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 7 ("Benji of Emperor Cheng"), ch. 73 (biography of Yu Liang) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 晋康帝 · 主要事迹

司马岳字世同，明帝子，成帝弟，封琅邪王。咸康八年成帝崩，庾冰等以国有强敌、宜立长君，遂迎立岳，改元建元——东晋「兄终弟及」自此为常。康帝在位仅二年，朝政仍操于庾氏兄弟：何充等辅政，庾翼以帝舅之亲镇武昌，欲北伐中原，经营襄阳，然未及举事而帝崩。

建元二年九月，康帝崩，年二十三，太子司马聃即位，即穆帝，年仅二岁。康帝之世，唯一大事为庾翼北伐之议：时后赵石虎已衰，庾翼欲乘机北上，然朝议不一，事未成行。其后桓温崛起，东晋北伐之业，终落于桓氏之手。

史家评康帝：「在位二年，国事多仍门阀。」以短祚之君，当强臣之朝，无所作为，亦无所失德。然其立也，出于庾氏「立长君」之谋；其崩也，遗子幼冲——东晋「主少国疑」之局，自明帝崩后屡见不鲜，康帝不过其间一过客。庾氏之强，遂成东晋门阀政治之缩影。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Yue, styled Shitong, was a son of Emperor Ming and younger brother of Emperor Cheng, enfeoffed Prince of Langya. In the 8th year of Xiankang, on Cheng's death, Yu Bing and the others — "with strong enemies abroad, a grown sovereign should be raised" — brought in Yue, changing the era to Jianyuan. Eastern Jin's practice of brother succeeding brother became the norm. Kang reigned barely two years, the government still in the Yu brothers' hands: He Chong and the others were regents, while Yu Yi, the emperor's uncle, held Wuchang and planned a northern expedition, building up Xiangyang — but he died before the enterprise could begin.

In the ninth month of the 2nd year of Jianyuan Kang died at twenty-three, and his son Sima Dan, two years old, took the throne as Emperor Mu. The one notable thing of Kang's reign was Yu Yi's northern plan: with Shi Hu of Later Zhao already failing, Yi wished to strike north, but the court could not agree, and nothing came of it. The northern enterprise then passed to Huan Wen and the Huan house.

The historians say of Kang: "Two years on the throne, the government still of the great clans." A brief reign amid strong ministers, he did nothing and did no harm. But he came to the throne by the Yu clan's "grown sovereign" plot, and left a child heir — the Eastern Jin pattern of "a child sovereign, a doubtful state" continued; Kang was but a passing figure in it, the Yu clan's power the real story of his age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 7 ("Benji of Emperor Kang"), ch. 73 (biography of Yu Yi) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 晋穆帝 · 主要事迹

司马聃字彭子，康帝子。建元二年康帝崩，聃即位，年二岁，褚太后临朝，改元永和。穆帝之朝，实为桓温之朝：永和三年，桓温伐蜀，灭成汉，李势降，东晋之疆域复通巴蜀；永和五年石虎死，后赵大乱，殷浩北伐，永和六年溃败，桓温之势更盛；永和十年，温北伐至霸上，关中父老争持牛酒迎劳，然持重不进，粮尽而还；永和十二年，温败姚襄，收复洛阳，修谒先帝诸陵——北伐之业，一时大振。

升平年间，桓温驻荆、扬，遥控朝廷；谢万北征败绩，许昌、颍川复失；升平四年谢安出仕，为桓温司马。东晋之政局，自此转入谢氏与桓氏之争。

升平五年五月，穆帝崩，年十九。史臣评穆帝：「幼冲嗣位，政在强臣。」桓温北伐之武功，皆其朝事而非其功；然以二岁童子坐帝位十七年，国家不至大乱，赖褚太后与诸大臣维持。东晋偏安之局，至此已历五帝，门阀相争愈烈，桓温北伐之业，终成其篡位之资。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷008《穆帝纪》、卷098《桓温传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Dan, styled Pengzi, was the son of Emperor Kang. On Kang's death in the 2nd year of Jianyuan he took the throne at two, with Empress Chu as regent and the era changed to Yonghe. Mu's reign was in fact Huan Wen's: in the 3rd year of Yonghe Wen conquered Shu, destroyed Cheng Han, and took Li Shi's surrender, rejoining Bashu to Eastern Jin; in the 5th year Shi Hu died and Later Zhao collapsed, and Yin Hao's expedition of the 6th year failed, leaving Wen stronger than ever; in the 10th year Wen marched to Bashang, where the elders of Guanzhong came out with wine and meat to welcome him — but he hesitated, ran out of grain, and withdrew; in the 12th year he defeated Yao Xiang, restored Luoyang, and repaired the imperial tombs. The northern enterprise flourished as never before.

In the Shengping years Wen held Jingzhou and Yangzhou, commanding the court from afar; Xie Wan's campaign of the 1st year collapsed and Xuchang and Yingchuan were lost again; in the 4th year Xie An first entered office, as Wen's military adviser. Eastern Jin's politics turned on the struggle of the Xie and Huan houses.

In the fifth month of the 5th year of Shengping Mu died at nineteen. The historians say: "A child on the throne, the government with the strong ministers." Huan Wen's northern victories were deeds of the reign, not of the sovereign; yet a two-year-old holding the throne seventeen years without the state's collapse was thanks to Empress Chu and the great officers. Eastern Jin, through five sovereigns, had settled into its pattern — the great clans contending, and Huan Wen's northern glory becoming the springboard of his ambition.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 8 ("Benji of Emperor Mu"), ch. 98 (biography of Huan Wen) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 晋哀帝 · 主要事迹

司马丕字千龄，成帝长子，母周氏，封琅邪王。升平五年穆帝崩，无子，丕以成帝长子入继大统，改元隆和。哀帝即位时年二十，本可亲政有为，然性好黄老之术，断谷服食长生药，政务遂废。

隆和元年，桓温请迁都洛阳，朝议纷纭，帝以「未暇」婉拒，其事遂寝——然桓温之势，自此愈张。兴宁元年，桓温进位大司马，都督中外诸军事，权威更重。兴宁二年，帝服饵过度，药发不能亲政，褚太后复临朝摄政。兴宁三年二月，帝崩，年二十五。

哀帝之崩，史书直书「药发」——断谷饵药，遂至委顿，为东晋诸帝之奇祸。史家论曰：帝非昏暴之主，亦无失德之事，然以长生之妄，丧其躯命；桓温之强，亦在其世坐大。东晋自明帝以下，主皆幼冲或庸弱，哀帝年长而不自爱，尤为可惜。桓温废立之谋，已见端于此朝。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷008《哀帝纪》、卷098《桓温传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Pi, styled Qianling, was the eldest son of Emperor Cheng by Lady Zhou, enfeoffed Prince of Langya. In the 5th year of Shengping Emperor Mu died without issue, and Pi, as Cheng's eldest son, took the throne at twenty, changing the era to Longhe. Old enough to govern in person, he chose instead to devote himself to Huang–Lao: he gave up grain and took the elixirs of immortality, and the business of government fell away.

In the 1st year of Longhe Huan Wen urged moving the capital to Luoyang; the court argued endlessly, the emperor pleaded "no leisure," and the matter died — but Wen's power had grown visibly. In the 1st year of Xingning Wen was made grand marshal with command over all the armies, more formidable than ever. In the 2nd year of Xingning the drugs overpowered the emperor; unable to attend to government, he gave the regency to Empress Chu again. In the second month of the 3rd year he died at twenty-five.

The histories record his death plainly: the drugs. His fasting and elixirs wasted him — the strange fate of an Eastern Jin sovereign. He was no tyrant and did nothing wrong; he simply destroyed himself chasing immortality. Huan Wen's power swelled in his reign, and the plot of deposition was already in view. Of the Eastern Jin emperors after Ming, most were children or weaklings; Ai, grown and healthy, was the more to be pitied for wasting himself.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 8 ("Benji of Emperor Ai"), ch. 98 (biography of Huan Wen) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 晋废帝 · 主要事迹

司马奕字延龄，成帝子，哀帝弟，封东海王。兴宁三年哀帝崩，奕即位，改元太和。废帝在位六年，无大失德；然其时桓温北伐前燕，太和四年至枋头，粮尽退军，大败而归——北伐之望绝，桓温之威受挫。

桓温素有异志，枋头之败后，名实俱损，遂思借废立以立威：太和六年十一月，温入朝，诬帝「痿疾不能男」，以太后令废帝为东海王，又降为海西公。帝被废后，温犹使人构陷，帝「深自晦匿」，杜口不谈朝事，惟以声色自晦——「海西公」遂得善终。

太元十一年，海西公薨于吴，年四十五。史家论废帝：「帝实无大过，温欲立威而废之。」东晋门阀政治，权臣可以一言废立天子，自桓温废帝始；其后桓玄篡位、刘裕禅代，皆沿此轨。废帝以一庸主之身，遭权臣之诬，虽保首领，然中国皇权之尊严，自此扫地。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷008《海西公纪》、卷098《桓温传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Sima Yi, styled Yanling, was a son of Emperor Cheng and younger brother of Emperor Ai, enfeoffed Prince of Donghai. On Ai's death in the 3rd year of Xingning he took the throne, changing the era to Taihe. Six years he reigned without great fault; but in the 4th year of Taihe Huan Wen's northern expedition against Former Yan ran out of grain at Fangtou and came back in ruin — the hope of the north was gone, and Wen's prestige was wounded.

Wen, who harbored designs, sought to restore his name by deposing the emperor: in the eleventh month of the 6th year of Taihe he came to court, falsely charged the emperor with impotence — "the emperor cannot father sons" — and by the empress dowager's edict deposed him as Prince of Donghai, later reducing him to Duke of Haixi. Even in exile Wen's men came to slander him; the deposed emperor "hid himself utterly," never speaking of court affairs, hiding in music and women — and so the Duke of Haixi died in his bed.

In the 11th year of Taiyuan the Duke of Haixi died in Wu at forty-five. The historians say: "The emperor was in fact without great fault; Wen deposed him to awe the court." That a strong minister could depose an emperor on a word began with Huan Wen's act; Huan Xuan's usurpation and Liu Yu's abdication followed the same road. A mediocre sovereign done to death by calumny, he kept his life but not his throne — and the dignity of the imperial office, in Eastern Jin, was never quite the same.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 8 ("Benji of the Duke of Haixi"), ch. 98 (biography of Huan Wen) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 晋简文帝 · 主要事迹

司马昱字道万，元帝少子，封会稽王。性清虚寡欲，尤善玄言，为东晋清谈宗主；历成、康、穆、哀、废五朝，长期辅政，录尚书事。太和六年，桓温废帝，迎立昱即位，改元咸安——时昱年五十二，在帝位不及一年。

简文帝之立，纯为桓温废立之需：温入朝，昱垂涕而受禅，即位后，温欲求九锡、觊觎禅让。帝与王坦之、谢安等周旋，温病笃而请不行——「温求九锡未成」，晋祚得延。咸安二年七月，帝崩于东堂，年五十三，遗诏「大司马温依周公居摄故事」，孝武帝曜即位，时年十一。

史臣评简文帝：「清虚寡欲，尤善玄言。」以清谈名士坐天子位，本无治世之才，亦无争权之志；其在位之业，惟在婉拒桓温之禅让，为司马氏延祚十载。然谢安、王坦之能周旋其间，实赖其主之谦抑——简文一朝，虽无德政，然以「受制权臣而无尺寸之权」之身，得全晋祚，亦不失为乱世自全之道。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷009《简文帝纪》、卷098《桓温传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。
