bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Hong (born into the Tuoba clan) is a pivot of institutional reform that no reader of the Northern and Southern Dynasties can bypass. He ascended the throne as a child at Pingcheng in Yanxing 1 (471), with Empress Dowager Wenming (Feng) ruling as regent in his early years. This page takes 《魏书·高祖纪》（卷007上下） as the backbone of its chronology, cross-checked against the empresses' biographies (皇后传) and the Treatise on Food and Money (食货志) in the Book of Wei, and against the corresponding annals of 《资治通鉴》.

During the Taihe era, the salary system (Taihe 8) paid officials to reward integrity and discipline the bureaucracy; the equal-field system (Taihe 9) was promulgated and would deeply shape Sui–Tang debates on land tenure; and the three-elders system (Taihe 10) rebuilt grassroots administration. Together these Taihe New Policies formed the institutional skeleton of the reform.

In Taihe 17 (493), under the pretext of a southern campaign, he moved the capital to Luoyang, shifting Northern Wei's political center south. There followed the ban on Hu dress and speech, the fixing of aristocratic clan rankings, and the change of the Tuoba surname to Yuan—sinicization rolled out in full. The costs were equally clear: in Taihe 20 (496), Crown Prince Yuan Xun, who had resisted sinicization, was deposed, shaking the palace.

In his final years he campaigned persistently on the Xiangyang front, draining the state's strength; in Taihe 23 (499) he died in the army during a southern campaign and was buried back at Luoyang. The sinicization line was carried on by Xuanwu, while the controversies of radical reform and the tensions with the Six Garrisons were sown here as well. Read alongside
: one first completed the unification of the north by arms, the other remade the dynasty's face through institutional reform—the two faces of Northern Wei meet and part in these two men.

emperors.bio_md:
# 宣武帝 · 主要事迹

元恪，孝文帝第二子。太和二十三年，孝文帝崩于南伐途中，恪即位，年十七，改元景明。宣武帝景明元年罢六辅亲政，亲理万机；在位十六年，北魏由孝文之锐意改革转入守成。其朝与梁武帝对峙：景明中，与梁争淮南、义阳等地，互有胜负，钟离之战魏军大败——北魏南进之势，自此受挫。

宣武之世，佛教极盛：王公贵戚竞造佛寺，「洛阳伽蓝，鳞次栉比」，佛寺千余所；帝亦亲讲佛经、度僧尼。然寺院经济坐大、僧侣免赋，为北魏末年社会矛盾之一因。宣武又崇汉化之余绪，然「宽以驭下，法网疏阔」，宗室权贵骄奢，北魏之弊渐积。

延昌四年，宣武帝崩，年三十三，子诩即位，是为孝明帝；胡太后临朝，北魏由盛转衰。史评宣武：「笃好文雅，登极之后，于时政事，颇留心焉」，然「委任群小，朝纲渐弛」。宣武承孝文之业而不能继其志，北魏之衰，自其世始。

> 本地参考：点校本《魏书》卷008《世宗纪》、卷114《释老志》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Ke, second son of Emperor Xiaowen, took the throne at seventeen when Xiaowen died on the southern campaign in the 23rd year of Taihe, changing the era to Jingming. In the 1st year of Jingming he dismissed the six regents and took up the government himself. His sixteen years turned from Xiaowen's eager reform to stewardship. His age faced Emperor Wu of Liang: in mid-Jingming he contended for Huainan and Yiyang with Liang, fortunes divided — until the great defeat at Zhongli, and the southern advance of Wei was checked.

His age saw Buddhism at its height: the princes and nobles raced to raise monasteries, "the monasteries of Luoyang packed like the teeth of a comb," over a thousand of them; the emperor lectured on the sutras himself and ordained monks. But the monastery economy grew, and monks freed from taxes — one seed of the realm's later ills. He carried on the sinicization, but "governed loosely, the net of the law wide," and the princes grew arrogant; the diseases of Northern Wei gathered.

He died in the 4th year of Yanchang at thirty-three; his son Xu, Emperor Xiaoming, succeeded, with Empress Hu entering the government — the turn of Northern Wei from height to decline. The histories say he "truly loved letters and, once on the throne, gave real care to government," yet "trusted the petty men, and the court's discipline slackened." He inherited Xiaowen's enterprise but not his purpose; the decline of Wei began in his reign.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Weishu*, ch. 8 ("Benji of Emperor Xuanwu"), ch. 114 ("Treatise on Buddhism and Daoism") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 孝明帝 · 主要事迹

元诩，宣武帝第二子。延昌四年宣武崩，诩即位，年六岁，胡太后临朝称制。孝明之世，北魏由盛转衰之关键：正光元年，元叉、刘腾幽胡太后于北宫，专政数年，朝政日非；正光四年，沃野镇破六韩拔陵起兵，六镇起义爆发——北镇军户之乱，席卷北方，北魏根基动摇。

武泰元年，胡太后复临朝，鸩杀孝明帝，年十九，立临洮王元钊（三岁幼主）；尔朱荣以此为口实，举兵南下，沉胡太后及幼主于河阴，又杀王公卿士二千余人——史称「河阴之变」，北魏宗室元气尽丧，自此名存实亡。

孝明帝「幼冲当乱，权在母后权臣」：其在位十三年，始终为胡太后、元叉等所制，不能自振。六镇起义为北魏亡国之导火索，而孝明之死、河阴之变，则直接开启北魏分裂之门——北魏之亡，实自孝明之世始。

> 本地参考：点校本《魏书》卷009《肃宗纪》、卷013《皇后传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Xu, second son of Emperor Xuanwu, took the throne at six on his father's death in the 4th year of Yanchang, with Empress Dowager Hu holding the court in her own name. His reign was the hinge of Northern Wei's fall: in the 1st year of Zhengguang, Yuan Cha and Liu Teng confined the empress in the northern palace and ruled for years, and the government decayed; in the 4th year of Zhengguang Poliuhan Baling rose at Woye garrison — the Six Garrisons rising swept the north, and the foundations of Wei trembled.

In the 1st year of Wutai the empress dowager returned to power and had Xiaoming poisoned, aged nineteen, setting up the infant Yuan Zhao; Erzhu Rong, taking this as his cause, marched south, drowned the empress and the infant in the river, and slew over two thousand princes and ministers — the Heyin massacre. The princes of Wei were spent, and the realm was a name only.

Xiaoming, "a child in the storm, the power with his mother and the strong ministers," sat thirteen years in the grip of Empress Hu and Yuan Cha, unable to move. The Six Garrisons rising was the fuse of Wei's ruin, and his death and the Heyin massacre opened the split of the realm — the fall of Northern Wei began in his reign.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Weishu*, ch. 9 ("Benji of Emperor Xiaoming"), ch. 13 (biographies of the empresses) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 孝庄帝 · 主要事迹

元子攸，彭城王元勰第三子。武泰元年，尔朱荣以胡太后鸩杀孝明帝为口实，举兵南下，立子攸为帝，改元建义。子攸即位即逢「河阴之变」：尔朱荣沉胡太后及幼主于河，杀王公卿士二千余人——北魏宗室之精英，一朝而尽。子攸虽居帝位，实为尔朱荣之傀儡。

永安二年，梁扶北魏宗室元颢入洛，子攸北奔，旋随尔朱荣复还洛阳；永安三年，尔朱荣擅权日甚，欲篡位，子攸与左右密谋，于明光殿手刃尔朱荣——「帝手刃荣，荣死」，一时快意。然尔朱氏余党未除：尔朱兆闻变，率兵入洛，执子攸，缢于晋阳三级佛寺，年二十四。

孝庄帝以复仇之志、手刃权臣，其勇可嘉；然「力不从心」，尔朱氏之势力未动分毫，而帝身死国乱。史评孝庄：「有英武之姿，而遭时多难」；其手刃尔朱荣一事，为北魏末年唯一之壮举，然亦不过回光返照——北魏自此转入尔朱、高欢、宇文泰之乱局。

> 本地参考：点校本《魏书》卷010《孝庄纪》、卷074《尔朱荣传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Ziyou, third son of the Prince of Pengcheng, Yuan Xie, was set up by Erzhu Rong in the 1st year of Jianyi, when Rong, using Empress Hu's poisoning of Xiaoming as his cause, marched south. His accession opened with the Heyin massacre: Rong drowned the empress and the infant emperor in the river and slew over two thousand princes and ministers — the elite of the Wei house, gone in a day. Ziyou sat as Rong's puppet.

In the 2nd year of Yong'an, Liang propped up the Wei prince Yuan Hao to enter Luoyang; the emperor fled north and soon returned with Rong. In the 3rd year of Yong'an, Rong's arrogance grew to usurpation, and Ziyou, plotting with his attendants, cut Rong down with his own hand in the Mingguang Hall — "the emperor slew Rong with his own hand, and Rong died" — a moment of satisfaction. But the Erzhu party was not spent: Erzhu Zhao, hearing of it, marched into Luoyang, seized Ziyou, and had him strangled at the Jinyang temple of three stories, aged twenty-four.

His will to avenge and his own hand against the strong minister were brave; but "the strength did not match," the Erzhu power was untouched, and the emperor died and the realm fell into chaos. The histories say he "had the bearing of a hero, but the age was against him": the slaying of Erzhu Rong was the one great deed of Wei's last years — yet only a dying ember, as the realm passed to the Erzhu, to Gao Huan, to Yuwen Tai.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Weishu*, ch. 10 ("Benji of Emperor Xiaozhuang"), ch. 74 (biography of Erzhu Rong) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 节闵帝 · 主要事迹

元恭，广陵王元羽之子，字修业。北魏末年宗室多遭杀戮，元恭「以佯聋自晦」，称疾不仕，历孝明、孝庄两朝，「佯聋积岁」。永安三年，孝庄帝被弑，尔朱世隆等议立新君，元恭佯聋已久之名，反成「聪明」之证——普泰元年，尔朱世隆等立恭为帝，改元普泰。

元恭在位约一年，傀儡于尔朱氏：尔朱兆据晋阳、尔朱世隆居洛阳，政出多门；又与建明帝元晔等并立，纪年混乱。普泰二年，高欢起兵讨尔朱氏，入洛阳，废节闵帝，幽于崇训佛寺，立平阳王元修（孝武帝）；旋以「外邀陈留王」之罪名，鸩杀之，年三十五。

史评节闵帝：「佯聋避祸，终亦不免。」北魏末年，宗室之死生操于权臣之手；元恭以佯聋全身，然终为高欢所废杀。其被废之时，「下车而拜，揖让而去」，从容受死，为乱世宗室中难得之气象。图鉴以其在位短促、名分存于魏统而列为准帝。

> 本地参考：点校本《魏书》卷011《前废帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Gong, styled Xiuye, was the son of the Prince of Guangling, Yuan Yu. In the last years of Northern Wei the princes were slaughtered wholesale, and Gong "hid himself by feigning deafness," pleading illness and refusing office through the reigns of Xiaoming and Xiaozhuang — "feigning deafness for years." After Xiaozhuang's slaying in the 3rd year of Yong'an, Erzhu Shilong and the others sought a new sovereign; Gong's long feigned deafness itself became his "wisdom" — in the 1st year of Putai they set him up, changing the era to Putai.

About a year he reigned as the Erzhu's puppet: Erzhu Zhao held Jinyang, Erzhu Shilong sat at Luoyang, and the government came from many mouths; he stood at once with the Jianming emperor and the rest, the eras tangled. In the 2nd year of Putai, Gao Huan rose against the Erzhu house, entered Luoyang, deposed Jiemin, confined him in the Chongxun monastery, and set up the Prince of Pingyang, Yuan Xiu (Emperor Xiaowu); then, on the charge of "summoning the Prince of Chenliu," had him poisoned, aged thirty-five.

The histories say: "he hid by feigning deafness, and could not escape in the end." In Wei's last years the princes lived and died by the strong ministers' will; Gong's feigned deafness saved him for a time, and Gao Huan destroyed him in the end. At his deposition, the records say, "he descended from the carriage, bowed, and went with folded hands" — a composure rare among the princes of that age. The gazetteer lists him as quasi-emperor for his brief reign and his place in the Wei line.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Weishu*, ch. 11 ("Benji of the Former Deposed Emperor") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 孝武帝 · 主要事迹

元修，广平武穆王元怀第三子，封平阳王。普泰二年，高欢废节闵帝，立修为帝，改元太昌。孝武帝「沉雅有度量」，然不甘为高欢傀儡：高欢居晋阳遥控朝政，帝与亲信密谋图欢，事泄；永熙三年，帝率轻骑出洛阳，西奔长安，依关中大行台宇文泰——北魏由此分为东西。

孝武帝入关后，改元永熙；然宇文泰之强，不亚于高欢：帝欲自专，与宇文泰矛盾渐深。同年（永熙三年）十二月，宇文泰使人鸩杀孝武帝于长安，年二十五。高欢闻孝武遇害，另立清河王世子元善见为帝（孝静帝），迁都邺——东魏始；宇文泰亦立元宝炬于长安——西魏始。北魏自道武开国至此凡一百四十九年，正式分裂。

史评孝武帝：「身当魏分，西奔不得善终。」其以不甘受制之志，西奔依泰，本欲借关中之力以图自振；然「入虎穴而投豺狼」，终为宇文氏所害。孝武之死，标志北魏统一之局终结：东西魏对峙、进而北齐北周对峙，中国历史转入新一轮南北朝。

元修，广平武穆王元怀第三子，封平阳王。普泰二年，高欢废节闵帝，立修为帝，改元太昌。孝武帝「沉雅有度量」，然不甘为高欢傀儡：高欢居晋阳遥控朝政，帝与亲信密谋图欢，事泄；永熙三年，帝率轻骑出洛阳，西奔长安，依关中大行台宇文泰——北魏由此分为东西。

孝武帝入关后，改元永熙；然宇文泰之强，不亚于高欢：帝欲自专，与宇文泰矛盾渐深。同年（永熙三年）十二月，宇文泰使人鸩杀孝武帝于长安，年二十五。高欢闻孝武遇害，另立清河王世子元善见为帝（孝静帝），迁都邺——东魏始；宇文泰亦立元宝炬于长安——西魏始。北魏自道武开国至此凡一百四十九年，正式分裂。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Xiu, third son of the Prince of Guangping, Yuan Huai, was enfeoffed Prince of Pingyang. In the 2nd year of Putai, Gao Huan deposed Emperor Jiemin and set up Xiu, changing the era to Taichang. Xiaowu "was grave and of real measure," but would not be Gao Huan's puppet: Huan sat at Jinyang ruling from afar, and the emperor, plotting with his intimates to destroy Huan, was discovered; in the 3rd year of Yongxi he rode out of Luoyang with a light escort, fled west to Chang'an, and leaned on the great governor of Guanzhong, Yuwen Tai — Northern Wei split into east and west.

In the pass he changed the era to Yongxi; but Yuwen Tai's grip was no lighter than Gao Huan's: as the emperor tried to stand alone, the breach with Tai widened. That same year, in the twelfth month, Tai had him poisoned at Chang'an, aged twenty-five. Gao Huan, on word of the poisoning, set up the heir of the Prince of Qinghe, Yuan Shanjian, and moved the capital to Ye — Eastern Wei began; Yuwen Tai set up Yuan Baoju at Chang'an — Western Wei began. Northern Wei, a hundred and forty-nine years from Daowu's founding, was formally split.

The histories say: "he sat at the split of Wei, fled west, and came to no good end." His resolve not to be a puppet drove him west to Tai, hoping to stand by the power of Guanzhong; but "he entered the tiger's den to fall to the wolf," and the Yuwen house destroyed him. His death ended the unity of Wei: East and West Wei, then Northern Qi and Northern Zhou, carried the realm into a new age of division.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Weishu*, ch. 11 ("Benji of the Emperor Who Departed"), and the *Beishi*, ch. 5 (Wei basic annals) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 孝静帝 · 主要事迹

元善见，清河王元亶之子。永熙三年，孝武帝西奔长安遇鸩，高欢迎善见为帝，迁都邺——东魏始。孝静帝「聪慧好文，美姿容」，然为高欢所制：高欢居晋阳，遥控朝政，「政刑赏罚，皆自欢出」，帝拱手而已。东魏与西魏并立十六年，沙苑、邙山、玉壁诸大战，互有胜负，高欢终未能灭西魏。

武定五年高欢卒，其子高澄继掌朝政，更逼帝甚；孝静帝尝愤言：「朕亦何用生为！」武定八年，高洋（高澄弟）受禅，东魏亡，孝静帝封中山王，寻遇害，年二十八。

孝静帝在位十六年，为东魏唯一之君：其「傀儡而不失人君之度」，尝与高澄对弈而色不变；然「聪慧好文，终为高氏所制」。东魏之亡，标志高氏代魏——北齐之兴，实以东魏之傀儡为过渡。史家论孝静：「以冲年受禅，坐视社稷之移，身死国亡，非其罪也。」

> 本地参考：点校本《魏书》卷012《孝静纪》、北齐书卷001《神武纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Shanjian was the son of the Prince of Qinghe, Yuan Dan. In the 3rd year of Yongxi, after Emperor Xiaowu fled west and was poisoned, Gao Huan received Shanjian as emperor and moved the capital to Ye — the beginning of Eastern Wei. Xiaojing was "sharp, fond of letters, and handsome," but Gao Huan held him: Huan sat at Jinyang ruling from afar, "rewards and punishments all coming from Huan," and the emperor folded his hands. Sixteen years Eastern and Western Wei stood side by side, the great battles of Shayuan, Mangshan, and Yubi fought to a standstill — Huan could never destroy the west.

In the 5th year of Wuding Huan died, and his son Gao Cheng took the government, pressing the emperor harder; Xiaojing once cried out, "Of what use is my life!" In the 8th year of Wuding, Gao Yang (Cheng's brother) received the abdication — Eastern Wei was no more — and Xiaojing, made Prince of Zhongshan, was soon done to death, aged twenty-eight.

Sixteen years the only sovereign of Eastern Wei: "a puppet, yet keeping the sovereign's bearing" — he played Go with Gao Cheng without changing color. But "sharp and fond of letters, in the end the Gao house's captive." The fall of Eastern Wei marked the Gao house's succession — the rise of Northern Qi ran through the puppet throne of Eastern Wei. The historians absolve Shanjian: "a child receiving the abdication, watching the realm pass, dying with the state — it was not his fault."

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Weishu*, ch. 12 ("Benji of Emperor Xiaojing"), and the *Bei Qishu*, ch. 1 ("Annals of the Divine Warrior") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 西魏文帝 · 主要事迹

元宝炬，京兆王元愉之子，孝文帝之孙。永熙三年，孝武帝西奔长安遇鸩，宇文泰立宝炬为帝，都长安，改元大统——西魏始。文帝在位十七年，为宇文泰之傀儡：大统三年，宇文泰于沙苑大破高欢，西魏立足；大统九年，邙山之战互有胜负——东西魏对峙之局，自此定型。

西魏之政，尽出宇文泰：其推行府兵制，置六军、二十四军，「广募关陇豪右以增军旅」，又行「六条诏书」之治，为北周及隋唐制度之渊源。文帝「垂拱而治」，国政一决于泰。大统十七年，文帝崩，年四十五，子钦继位。

史评文帝：「恭俭仁恕，守文之主。」西魏以偏安关中之地，与东魏抗衡而不败，赖宇文泰之经营；文帝虽无实权，然其恭默守位，为关陇集团之形成提供了稳定的皇权外壳——北周、隋、唐三代之基，实自西魏始。

> 本地参考：点校本《北史》卷005《魏本纪》、周书卷001《文帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Baoju, son of the Prince of Jingzhao, Yuan Yu, was a grandson of Emperor Xiaowen. In the 3rd year of Yongxi, after Xiaowu was poisoned at Chang'an, Yuwen Tai set up Baoju, with his capital at Chang'an, changing the era to Datong — the beginning of Western Wei. Seventeen years he reigned as Tai's puppet: in the 3rd year of Datong Tai broke Gao Huan at Shayuan and Western Wei stood; in the 9th year the Mangshan battle left fortunes divided — the standoff of East and West was fixed.

All the government of Western Wei came from Tai: he set up the fubing system, raising the six and twenty-four armies, "recruiting widely the strong houses of Guanzhong and Longxi to swell the ranks," and governed by the "six articles" — the seed of the institutions of Northern Zhou, Sui, and Tang. Wen "reigned with folded hands," every matter decided by Tai. He died in the 17th year of Datong at forty-five; his son Qin succeeded.

The histories say of him: "frugal, benevolent, a sovereign of preservation." Cramped in Guanzhong, Western Wei held Eastern Wei at bay through Tai's management; and Wen, though powerless, gave the emerging Guanzhong bloc a stable shell of imperial legitimacy — the foundations of Northern Zhou, Sui, and Tang were laid in Western Wei.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Beishi*, ch. 5 (Wei basic annals), and the *Zhoushu*, ch. 1 ("Annals of Emperor Wen") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 西魏废帝 · 主要事迹

元钦，文帝长子。大统十七年文帝崩，钦即位——史称「不建年号」，其意在革除汉化之弊、复鲜卑旧制（宇文泰主导）。废帝在位三年，无所作为，国政尽归宇文泰：大统十七年，西魏军破江陵，灭梁元帝，「收其府库珍宝及宋齐梁之书」——南朝文化之精华，尽入关中。

废帝不甘傀儡，与宇文泰谋：「帝密谋诛泰，泰觉之。」三年，宇文泰废钦为安定公，立其弟齐王元廓，旋鸩杀钦，年三十。史评废帝：「欲自振而败。」西魏之皇权，自孝武西奔后已尽入宇文氏；元钦欲复皇权，然「时异势殊」，终以废死终。

西魏废帝之死，标志关陇集团「君权虚置」之定型：此后西魏恭帝、北周诸帝，皆宇文氏掌中之物。而破江陵一役，使西魏尽收南朝文物——隋唐制度之源，自西魏而盛。

> 本地参考：点校本《北史》卷005《魏本纪》、周书卷002《文帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

Yuan Qin, eldest son of Emperor Wen, took the throne on his father's death in the 17th year of Datong — the histories note he "fixed no era name," a move of Yuwen Tai's to strip away the sinicizing forms and restore Xianbei ways. Three years he reigned, doing nothing, the government wholly Tai's: in the 3rd year the Western Wei armies broke Jiangling and destroyed Emperor Yuan of Liang, "taking the treasures of his storehouses and the books of Song, Qi, and Liang" — the cultural wealth of the south passed into Guanzhong.

The Deposed Emperor would not be a puppet: "the emperor plotted secretly to slay Tai, and Tai learned of it." In the 3rd year Tai deposed Qin as Duke of Anding, set up his brother, the Prince of Qi, Kuo, and soon poisoned Qin, aged thirty. The histories say: "he would have stood on his own, and failed." Since Xiaowu's flight west, the power of the Western Wei throne was wholly the Yuwens'; Qin's attempt to restore it ended in deposition and death.

His fall fixed the "empty throne" of the Guanzhong bloc: from the Gong emperor of Western Wei through the emperors of Northern Zhou, the throne was the Yuwens' instrument. And the Jiangling conquest brought the south's books and institutions into Guanzhong — the sources of Sui–Tang institutions, gathered under Western Wei.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Beishi*, ch. 5 (Wei basic annals), and the *Zhoushu*, ch. 2 ("Annals of Emperor Wen") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 西魏恭帝 · 主要事迹

元廓，文帝第四子。三年，废帝元钦被废，宇文泰立廓为帝。恭帝在位两年余，国政尽归宇文泰：泰行「周礼」之制，仿古六官，西魏之政，皆泰之政。三年，宇文泰卒，年五十；其侄宇文护辅政，泰之子宇文觉承袭。

同年，宇文护逼恭帝禅位于宇文觉——西魏亡，北周立。恭帝禅后封宋公，旋遇害。西魏自文帝至恭帝，历三帝二十三年而亡；然西魏之制度遗产——府兵制、六官制、关陇集团——尽为北周继承，进而为隋唐之基。

史评恭帝：「身当禅代，西魏终结。」以幼冲之君，坐视宇文氏之代兴，身不由己；其禅位与遇害，与东魏孝静帝如出一辙——东西两魏，同为权臣之过渡政权。西魏虽亡，然其开创之关陇本位、府兵制度，实为隋唐帝国之直接源头。

> 本地参考：点校本《北史》卷005《魏本纪》、周书卷003《孝闵帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuan Kuo, fourth son of Emperor Wen, was set up by Yuwen Tai after the Deposed Emperor's fall in the 3rd year. Two years and more he reigned, the government wholly Tai's: Tai ran the state on the *Rites of Zhou*, restoring the six ministries of antiquity — the government of Western Wei was Tai's government. In the 3rd year Yuwen Tai died at fifty; his nephew Yuwen Hu took the regency, and Tai's son Yuwen Jue inherited the power.

That same year Hu pressed Gong to abdicate to Jue — Western Wei was no more, and Northern Zhou arose. Gong, made Duke of Song, was soon done to death. Western Wei, three emperors and twenty-three years from Wen's accession, passed away; but its institutional legacy — the fubing system, the six ministries, the Guanzhong bloc — passed entire to Northern Zhou and thence to Sui and Tang.

The histories say of him: "caught in the abdication, he ended Western Wei." A child sovereign watching the Yuwens take the realm, not his own master; his abdication and death mirror Emperor Xiaojing of Eastern Wei — the two Wei, both transitional states of strong ministers. Western Wei died, but the Guanzhong-based institutions and the fubing system it created were the direct source of the Sui–Tang empire.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Beishi*, ch. 5 (Wei basic annals), and the *Zhoushu*, ch. 3 ("Annals of Emperor Xiaomin") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 文宣帝 · 主要事迹

高洋字子进，高欢第二子。天保元年，东魏孝静帝禅位，洋即皇帝位，国号齐，都邺——北齐始。高洋即位之初，励精图治：「初践大位，留心政术」，革除魏末之弊，重用汉族士人杨愔等；又北讨山胡、契丹、库莫奚，「亲临矢石」，拓地至长城之外；天保六年发民夫筑长城，自西河至海——北齐武功之盛，实自文宣始。

然高洋晚年，以酒狂称：「末年遂昏淫残暴」，常于醉后杀人，或自为士卒于市，荒悖不可理喻；又「筑三台，穷极壮丽」。史家谓其「初政清明，末年酒狂」——同一人而前后判若两人，为北齐政治之一大怪象。

天保十年，高洋崩，年三十一，子高殷即位。史评文宣：「英主而暴君，兼而有之。」北齐立国之基，成于文宣之初政；北齐暴政之端，亦起于文宣之末年——其酒狂杀戮，为北齐暴君传统之始，其后武成、后主之昏，皆由此承。

> 本地参考：点校本《北齐书》卷004《文宣纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Gao Yang, styled Zijin, was the second son of Gao Huan. In the 1st year of Tianbao, Emperor Xiaojing of Eastern Wei abdicated; Yang took the throne, styled the realm Qi, and made Ye his capital — the beginning of Northern Qi. At first he governed with vigor: "on taking the throne he gave real care to the arts of government," clearing away the evils of Wei's last years and employing the Han gentry, Yang Yin and the rest; he campaigned north in person against the mountain Hu, the Khitan, and the Kumo Xi, carrying the border beyond the Great Wall; in the 6th year of Tianbao he drove the people to build the Wall from the Xi River to the sea — the martial glory of Northern Qi began with Wenxuan.

But in his last years he was known for drunken madness: "in his final years he sank into lewdness and cruelty," killing in his cups, playing the soldier in the streets, ungovernable in his folly; he "raised the three terraces, of the utmost splendor." The histories note the same man, clear in his first years and mad in his last — one of the great oddities of Northern Qi politics.

He died in the 10th year of Tianbao at thirty-one; his son Yin succeeded. The histories say of him: "hero and tyrant in one." The foundation of Qi was laid in his early government; the tradition of Qi's tyranny also began with his last years — his drunken slaughter opened the line of tyrants, and the darkness of Wucheng and the Last Sovereign followed.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Bei Qishu*, ch. 4 ("Benji of Emperor Wenxuan") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 北齐废帝 · 主要事迹

高殷，文宣帝长子。天保十年文宣崩，殷即位，年十五，改元乾明。废帝「幼而好学，美姿容」，其母李皇后为汉人——高殷之立，本为汉族士人杨愔等所拥戴，意在革除鲜卑贵戚之弊。

然北齐贵戚势力根深：文宣之弟常山王高演、长广王高湛等，皆鲜卑化之宗室，素轻汉人。乾明元年，高演与高湛等发动政变，杀杨愔、燕子献等，废殷为济南王；皇建元年，高演自立为帝；皇建二年，高演使人害殷于晋阳，年十七。

废帝之废，为北齐「叔夺侄位」之始：其后孝昭、武成相继以宗室篡立，北齐皇权落入鲜卑贵戚之手，汉族士人势力一蹶不振。史评废帝：「幼而好学，不能自固。」以十五岁冲主当强叔之朝，其废其死，皆身不由己——北齐之衰，自废帝之废而加速。

> 本地参考：点校本《北齐书》卷005《废帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Gao Yin, eldest son of Emperor Wenxuan, took the throne on his father's death in the 10th year of Tianbao at fifteen, changing the era to Qianming. The Deposed Emperor was "studious from youth and handsome," and his mother, Empress Li, was a Han — his accession was backed by the Han gentry, Yang Yin and the rest, who meant to check the Xianbei nobles.

But the nobles' roots ran deep: his uncles the Princes of Changshan and Zhangguang, Gao Yan and Gao Zhan, were Xianbei in spirit and held the Han in contempt. In the 1st year of Qianming they staged their coup, slew Yang Yin, Yan Zixian, and the others, and deposed Yin as Prince of Jinan; in the 1st year of Huangjian Yan took the throne himself; in the 2nd year Yan had Yin done to death at Jinyang, aged seventeen.

His deposition began the "uncle taking the nephew's throne" of Northern Qi: Xiaozhao and Wucheng in turn usurped as princes, the throne fell into the Xianbei nobles' hands, and the Han gentry's power was broken at a stroke. The histories say: "studious from youth, unable to hold his own." A fifteen-year-old before strong uncles, his deposition and his death were not his choosing — and the decline of Qi quickened from his fall.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Bei Qishu*, ch. 5 ("Benji of the Deposed Emperor") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 孝昭帝 · 主要事迹

高演字延安，高欢第六子。皇建元年，演与弟湛等废侄高殷，自立为帝，改元皇建。孝昭帝「留心政事」，史称「明察俭约」：即位后大赦改元、任用旧臣，欲革文宣末年之弊；又减轻赋役、整顿吏治，北齐政治为之一新。

然孝昭在位仅一年：皇建二年，亲征库莫奚，堕马伤肋，「遂不能兴」，寻崩，年二十七。临终传位弟高湛（武成帝），以「太子年幼」为由，兄终弟及。史载孝昭临终之悔：因杀废帝高殷，「自以不义」，尝自愧曰「吾尝害济南王」——杀侄夺位之事，终成其心疾。

史评孝昭：「明察俭约，欲革文宣之弊」，然「以篡得位，享年不永」。北齐五帝之中，孝昭最称贤明，惜其短祚；其废侄之事，虽得位不正，然其治绩为北齐短暂之清明。孝昭崩后，武成即位，北齐复入昏暴之途。

bio_parts_en.value:
Gao Yan, styled Yan'an, was the sixth son of Gao Huan. In the 1st year of Huangjian, with his brother Zhan, he deposed his nephew Yin and took the throne himself, changing the era to Huangjian. Xiaozhao "attended to government," the histories calling him "clear-sighted and frugal": on accession he granted amnesty, employed the old ministers, and set out to repair the evils of Wenxuan's last years; he lightened the levies and disciplined the officials, and the government of Qi was renewed for a moment.

But he reigned barely a year: in the 2nd year of Huangjian, campaigning in person against the Kumo Xi, he fell from his horse, hurt his ribs, "and could not rise," dying soon after at twenty-seven. On his deathbed he passed the throne to his brother Zhan (Emperor Wucheng), "the heir being young" — brother succeeding brother. The records tell of his dying remorse: having slain the deposed emperor Yin, "he thought himself unjust," and said, "I once harmed the Prince of Jinan" — the usurpation had become his sickness.

The histories say: "clear-sighted and frugal, he meant to repair Wenxuan's evils," yet "won the throne by usurpation, and his years were few." Of Qi's five sovereigns Xiaozhao was the worthiest — pity his reign was brief; his seizure of the throne was ill-gotten, but his government was the one brief clarity of Qi. With his death Wucheng took the throne, and Qi returned to the dark road.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Bei Qishu*, ch. 6 ("Benji of Emperor Xiaozhao") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 武成帝 · 主要事迹

高湛，高欢第九子。皇建二年孝昭崩，湛即位，改元太宁，次年改元河清。武成帝即位之初，尚有可称：太宁元年颁行律令，河清年间修撰《齐律》，为北齐法制之成就；又以斛律光等宿将为辅，与北周对峙，北齐疆域尚称稳固。

然武成帝「荒淫无度」：史载其「奢淫骄纵」，宠幸和士开等佞臣，朝政日坏；河清四年，禅位太子高纬，自称太上皇，「犹预国政」，而天统年间宠臣弄权更甚。武成之世，北齐由盛转衰：斛律光等名将渐被疏远，佞幸把持朝政，「齐政之衰，自武成始」。

天统五年，武成崩于晋阳，年三十二。史评武成：「荒淫委任佞幸，为齐衰张本。」北齐之亡，不亡于后主一朝，而亡于武成之荒纵：杀贤臣、任佞幸、禅位自娱，北齐之弊政，皆自武成开其端。

> 本地参考：点校本《北齐书》卷007《武成纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Gao Zhan, ninth son of Gao Huan, took the throne after Xiaozhao's death in the 2nd year of Huangjian, changing the eras to Taining and then Heqing. His opening years had something to show: in the 1st year of Taining he issued the statutes, and in the Heqing years the *Qi Code* was compiled — the legal achievement of Northern Qi; with the veterans like Hulü Guang beside him, he held the line against Northern Zhou, and the borders of Qi held.

But he "sank into debauchery without limit": the records tell of his "extravagance and arrogance," his favoring of the flatterer He Shikai, and the government rotted; in the 4th year of Heqing he abdicated to his heir Gao Wei and styled himself Grand Emperor, "still taking part in the government," while in the Tiantong years the favorites' power grew worse. The turn of Qi from strength to decline came in his reign: the great generals like Hulü Guang were pushed aside, the favorites held the court — "the decline of Qi's government began with Wucheng."

He died at Jinyang in the 5th year of Tiantong at thirty-two. The histories say: "debauched, trusting flatterers, he laid the ground of Qi's decline." Qi did not fall in the Last Sovereign's reign alone; it fell to Wucheng's license — slaying the worthy, trusting the favorites, abdicating to his pleasures: the diseases of Qi all began with him.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Bei Qishu*, ch. 7 ("Benji of Emperor Wucheng") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 北齐后主 · 主要事迹

高纬字仁纲，武成帝长子。天统元年武成禅位，纬即位，年十岁，改元天统。后主「好弹琵琶」，尝自作《无愁曲》，自弹自唱，侍者数百人和之，史称「无愁天子」——以亡国之忧为无愁之乐，其昏聩可知。

后主在位十二年，北齐由衰而亡：武平三年，听信祖珽等谗言，杀名将斛律光——「国之干城，一朝而尽」，北周闻之大喜；又杀兰陵王高长恭等宗室名将，自毁长城。武平七年，周武帝亲征伐齐，晋州失守，后主仓皇奔邺，又传位幼主高恒；承光元年，周军克邺，后主被俘，北齐亡。

后主被俘后，周武帝封为温国公，未几以「谋反」之罪赐死。史评后主：「无愁天子，亡国之君。」北齐以高欢、高洋两代经营之基业，传六帝二十八年而亡——其间武成之荒纵、后主之昏聩，自毁长城，终致国亡。「无愁」二字，遂成北齐亡国之谶。

> 本地参考：点校本《北齐书》卷008《后主纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Gao Wei, styled Rengang, was the eldest son of Wucheng. In the 1st year of Tiantong Wucheng abdicated and Wei took the throne at ten, changing the era to Tiantong. The Last Sovereign "loved the pipa," and composed a *Song without Sorrow* which he played and sang himself while hundreds of attendants joined in — the histories call him the "Sorrowless Sovereign": making the realm's ruin a joy without sorrow, his blindness could go no further.

Twelve years he reigned, and Qi went from decline to death: in the 3rd year of Wuping, on the slanders of Zu Ting and the rest, he slew the great general Hulü Guang — "the realm's shield, gone in a day," to the joy of Zhou; he also slew the Prince of Lanling, Gao Changgong, and other princes and generals, pulling down his own wall. In the 7th year of Wuping Emperor Wu of Zhou campaigned in person; Jinzhou fell, the Last Sovereign fled to Ye in panic, and passed the throne to the infant Gao Heng; in the 1st year of Chengguang the Zhou army took Ye, the Last Sovereign was captured, and Northern Qi was no more.

Taken to Chang'an, he was made Duke of Wenguo by Emperor Wu of Zhou, and soon put to death on a charge of "revolt." The histories say: "the Sorrowless Sovereign, the sovereign of a lost realm." The enterprise of Gao Huan and Gao Yang, six sovereigns and twenty-eight years, was spent — Wucheng's license and the Last Sovereign's blindness pulling down the wall until the realm fell. "Without sorrow" became the prophecy of Qi's ruin.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Bei Qishu*, ch. 8 ("Benji of the Last Sovereign") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 孝闵帝 · 主要事迹

宇文觉，宇文泰第三子。宇文泰卒后，其侄宇文护辅政；西魏恭帝三年，宇文护逼恭帝禅位于觉，觉即天王位，国号周——北周始。孝闵帝时年十五，初称天王而未称皇帝（仿周礼之制，宇文泰遗意）。

孝闵帝不甘为宇文护傀儡：尝与李植、孙恒等密谋诛护，事泄。同年九月，宇文护废觉为略阳公，幽于旧邸，旋弑之，年十六。觉之立、之废、之死，皆在一年之内——北周开国之主，竟为权臣所弑。

史评孝闵：「幼冲受禅，权在晋公护。」北周之制，仿《周礼》而行，天王之称、六官之设，皆宇文泰之遗策；然皇权未立而权臣已强，孝闵不过其间一过客。北周之皇权，至武帝宇文邕诛护而后复振——孝闵之死，为北周权臣专权之第一次爆发。

> 本地参考：点校本《周书》卷003《孝闵帝纪》、卷011《晋荡公护传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

Yuwen Jue was the third son of Yuwen Tai. After Tai's death his nephew Yuwen Hu took the regency; in the 3rd year of the Gong emperor of Western Wei, Hu pressed the emperor to abdicate to Jue, who took the title Heavenly King of the realm Zhou — the beginning of Northern Zhou. Xiaomin was fifteen, and bore the title of king, not yet emperor (the rite of the *Zhouli*, per Tai's design).

He would not be Hu's puppet: with Li Zhi, Sun Heng, and the others he plotted against Hu, and the plot leaked. That same ninth month Hu deposed him as Duke of Lüeyang, confined him in the old mansion, and soon slew him, aged sixteen. His enthronement, his deposition, and his death all fell within a year — the founder of Northern Zhou slain by his minister.

The histories say: "a child receiving the abdication, the power with the Duke of Jin, Hu." Northern Zhou ran on the *Zhouli* — the title of Heavenly King, the six ministries, all Tai's design; but the throne was not yet strong when the minister was, and Xiaomin was but a passing figure. The throne of Zhou recovered only when Emperor Wu slew Hu — Xiaomin's death was the first eruption of the minister's tyranny in Northern Zhou.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Zhoushu*, ch. 3 ("Benji of Emperor Xiaomin"), ch. 11 (biography of the Duke of Jin, Hu) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 北周明帝 · 主要事迹

宇文毓，宇文泰长子，孝闵帝之兄。孝闵被废，宇文护立毓，即天王位。武成元年，毓改称皇帝，建年号武成——北周之正式称帝，自明帝始。明帝「宽明仁厚，好学能诗」，史称其「善属文」，「常与群臣论诗文」，为北周诸帝中文采最盛者。

然明帝在位三年，军国大事一决于宇文护：护「性无学术，任情以逞」，明帝虽欲有为，无尺寸之权。武成二年，宇文护使人于饮食中下毒，明帝中毒而崩，年二十七；临终遗诏，以弟宇文邕继位——「帝知护将害己，遂遗诏邕即位」，北周之中兴，自此始。

史评明帝：「宽明仁厚，而见鸩于权臣。」北周开国三帝（孝闵、明帝、武帝），前二帝皆死于宇文护之手；明帝以好学能诗之君，当权臣专权之世，其死尤为可惜。其遗诏立邕，为北周选中一代英主——明帝之死，反成北周之福。

> 本地参考：点校本《周书》卷004《明帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuwen Yu, eldest son of Yuwen Tai and elder brother of Xiaomin, was set up by Yuwen Hu after Xiaomin's fall, taking the heavenly kingship. In the 1st year of Wucheng he took the title of emperor and opened the era — the formal empire of Northern Zhou begins with Ming. He was "generous, kind, learned, and a poet," "skilled in prose," often "debating verse with his ministers" — the most cultivated of the Zhou sovereigns.

But in his three years the armies and the realm were decided wholly by Hu, who "without learning, did as he pleased"; Ming, for all his wish, had not an inch of power. In the 2nd year of Wucheng, Hu had poison put in his food; Ming died of it at twenty-seven, his last will naming his brother Yong — "the emperor, knowing Hu meant to kill him, willed the throne to Yong" — and the revival of Zhou began there.

The histories say: "generous and kind, and poisoned by the strong minister." Of the first three Zhou sovereigns, two died by Yuwen Hu's hand; Ming, the poet on the captive throne, is the more to be pitied. His will chose the hero of the age — his death was, in the end, Zhou's good fortune.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Zhoushu*, ch. 4 ("Benji of Emperor Ming") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 北周武帝 · 主要事迹

宇文邕，宇文泰第四子，明帝遗诏继位。武帝即位之初，韬光养晦：宇文护专权十二年，邕「深自晦匿」，曲意事护，而其志在必诛。建德元年，邕与弟卫王直等密谋，召护入宫，于太后之前手刃之——「帝以玉珽自后击护，护踣地」，遂诛其党，亲总万机。北周皇权，至此而复。

武帝之政，以俭约、崇儒为纲：建德三年，断佛道二教，毁经像，令沙门道士还俗，「民役稍苏」——北周国力因此充实；又禁奢靡、减宫室，节俭之风，迥异南朝。建德六年，武帝亲征伐齐，克邺，俘后主高纬，北齐亡——北方自北魏分裂三十余年后，复归一统，北周疆域至此极盛。

宣政元年，武帝北伐突厥，道病，崩于云阳，年三十六。武帝「英武节俭」，为南北朝后期第一雄主；然其早崩，子宣帝荒暴，杨坚乘隙代周——北周一统北方之业，未及传世而隋代之。史评武帝：「雄略过人，统一北方」，惜乎「早崩遗祸」，隋之代周，实为北周之续。

> 本地参考：点校本《周书》卷005、006《武帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuwen Yong, fourth son of Yuwen Tai, succeeded by Ming's will. At first he hid his purpose: Yuwen Hu had ruled twelve years, and Yong "kept himself obscure," serving Hu with care while his mind was set on the killing. In the 1st year of Jiande, plotting with his brother the Prince of Wei, he summoned Hu to the palace and struck him down before the empress dowager — "the emperor struck Hu from behind with the jade tablet, and Hu fell" — destroyed his party, and took up the government himself. The throne of Zhou was restored.

His rule ran on frugality and the Confucian way: in the 3rd year of Jiande he cut off Buddhism and Daoism, destroyed the scriptures and images, and sent monks and priests back to lay life — "the people's burdens were lightened," and the state's strength grew; he forbade luxury and trimmed the palaces, a frugality far from the southern courts. In the 6th year of Jiande he campaigned in person against Qi, took Ye, and captured the Last Sovereign Gao Wei — the north, split since the division of Wei, was one again, and Zhou stood at its greatest.

In the 1st year of Xuanzheng, on the campaign against the Turks, he fell ill on the road and died at Yunyang, aged thirty-six. "Heroic and frugal," he was the first sovereign of the later northern age; but his early death left the throne to the tyrant Xuan, and Yang Jian took the realm — the unity he won passed within years to Sui. The histories say: "of surpassing strategy, he united the north," but "his early death loosed the disaster" — Sui was Zhou's continuation.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Zhoushu*, ch. 5 and 6 ("Benji of Emperor Wu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 北周宣帝 · 主要事迹

宇文赟，武帝长子。宣政元年武帝崩，赟即位。宣帝「即位之后，荒淫骄奢」，一反武帝之政：自称「天元皇帝」，以天自比，居于「天台」，臣下奏事必称「天」；又同时立四皇后，「天元大皇后」以下并立——礼制之坏，为北周之极。

宣帝刑杀无度：即位即杀叔父齐王宇文宪，又诛功臣王轨等；「每笞人以百二十为度」，刑罚酷烈。大象元年，禅位太子宇文阐，自称天元皇帝，「犹预国政」，骄奢更甚；大象二年，宣帝崩，年二十二——其暴政虽仅两载，然北周元气已伤。

宣帝崩后，幼主静帝即位，杨坚矫诏辅政，旋受禅代周——北周之亡，实亡于宣帝之暴。史评宣帝：「天元侈暴，自毁其国。」武帝一统北方之业，未及十年而付诸东流；北周之兴也勃，其亡也忽——宣帝之昏暴，为北周画上句点。

> 本地参考：点校本《周书》卷007《宣帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuwen Yun, eldest son of Emperor Wu, took the throne on his father's death in the 1st year of Xuanzheng. On the throne he "gave himself to debauchery and arrogance," reversing Wu's course: he styled himself the "Heavenly Emperor Tianyuan," comparing himself to Heaven, dwelling in the "Terrace of Heaven" where all petitions had to speak of Heaven; he set up four empresses at once, the "Heavenly Grand Empress" and the rest standing together — the rites of Zhou fell apart.

He punished and slew without measure: on accession he slew his uncle the Prince of Qi, Yuwen Xian, then the meritorious Wang Gui and the others; "he beat men to a hundred and twenty strokes," the tortures cruel. In the 1st year of Daxiang he abdicated to his heir Yuwen Chan but, styling himself the Tianyuan Emperor, "still took part in the government," more extravagant than ever; he died in the 2nd year of Daxiang at twenty-two — two years of tyranny had spent the realm.

After his death the child Jing took the throne and Yang Jian, by forged edict, the regency — and soon the abdication: Northern Zhou fell to Xuan's tyranny. The histories say: "the Tianyuan's excess destroyed his own realm." The unity won by Emperor Wu was thrown away within ten years; Zhou rose swiftly and fell swiftly, and Xuan's darkness wrote its ending.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Zhoushu*, ch. 7 ("Benji of Emperor Xuan") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 北周静帝 · 主要事迹

宇文阐，宣帝长子，初名衍。大象元年，宣帝禅位，阐即位，年七岁，杨坚（宣帝皇后之父）为左大丞相、总揽朝政。大象二年，宣帝崩，杨坚矫诏辅政，尽诛北周宗室之强藩；同年，相州总管尉迟迥、郧州司马消难等起兵讨坚，杨坚遣韦孝宽等讨平之——北周宗室之反抗，一朝而尽。

大定元年二月，杨坚受禅称帝，国号隋，北周亡。静帝禅后封介国公，五月遇害，年九岁。北周自孝闵受禅至静帝禅位，历五帝二十五年而亡；而隋之代周，实为北周之直接延续——杨坚以外戚之身，受北周之禅，其制度、疆域，皆承北周。

史评静帝：「幼冲当禅，身成隋基。」以七岁幼主，坐视祖业之移，身不由己。北周之亡，与其亡于静帝，不如亡于宣帝之暴；静帝不过承其祸而已。而隋之统一天下，则上承北周之基、下启大唐之盛——北周虽亡，其影响深远。

> 本地参考：点校本《周书》卷008《静帝纪》、隋书卷001《高祖纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yuwen Chan, eldest son of Xuan, first named Yan, took the throne in the 1st year of Daxiang at seven, with Yang Jian — father of the emperor's empress — as grand chancellor of the left, holding all the government. In the 2nd year of Daxiang Xuan died, and Jian, by forged edict, took the regency and cut down the strong princes of the Zhou house; that same year the governors Yuchi Jiong of Xiangzhou and Sima Xiaonan of Yunzhou rose against him, and Jian's generals, Wei Xiaokuan and the rest, destroyed them — the Zhou princes' resistance was spent in a day.

In the second month of the 1st year of Dading Jian received the abdication, styled the realm Sui, and Northern Zhou was no more. The former emperor, made Duke of Jie, was done to death in the fifth month, aged nine. From Xiaomin's abdication to Jing's, Zhou ran five sovereigns and twenty-five years; and Sui, taking the Zhou abdication, was its direct continuation — the institutions and the borders passed entire.

The histories say: "a child in the abdication, his life the foundation of Sui." A seven-year-old watching his grandfather's realm pass, not his own master. Zhou fell not to Jing but to Xuan's tyranny; Jing only inherited the disaster. And the Sui reunification, carrying Zhou's foundations into the age of Tang, shows how far the fallen Zhou still reached.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Zhoushu*, ch. 8 ("Benji of Emperor Jing"), and the *Suishu*, ch. 1 ("Benji of Emperor Wen") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉（前赵）高祖 · 主要事迹

刘渊字元海，新兴匈奴人，冒顿之后。幼好学，习《毛诗》《京氏易》及孙吴兵法，「猿臂善射，膂力过人」。八王之乱起，刘渊乘乱于离石起兵，称大单于，旋称汉王，建元元熙——以「汉之甥」自居，尊刘禅为孝怀皇帝，立汉高祖以下三祖五宗神主而祭之，欲争华夏正统。十六国割据，自刘渊始。

永嘉二年，渊即皇帝位，国号汉，迁都平阳，署置百官；遣刘聪、王弥等攻洛阳不克，为日后陷洛之铺垫。然匈奴汉国之制，胡汉分治、军政混行，其政权之根基未固。永嘉四年，刘渊崩，谥光文皇帝。子和继立，旋为弟聪所杀，汉国之政归于刘聪。

刘渊以匈奴之裔，乘晋室之乱而建政权，首开「五胡乱华」之局。其以绍汉为号召、行汉家礼仪，可见汉文化之浸润已深；然其政权终以武功立、以暴政传，后嗣相残、民心不附，不过二十余年而国灭。渊之起兵，非为仁政，实为野心，史家于其「聪敏好学」之外，更见胡汉冲突之始。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷101《刘元海载记》、卷102《刘聪载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Yuan, styled Yuanhai, was a Xiongnu of Xinxing, descended from Modu. Studious from youth, he mastered the Mao Odes, the Jing-school Changes, and the military art of Sun and Wu, "long of arm, a fine archer, of unusual strength." When the War of the Eight Princes broke out, he rose at Lishi, styled himself Great Chanyu, then King of Han — claiming descent through a Han princess, he honored Liu Shan as Emperor Xiaohuai and set up the ancestral tablets of the Han emperors to contest legitimacy with the Jin. The Sixteen States era begins with Liu Yuan.

In the 2nd year of Yongjia he took the imperial throne, styled the realm Han, moved his capital to Pingyang, and installed his officials; his lieutenants Liu Cong and Wang Mi attacked Luoyang without success — the prelude to its fall. But the Xiongnu Han state ran on a divided system of Hu and Han, arms and government mixed, and its foundations were never firm. In the 4th year of Yongjia Liu Yuan died, posthumously Guangwen. His son He succeeded and was at once slain by his brother Cong, and the state passed to Cong.

A Xiongnu who rode the Jin collapse to found a state, Liu Yuan opened the "Five Barbarian invasions." His claim of succession to Han and his adoption of Han rites show how deep Chinese culture had sunk into him; yet his state stood on arms and passed on tyranny — heirs murdering heirs, the people's hearts lost — and perished within a generation. His rising was ambition, not benevolence; the historians, beyond his "quickness and love of learning," see the beginning of the Hu–Han conflict.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 101 (records of Liu Yuanhai), ch. 102 (records of Liu Cong) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 汉（前赵）烈宗 · 主要事迹

刘聪字载明，刘渊第四子。永嘉四年，杀兄和自立，改元光兴。聪在位八年，武功极盛：永嘉五年，遣刘曜、王弥等破洛阳，俘晋怀帝，杀王公士民三万余人，「永嘉之乱」于此为最；建兴元年，怀帝于平阳青衣行酒，为聪所杀；建兴四年，刘曜破长安，俘愍帝，西晋亡——中国北方，自此尽入胡汉诸国之手。

然刘聪之治，暴虐失德：史载其游猎无度、后宫侈靡，「食则太官，衣则御府」，宠信靳准等佞臣；建兴末又杀愍帝于平阳，弑君之罪，无所忌惮。麟嘉三年，刘聪崩，子粲继，旋为靳准所杀，汉国分裂——刘曜于长安继位改号赵，石勒于襄国称赵王，前赵后赵并立之局始成。

刘聪以灭晋之功，居五胡君主武功之首；然「得天下不以仁义」，其暴政使匈奴汉国仅二世而衰。聪之灭晋，标志五胡十六国之局全面展开：北方自此无复统一，而南朝偏安之局，亦由此定。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷102《刘聪载记》、卷005《怀帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Cong, styled Zaiming, was the fourth son of Liu Yuan. In the 4th year of Yongjia he slew his brother He to take the throne, changing the era to Guangxing. His eight years reached the height of arms: in the 5th year of Yongjia he sent Liu Yao and Wang Mi to break Luoyang, capturing Emperor Huai and slaying over thirty thousand princes, officials, and people — the summit of the Yongjia disaster; in the 1st year of Jianxing the captive emperor, made to serve wine in servant's dress, was put to death at Pingyang; in the 4th year of Jianxing Liu Yao took Chang'an and captured Emperor Min — Western Jin was at an end, and the north had passed to the barbarian and half-barbarian states.

His rule was tyranny: the records harp on his boundless hunting and extravagant harem, his favoring of the flatterer Jin Zhun; and he put Emperor Min to death without scruple. In the 3rd year of Linjia he died; his son Can succeeded and was at once slain by Jin Zhun, and the realm split — Liu Yao took the throne at Chang'an and renamed the realm Zhao, while Shi Le styled himself King of Zhao at Xiangguo: the age of Former Zhao and Later Zhao had begun.

For destroying the Jin, Cong stands first in arms among the Five Barbarian sovereigns; but he "won the realm without benevolence," and his tyranny brought the Xiongnu Han state low within two generations. His destruction of Western Jin opened the full age of the Sixteen States: the north would know no unity, and the southern courts' long isolation was fixed.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 102 (records of Liu Cong), ch. 5 ("Benji of Emperor Huai") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 赵（前赵）主 · 主要事迹

刘曜字永明，刘渊族子。靳准之乱后，曜于长安即皇帝位，改国号赵（史称前赵），迁都长安。曜少聪慧，好读书，善属文；在位期间立太学、造浑仪、置史官，关中文化一度振兴。然其亦好杀，史载其「以赤族为戏」，关中氐羌屡叛屡平。

太宁三年，曜与后赵石勒决战洛阳城西。曜饮酒至醉，出阵不利，马陷石渠，为石勒所擒，押送襄国。石勒使曜遗书其子熙，令举国来降，曜不从，遂被杀。翌年，其子熙、胤等退守上邽，为石勒所灭，前赵亡。

刘曜勇武有余，谋略不逮石勒：定都长安而不得关东之助，胡汉离心而民心不附，终以洛阳一败而国亡身死。史家评曰：曜「少聪慧，及长雄武过人」，然「军政失道，民庶流亡」，前赵之亡，实由其失人和之故。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷103《刘曜载记》、卷104《石勒载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Yao, styled Yongming, was a cousin of Liu Yuan's line. After the Jin Zhun troubles he took the imperial throne at Chang'an, renamed the realm Zhao (Former Zhao to history), and made Chang'an his capital. Sharp from youth, fond of books and skilled in prose, he founded an academy, cast an armillary sphere, and appointed historians — Guanzhong's culture revived for a time. But he too loved killing: the records say he "made sport of destroying whole families," and the Di and Qiang of Guanzhong rose and were put down again and again.

In the 3rd year of Taining he met Shi Le of Later Zhao in battle west of Luoyang. Drunk, he rode out at disadvantage, his horse stumbled into a stone ditch, and he was taken and carried to Xiangguo. Shi Le made him write to his son Xi, ordering the realm to surrender; Yao refused, and was put to death. The next year his sons Xi and Yin fell back to Shanggui and were destroyed by Shi Le — Former Zhao was no more.

Yao's courage exceeded his counsel, which fell short of Shi Le's: he fixed his capital at Chang'an without the support of the east, the Hu and the Han were estranged, and the people's hearts were not with him — one defeat at Luoyang ended the state and the man. The historians say he was "sharp from youth and of more than common courage when grown," but "government lost the way and the people scattered": Former Zhao fell for want of men's hearts.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 103 (records of Liu Yao), ch. 104 (records of Shi Le) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后赵高祖 · 主要事迹

石勒是羯人，少时约当西晋永兴前后被掠卖为奴，后来聚众起兵，最终登上帝位——从奴隶到天子的跨度，使他成为十六国史里最戏剧性的创业者。本页以《晋书》卷一百四至一百五石勒载记为年表主线，辅以《资治通鉴》编年（本地参考库已备）。

创业之初，他一度归入刘渊、刘聪的汉赵系统，借汉赵旗帜在华北作战中积累实力。永嘉五年（311）洛阳陷落前后，他参与永嘉之乱后的华北混战，军势迅速坐大，成为割据一方的主力。

太兴二年（319），石勒称赵王、都襄国，正式脱离前赵阴影，后赵政权由此成立；两年后进称大单于，名号与制度同步升格。咸和三年至四年（328–329），他与前赵末主刘曜在洛阳一线决战，破刘曜、灭前赵，北方大部归入后赵版图。咸和五年（330），他在襄国称皇帝，帝制完备，完成了从奴隶到天子的全过程。

石勒并非只有武功。他以张宾为谋主，兴学校、定制度，设君子营安置士人，在胡汉分治的框架下做秩序建设的探索。需要注意，史籍中后赵的残暴记载多须区分石勒本人与其后继者石虎；对石勒本人，史家仍称其雄略。

咸和八年（333），石勒崩于襄国。他生前安排的继承人石弘旋即为石虎所夺，后赵政治迅速恶化，国祚不长。与[[q-qin-fu-jian|前秦苻坚]]对读：同为十六国胡人政权的立国或中兴之主，一前一后，可见那个时代创业与治乱的不同路径。

bio_parts_en.value:
Shi Le was a Jie. In his youth, around the Yongxing era of the Western Jin, he was kidnapped and sold into slavery; he later gathered a following, rose in arms, and finally ascended the imperial throne — the span from slave to Son of Heaven makes him the most dramatic state-founder in the history of the Sixteen Kingdoms. This page takes the Shi Le annals in juan 104–105 of the 《晋书》 as its chronological backbone, supplemented by the chronicle of the 《资治通鉴》 (available in the local reference library).

At the start of his enterprise he attached himself for a time to the Han-Zhao system of Liu Yuan and Liu Cong, building strength through campaigns in north China under the Han-Zhao banner. Around the fall of Luoyang in Yongjia 5 (311), he joined the melee that followed the Yongjia upheaval in north China; his military power swelled rapidly, making him a leading force among the regional powers.

In Taixing 2 (319) Shi Le took the title King of Zhao and made Xiangguo his capital, formally stepping out of Former Zhao's shadow — the Later Zhao regime was thereby founded; two years later he advanced to Great Chanyu, his titles and institutions rising in step. In Xianhe 3–4 (328–329) he fought the decisive battle along the Luoyang line against Liu Yao, the last ruler of Former Zhao: he defeated Liu Yao, destroyed Former Zhao, and most of the north entered the Later Zhao map. In Xianhe 5 (330) he proclaimed himself emperor at Xiangguo, completing the imperial system — and with it the entire passage from slave to Son of Heaven.

Shi Le was not a man of martial feats alone. He made Zhang Bin his chief strategist, promoted schools and fixed institutions, established the Gentlemen's Camp to house men of letters, and explored the building of order within the framework of Hu-Han dual rule. One caveat: the records of Later Zhao cruelty in the histories must often be divided between Shi Le himself and his successor Shi Hu; of Shi Le himself, historians still speak of his boldness of design.

In Xianhe 8 (333) Shi Le died at Xiangguo. Shi Hong, the heir he had arranged, was at once dispossessed by Shi Hu; Later Zhao politics deteriorated quickly, and the dynastic line did not last long. Read him against
: both were founders or restorers of Hu states in the Sixteen Kingdoms period, one earlier and one later, and together they show the era's different paths of state-building and of order and collapse.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后赵武帝 · 主要事迹

石虎字季龙，石勒之侄。骁勇善战，为石勒方面大将，攻城略地，多出其力。咸和八年石勒崩，虎受遗辅石弘，旋专权；咸和九年，废杀石弘自立，称居摄赵天王，后称帝。石虎迁都于邺，大营宫殿苑囿，「发民夫四十余万」筑华林苑、猎场，又括民女充后宫，史称百姓愁怨。

石虎之暴，为十六国君主之最：役民无度，杀人如麻，「既而自以无子，复立其幼子」，诸子争立，骨肉相残；又发兵攻前燕、前凉，武功虽盛，而民力已竭。永和五年，石虎崩，诸子为争帝位自相残杀，石闵（冉闵）乘乱起兵，杀胡人二十余万，后赵迅即崩溃——其盛也暴，其亡也速。

史家论石虎：「季龙以凶戾之资，奋残暴之性，虽复冠带蛮貊，终为豺狼之德。」后赵之武功，尽丧于暴政；其「胡汉相杀」之祸，更为五胡之乱中最惨烈者。虎之兴亡，足为暴政亡国之鉴。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷106《石季龙载记》、卷107《石闵载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Shi Hu, styled Jilong, was the nephew of Shi Le, a fierce warrior who took cities for his uncle as one of his field commanders. In the 8th year of Xianhe Le died; Hu, by the late will, assisted Shi Hong — and at once seized power. In the 9th year he deposed and slew Hong and stood himself, calling himself Heavenly King of Zhao Regent, later emperor. He moved the capital to Ye, raised palaces and parks on a grand scale, and "drove over 400,000 laborers" to build the Huayuan park and hunting grounds; he swept the realm's women into his harem — the records say the people grieved and raged.

His tyranny was the worst of the Sixteen States: corvée without limit, slaughter without mercy; and with his sons contending, kin slew kin. He campaigned against Former Yan and Former Liang, his arms at their height while the people's strength ran out. In the 5th year of Yonghe he died; his sons fought for the throne, and Shi Min (Ran Min) rose in the chaos and slew over 200,000 Hu — Later Zhao collapsed at once. It rose in tyranny and fell in a moment.

The historians say of him: "With a savage nature and a brutal temper, though he put on the robes of civilization, his virtue was the wolf's." The realm's strength was spent in cruelty; and the Hu–Han slaughter of his fall was the bitterest of the barbarian age. His rise and ruin stand as the warning of tyranny.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 106 (records of Shi Jilong), ch. 107 (records of Shi Min) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 成汉太宗 · 主要事迹

李雄字仲俊，巴氐流民首领李特之子。太安二年，李特与益州刺史罗尚相攻，兵败被杀；雄继统部众，与罗尚等相持。建兴元年，雄称成都王，建元；晏平元年，即皇帝位，国号大成，都成都。成汉遂与中原诸国并立，为十六国中偏安巴蜀者。

李雄在位三十年，史称其「宽政安蜀」：轻徭薄赋，刑狱宽简，「赋役俱省，民庶丰溢」，蜀人安之。雄无子，养兄李荡之子班为太子；玉衡二十四年，雄崩，兄子班继位。然李雄诸子不服，李期等发动政变杀班自立，成汉自此中衰——雄之宽政，未能传之后嗣。

史家评李雄：「雄以宽仁之量，抚流移之民，故能据有巴蜀，垂三十年。」在十六国暴君辈出之际，李雄之治实属难得；然传位不明、诸子争立，其宽政终成昙花一现。成汉后为东晋桓温所灭，偏安之局遂终。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷121《李雄载记》、卷120《李特载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Xiong, styled Zhongjun, was the son of Li Te, leader of the Ba-Di refugee host. In the 2nd year of Tai'an, Li Te, fighting the Yi Province governor Luo Shang, was defeated and slain; Xiong took command and held off Luo Shang. In the 1st year of Jianxing he styled himself King of Chengdu and opened an era; in the 1st year of Yanping he took the imperial throne, styling the realm Dacheng with its capital at Chengdu. Cheng Han stood beside the states of the Central Plains — the one of the Sixteen that held Bashu alone.

In thirty years Xiong's rule was the most benign of the age: light levies, easy justice, "tax and corvée both spared, the people prosperous," and the people of Shu at peace. He had no son and raised his nephew Ban as heir; when he died in the 24th year of Yuheng and Ban succeeded, Xiong's own sons would not bear it — Li Qi and the others murdered Ban, and Cheng Han began its decline. His benevolence could not bequeath itself.

The historians say: "With a measure of benevolence Xiong nourished the refugees, and so held Bashu for nearly thirty years." Amid the tyrants of the Sixteen States his rule stands out; but the succession was unsecured and his sons tore the state — the good rule was a brief spring. Huan Wen of Eastern Jin later destroyed Cheng Han, and the enclave ended.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 121 (records of Li Xiong), ch. 120 (records of Li Te) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前燕文明帝 · 主要事迹

慕容皝字元真，鲜卑慕容部首领慕容廆之子。咸和八年廆死，皝嗣辽东公，讨平其兄翰等之乱；咸康三年，自称燕王——前燕王政自此始。皝建元、置僚属，筑龙城而都之，开拓辽西；又破宇文部、击段部，辽东霸权遂固。

皝之治，兼用胡汉：以汉族士人裴嶷、封奕等为谋主，劝农桑、立学校，「览政之暇，亲临东庠考试学生」；军事上则倚其弟慕容翰、慕容恪等名将。慕容部之崛起，自皝而兴。永和四年，皝崩，谥文明皇帝，子儁继位。

慕容皝以辽东一隅，经营前燕基业，「威德兼举，士庶归心」；其子慕容儁灭冉魏、入中原，其孙慕容暐时前燕全盛——皆皝奠基之功。然皝猜忌兄弟，逼走慕容翰，晚年兄弟相攻之祸已伏；燕之兴也勃，其亡也忽，内乱之根，盖植于此。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷109《慕容皝载记》、卷110《慕容儁载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Murong Huang, styled Yuanzhen, was the son of Murong Hui, chief of the Murong Xianbei. In the 8th year of Xianhe Hui died; Huang succeeded as Duke of Liaodong and put down the rising of his brothers; in the 3rd year of Xiankang he styled himself King of Yan — the kingship of Former Yan began. He opened an era, installed officers, built Longcheng as his capital, opened up Liaoxi, broke the Yuwen tribe and struck the Duan, and his hegemony of Liaodong was fixed.

He ruled with both Hu and Han: the Han gentry Pei Ni, Feng Yi, and the rest were his counselors; he encouraged farming and mulberries, founded schools, and "in his leisure from government examined the students in person"; in arms he leaned on his brothers Murong Han and Murong Ke, generals of the first rank. The rise of the Murong house began with Huang. He died in the 4th year of Yonghe, posthumously Emperor Wenming, and his son Jun succeeded.

From one corner of Liaodong Huang built the foundations of Former Yan, "his authority and virtue together drawing the gentry and the people." His son Jun destroyed Ran Wei and entered the Central Plains; his grandson Wei reigned at the height of Former Yan — the work of Huang's founding. But he distrusted his brothers, driving Murong Han away, and the seed of the house's internal wars was sown here: Former Yan rose swiftly and fell swiftly, and the root of the ruin lay in the founder.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 109 (records of Murong Huang), ch. 110 (records of Murong Jun) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前燕景昭帝 · 主要事迹

慕容儁字宣英，慕容皝次子。永和四年皝崩，儁嗣燕王。永和六年，乘后赵石虎之死、中原大乱，儁遣慕容恪、慕容评等南下争河北，取蓟城、克中山；永和八年，俘杀冉闵，遂即皇帝位，国号燕——前燕入主中原，与东晋、前秦鼎足而三。

儁迁都邺，据石氏故都，「宫室制度，皆仿洛阳」；又令州郡核实户口，劝课农桑。前燕全盛时，「南至汝颍，东尽青齐，西抵崤渑」，为十六国中之强者。然儁在位后期，好大喜功：欲发兵百万攻东晋、前秦，与东晋争正统；又猜忌其弟慕容垂。光寿四年，儁崩，子暐年仅十一继位，慕容恪辅政。

慕容儁以灭冉魏之功入主中原，前燕之盛极于此；然其穷兵黩武、猜忌宗室，为前燕中衰埋下伏线。史家评曰：儁「雄毅多权略」，然「以武立国，不修文德」，其兴也勃焉，其亡也忽焉。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷110《慕容儁载记》、卷111《慕容暐载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Murong Jun, styled Xuan Ying, was the second son of Murong Huang. On his father's death in the 4th year of Yonghe he succeeded as King of Yan. In the 6th year, riding the chaos after Shi Hu's death, he sent Murong Ke, Murong Ping, and the others south into Hebei, taking Ji and Zhongshan; in the 8th year he captured and slew Ran Min and took the imperial throne, styling the realm Yan — Former Yan entered the Central Plains, standing with Eastern Jin and Former Qin as the third of the age.

He moved the capital to Ye, the old seat of the Shi house, "his palaces and institutions modeled on Luoyang," and ordered the provinces to verify the household registers and encourage farming. At its height Former Yan "reached the Ru and Ying in the south, Qing and Qi in the east, and the Xiao and Mian in the west" — among the strongest of the Sixteen States. But in his later years he grew vainglorious: he would raise a million men against Jin and Qin to contest legitimacy, and he distrusted his brother Murong Chui. He died in the 4th year of Guangshou; his son Wei, eleven, succeeded under Murong Ke's regency.

For destroying Ran Wei and entering the Central Plains, Jun brought Former Yan to its height; but his endless wars and his suspicion of his own kin laid the fuse of its decline. The historians say he was "bold and full of stratagems," yet "a realm won by arms, not adorned by virtue — it rose swiftly and fell swiftly."

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 110 (records of Murong Jun), ch. 111 (records of Murong Wei) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前秦高祖 · 主要事迹

苻健字建业，略阳氐人，苻洪第三子。苻洪为后赵所害，健统其众。永和六年，健率众自枋头入关，击破杜洪，据长安；皇始元年，自称天王、大单于，国号大秦，都长安；皇始二年，即皇帝位。前秦立国之基，自苻健始。

皇始中，东晋桓温北伐，入关至霸上，关中震恐。苻健坚壁清野，尽收其麦，温军粮尽而退——「健以逸待劳」，遂保关中。苻健在位五年，抚流民、劝农桑、置百官，「虽戎狄之俗，渐染华风」。皇始五年，健崩，谥景明皇帝。其子苻生继位，残暴无道，旋为侄苻坚所杀——前秦之大业，终落于苻坚之手。

苻健以氐族之身，乘乱据关中，为前秦开创基业；其拒桓温之役，尤见将略。然健虽开基，未及大治，子生之暴、侄坚之兴，皆其身后之事。前秦自苻坚始成为十六国最强者，然其根柢，实植于苻健之世。

bio_parts_en.value:
Fu Jian, styled Jianye, was a Di of Lüeyang, third son of Fu Hong. When Fu Hong was done to death by Later Zhao, Jian took command of his host. In the 6th year of Yonghe he led his men through the pass, broke Du Hong, and took Chang'an; in the 1st year of Huangshi he styled himself Heavenly King and Great Chanyu of the realm Great Qin with his capital at Chang'an; in the 2nd year he took the imperial throne. The foundations of Former Qin were laid by Jian.

In mid-Huangshi, Huan Wen of Eastern Jin campaigned north and entered the pass, reaching Bashan, and Guanzhong was shaken. Jian cleared the land of its grain and held his walls; Wen's army ran out of food and withdrew — "Jian, at ease, wore the invader out," and Guanzhong was saved. In five years he gathered the refugees, encouraged farming, and installed his officials, "the barbarian custom gradually taking on Chinese ways." He died in the 5th year of Huangshi, posthumously Emperor Jingming. His son Sheng succeeded, a cruel tyrant, and was soon slain by his nephew Fu Jian — the great enterprise of Former Qin passed to the nephew.

A Di who seized Guanzhong in the chaos and founded Former Qin, Jian showed real generalship in denying Huan Wen. He founded the state but did not live to perfect it; the tyrant Sheng and the rise of Fu Jian were the work of his successors. Former Qin became the strongest of the Sixteen States under Fu Jian — but its roots were planted in Jian's reign.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 112 (records of Fu Jian), ch. 113 (records of Fu Jian the Great Ancestor) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前秦世祖 · 主要事迹

苻坚（357—385 在位）是十六国时期最接近统一天下的前秦君主。永兴元年（357）他诛暴主苻生，即天王位，改元永兴，前秦由此进入苻坚时代。本页以《晋书·苻坚载记》（卷113–114）为年表主线，辅以《资治通鉴·晋纪》编年对照。

即位之后，他把国政委于王猛。王猛整肃吏治、打击贵戚，前秦国力急升，构成苻坚一朝的文治底色。武功随之而起：太和五年（370）王猛克邺，前燕遂灭，北方统一进程加速；太元元年（376）再灭前凉，兼及代地，河西归于前秦，北方大体统一，版图臻于巅峰。

巅峰之后是急转。太元七年（382）朝议伐晋，其时王猛已卒，谏阻无力；次年苻坚决意南伐，史载有「投鞭于江，足断其流」一类豪语，倾国出兵。太元八年（383）淝水一战大败于东晋谢安、谢玄一系，前秦由此崩解，各族复起。需要说明的是，「投鞭断流」语出记载的文学性颇浓，但南伐的战略责任归于苻坚本人，这一点仍成立。

太元九年（384）慕容垂独立，燕秦瓦解；次年苻坚西奔五将山一带，为姚苌所害，前秦迅速瓦解。读苻坚，可与[[n-wei-taiwu|太武帝]]对读：两者皆以武力整合北方，一败于南征而国解，一再合北方而开启北朝，可见十六国北朝兴亡的节奏。

bio_parts_en.value:
Fu Jian (r. 357–385) was the Former Qin ruler who came closest to unifying all under Heaven in the Sixteen Kingdoms period. In Yongxing 1 (357) he executed the tyrannical ruler Fu Sheng, took the title Heavenly King, and changed the era name to Yongxing; Former Qin thereby entered the age of Fu Jian. This page takes the 《晋书·苻坚载记》 (juan 113–114) as its chronological backbone, checked against the chronicle of the 《资治通鉴·晋纪》.

After his enthronement he entrusted the affairs of state to Wang Meng. Wang Meng disciplined the bureaucracy and struck at powerful kinsmen; Former Qin's strength surged, forming the civil-government foundation of Fu Jian's reign. Military achievement followed: in Taihe 5 (370) Wang Meng took Ye, Former Yan was destroyed, and the unification of the north accelerated; in Taiyuan 1 (376) he further destroyed Former Liang, reaching as far as the land of Dai; Hexi fell to Former Qin, the north was largely unified, and the map reached its peak.

After the peak came the sharp turn. In Taiyuan 7 (382) the court debated attacking Jin; Wang Meng was already dead, and remonstrance carried no force. The next year Fu Jian resolved on the southern campaign — the histories record boasts of the sort "throw our whips into the river and they would dam its flow" — and mobilized the entire state. In Taiyuan 8 (383), at the single battle of the Fei River, he was crushingly defeated by the Eastern Jin line of Xie An and Xie Xuan; Former Qin disintegrated and the various peoples rose again. It should be noted that the phrase "whips damming the river" carries a strong literary coloring in the sources, but strategic responsibility for the southern campaign rests with Fu Jian himself — that point still stands.

In Taiyuan 9 (384) Murong Chui declared independence and the Yan-Qin order collapsed; the next year Fu Jian fled west to the Wujiangshan area, where he was killed by Yao Chang, and Former Qin rapidly fell apart. Reading Fu Jian, one may set him against

: both integrated the north by force; one broke on a southern campaign and lost his state, the other re-unified the north and opened the Northern Dynasties — together they show the rhythm of rise and fall across the Sixteen Kingdoms and Northern Dynasties.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后秦太祖 · 主要事迹

姚苌字景茂，南安赤亭羌人，姚弋仲第二十四子。淝水之战后，前秦土崩，姚苌于白雀元年叛苻坚自立，称万年秦王于北地——后秦始。白雀二年，姚苌围新平，苻坚走五将山，为苌所擒，缢杀之——一代雄主苻坚，竟死于其臣之刃。

建初元年，姚苌即皇帝位于长安，国号大秦。后秦立国之初，关中群雄并起：苻登据陇东，与前秦残部相攻，姚苌与苻登战于安定、新平间，久而不决；又讨平关中各郡。建初八年，姚苌病笃，苻登攻之益急，苌欲遁，为众所止，卒于长安，谥武昭皇帝。

姚苌以羌族之身，乘乱而起，弑苻坚而开基立国，史家谓之「枭雄」；然其弑主之罪、猜忌之性，使其形象在十六国君主中尤为负面。后秦之兴，兴于姚苌之谋；后秦之德，失于姚苌之弑——其子姚兴崇文兴佛，庶几补救，然终不能洗其父之污名。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷116《姚苌载记》、卷114《苻坚载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yao Chang, styled Jingmao, was a Qiang of Chiting in Nan'an, twenty-fourth son of Yao Yizhong. After the Fei River defeat, as Former Qin crumbled, Chang turned against Fu Jian in the 1st year of Baique and styled himself King of Wannian Qin in Beidi — the beginning of Later Qin. In the 2nd year of Baique he besieged Xinping; Fu Jian, fled to Mount Wujiang, was seized and strangled — the great hero of Former Qin died by his own minister's hand.

In the 1st year of Jianchu Chang took the imperial throne at Chang'an, styling the realm Great Qin. The founding years were hard: Fu Deng held the Longdong with the remnants of Former Qin, and Chang fought him between Anding and Xinping for years without decision; the commanderies of Guanzhong rose and were put down. In the 8th year of Jianchu, gravely ill with Fu Deng pressing, he wished to flee; his men would not let him, and he died at Chang'an, posthumously Emperor Wuzhao.

A Qiang who rose with the times, slew Fu Jian, and founded a realm — the historians call him an adventurer; his slaying of his lord and his jealousy blacken his name among the Sixteen States' sovereigns. Later Qin rose by Chang's cunning and lost its virtue by his crime; his son Yao Xing's patronage of learning and Buddhism partly repaired the name, but could not wash it clean.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 116 (records of Yao Chang), ch. 114 (records of Fu Jian) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

His succession was ill-managed, and he died in the 1st year of Yonghe.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后秦高祖 · 主要事迹

姚兴字子略，姚苌长子。建初八年苌崩，兴即位于长安。姚兴在位二十二年，为后秦全盛之期：皇初年间，兴破苻登，灭前秦残部，基本统一关陇——「陇右休屠、匈奴等皆降附」；又取洛阳，据有河东。后秦疆域，西至河西，东达洛阳，为十六国后期之强者。

姚兴之治，崇文尚佛：弘始三年，迎鸠摩罗什入长安，译经讲法，僧徒云集，「远近诸方，莫不归仰」，长安遂为佛教译经中心；又立律学于长安，召郡国生徒数百人受业，考其优劣；听政之暇，亲讲佛经。姚兴之世，后秦文化之盛，为十六国所仅见。

然姚兴晚年，立嗣不明：太子泓与弟弼相争，兴「以药疾」，诸子相攻，后秦元气大伤。永和元年，姚兴崩；永和十三年，后秦为东晋刘裕所灭。史家评姚兴：「留心政事，包容荒诞，虽政刑未理，而风教可观。」其文治在十六国君主中首屈一指，惜其武功不逮前代。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷117《姚兴载记》、卷118《姚泓载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yao Xing, styled Zilue, was the eldest son of Yao Chang. On his father's death in the 8th year of Jianchu he took the throne at Chang'an. His twenty-two years were the height of Later Qin: in the early Huangchu years he broke Fu Deng, destroyed the remnants of Former Qin, and roughly united Guanzhong and Longxi — "the Xiongnu of the Longyou submitted" — and he took Luoyang and held Hedong. The realm stretched from Hexi in the west to Luoyang in the east, one of the strong states of the later Sixteen.

His rule favored letters and Buddhism: in the 3rd year of Hongshi he brought Kumarajiva to Chang'an, where the master translated the scriptures before throngs of monks — "all quarters looked up to him" — and Chang'an became the center of scripture translation; he founded a law academy, summoned hundreds of students from the provinces to study and examined their merits; in his leisure from government he lectured on the sutras himself. The culture of his court was unique among the Sixteen States.

But his succession was ill-managed: the heir Hong and his brother Bi contended, and while Xing lay ill his sons fought, and the state's strength ebbed. He died in the 1st year of Yonghe; in the 13th, Liu Yu of Eastern Jin destroyed Later Qin. The historians credit him with "care for government" and note "though law and punishment were imperfect, manners and teaching were admirable": in civil rule he stands first among the Sixteen States' sovereigns, but in arms he fell short of his father.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 117 (records of Yao Xing), ch. 118 (records of Yao Hong) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后燕成武帝 · 主要事迹

慕容垂字道明，慕容皝第五子。十三岁随父征伐，「勇冠三军」，为前燕名将；枋头之战，大破桓温，威震中原。然为慕容评所忌，前燕亡后奔秦，仕苻坚。淝水之战，垂军独全，坚败后护之还洛阳——然其异志已萌。

燕元元年，垂叛秦，称燕王于荥阳，后燕始。建兴元年，即皇帝位于中山。垂复国后，先后讨平翟魏、西燕，又大破东晋桓冲；建兴十年，太子宝伐北魏，大败于参合陂，死者数万——垂之霸业，于此受挫。建兴十一年，垂亲征北魏，欲报参合陂之仇，行至上谷祖阳，病笃而崩，年七十一。

慕容垂一生，为将则名冠当世，为君则开国复燕；然「参合陂之败，虽非亲征，实丧其锐」——垂之死，后燕中衰，数年后即为北魏所灭。史家评垂：「少岐嶷有器度，身长七尺七寸，手垂过膝」，然「仁而不武，未能剪灭群雄」；其以旧将复国，终因后嗣不肖、强敌环伺而功败垂成。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷123《慕容垂载记》、卷124《慕容宝载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Murong Chui, styled Daoming, was the fifth son of Murong Huang. He followed his father's campaigns from thirteen, "first in valor of the whole army," the great general of Former Yan; at Fangtou he shattered Huan Wen, and his name ran through the Central Plains. But Murong Ping's jealousy drove him out; when Former Yan fell he took refuge with Fu Jian of Qin. At the Fei River, his was the one army left whole; he escorted the defeated Fu Jian back to Luoyang — but his designs were already formed.

In the 1st year of Yanyuan he turned on Qin, styled himself King of Yan at Xingyang, and Later Yan began. In the 1st year of Jianxing he took the imperial throne at Zhongshan. His restoration swept away the Zhai-Wei and Western Yan, and he broke Huan Chong of Eastern Jin; in the 10th year of Jianxing his heir Bao campaigned against Northern Wei and was shattered at the Canhe marshes, tens of thousands dead — the hinge of his fortunes. In the 11th year, campaigning in person to avenge the marshes, he fell ill at Zuyang in Shanggu and died, aged seventy-one.

As a general he was without equal in his age; as a sovereign he restored the Yan line. But "the Canhe disaster, though not his own campaign, broke his edge" — with his death Later Yan declined, and within years Wei destroyed it. The historians say he was "marked from youth for greatness, seven feet seven tall, his hands hanging past his knees," yet "benevolent without being martial, unable to cut down the heroes of the age": a veteran who rebuilt a state, only to see his heirs and his enemies undo it.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 123 (records of Murong Chui), ch. 124 (records of Murong Bao) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 西秦烈祖 · 主要事迹

乞伏国仁，陇西鲜卑乞伏部首领。淝水之战后，前秦瓦解，国仁于建义元年据苑川，称大单于，西秦始。国仁在位四年，讨破邻近鲜卑诸部如鲜卑匹兰、密贵等，拓地至金城；又与关陇诸政权周旋，受前秦苻登之官爵，为苑川王。

建义四年，国仁崩，其弟乾归继位，西秦延续。乾归时西秦略有规模，然其地狭力弱，与后秦、南凉、北凉相攻伐；西秦虽历国仁、乾归、炽磐三代，始终局促于陇西一隅，后为夏国所灭。

史家评国仁：草创开国，享国短促。西秦在十六国中为最弱小者之一，其兴也倚于前秦之崩，其亡也因于群雄之逼；乞伏氏以陇西鲜卑之部，割据数十年，可谓乱世自存之难。国仁之名，不过十六国风云中之一瞬。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷125《乞伏国仁载记》、卷125《乞伏乾归载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Qifu Guoren was the chief of the Qifu Xianbei of Longxi. After the Fei River defeat, with Former Qin dissolving, he held Yuanchuan in the 1st year of Jianyi and styled himself Great Chanyu — the beginning of Western Qin. In his four years he broke the neighboring Xianbei tribes, the Pilan and the Migu and the rest, extending his lands to Jincheng; he dealt with the powers of Guanzhong and Longxi, accepting from Fu Deng the titles of King of Yuanchuan and more.

He died in the 4th year of Jianyi, his brother Gangui carrying on Western Qin. Under Gangui and then Qifu Chipan the state had some measure of size, but it was ever cramped in one corner of Longxi, fighting Later Qin, Southern Liang, and Northern Liang, and was finally destroyed by the Xia state.

The historians judge him: a rough founding, and the realm's years were few. Western Qin was among the weakest of the Sixteen States; it rose on Former Qin's ruin and fell before the stronger powers — the difficulty of a single Xianbei tribe holding its own through decades of chaos. Guoren's name is but a moment in the storm.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 125 (records of Qifu Guoren), ch. 125 (records of Qifu Gangui) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后凉懿武帝 · 主要事迹

吕光字世明，略阳氐人，苻坚大将。建元十九年，奉苻坚命征西域：率步骑七万，越流沙，破焉耆、龟兹，「诸国皆降」，得鸠摩罗什以归。太安元年，光东还，闻苻坚为姚苌所杀，遂据姑臧自立，称凉州牧；龙飞元年，称三河王，后称天王——后凉始立。

吕光以武功据河西，然其治国无方：任子为将，诸子相攻；猜忌宗室，杀戮无辜。其晚年，秃发乌孤、沮渠蒙逊、段业等相继叛之，后凉之地四分五裂。承康元年，吕光崩，诸子争立，后凉遂衰，数年后为后秦所灭。

史家评吕光：「少沈毅，有器度」，然「性多猜忌，不任其下」。吕光以西征之功、据凉州之地，本可成一方之业；然其以武夫之资治国，无怀柔之量，河西诸部离心，终致后凉速亡。其征西域之功，为十六国君主所仅见，然武功之盛，不救治国之败。

bio_parts_en.value:
Lü Guang, styled Shiming, was a Di of Lüeyang and a general of Fu Jian. In the 19th year of Jianyuan, by Fu Jian's order, he campaigned in the Western Regions: with seventy thousand horse and foot he crossed the drifting sands, broke Karashahr and Kucha, "the kingdoms all submitting," and brought back Kumarajiva. In the 1st year of Tai'an, returning east on word that Yao Chang had slain Fu Jian, he held Guzang and stood alone, styling himself Governor of Liangzhou; in the 1st year of Longfei he took the title King of the Three Rivers, later Heavenly King — the beginning of Later Liang.

Guanzheng he was strong; governing he was without art: he made generals of his sons, and the sons fought; he distrusted his kin and slew them. In his old age Tufa Wugu, Juqu Mengxun, Duan Ye, and the others rose against him one after another, and his realm was torn into four. He died in the 1st year of Chengkang; his sons contended, Later Liang decayed, and within years Later Qin took it.

The historians say he was "resolute from youth and of real bearing," yet "jealous by nature, untrusting of his subordinates." With the glory of the western campaign and the possession of Liangzhou he might have built a lasting state; but he ruled as a soldier, without the arts of conciliation, the peoples of Hexi fell away, and Later Liang passed swiftly. His western conquest stands alone among the Sixteen States' sovereigns; but the glory of arms did not cure the failure of government.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 122 (records of Lü Guang), ch. 125 (records of Tufa Wugu) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 南凉武王 · 主要事迹

秃发乌孤，河西鲜卑秃发部首领。太初元年，叛后凉吕光，自称西平王，筑廉川堡为都，据湟中——南凉始。乌孤「雄勇有大志」，太初二年，拓地至广武、湟河，改称武威王；又用汉族士人史嵩等，谋据河西。

太初三年，乌孤酒醉，坠马伤胁，寻崩，年约四十。其弟利鹿孤、傉檀相继继位，南凉时盛时衰：利鹿孤徙都西平，傉檀徙都乐都，与后秦、北凉、西秦相攻伐。然南凉地狭民寡，终为西秦所灭。

史家评乌孤：「草创南凉，享国不永。」乌孤以河西鲜卑之部，乘后凉之衰而自立，其兴也速；然其酒祸丧身，后嗣之业不昌。秃发与拓跋同源之传说，见载记之序——其族之命运，竟与拓跋氏一盛一衰，相映成趣。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷126《秃发乌孤载记》、卷126《秃发傉檀载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Tufa Wugu was the chief of the Tufa Xianbei of Hexi. In the 1st year of Taichu he turned against Lü Guang of Later Liang, styled himself King of Xiping, and built the fort of Lianchuan as his capital, holding the Huangzhong — the beginning of Southern Liang. "Bold and great of purpose," he extended his lands to Guangwu and Huanghe in the 2nd year and took the title King of Wuwei; he drew in the Han gentry, Shi Song and the rest, and planned to hold Hexi.

In the 3rd year of Taichu, drunk, he fell from his horse, hurt his ribs, and died, around forty. His brothers Lilugu and then Nutan succeeded, and Southern Liang rose and fell by turns — Lilugu moving the capital to Xiping, Nutan to Ledu, fighting Later Qin, Northern Liang, and Western Qin. Cramped and poor in men, it was finally destroyed by Western Qin.

The historians judge Wugu: "a rough founding of Southern Liang, and the realm's years were few." A Hexi Xianbei tribe seizing its chance on Later Liang's decline, it rose swiftly; his death by drink left the succession weak. The records' preface notes the legend that the Tufa and the Tuoba share a common origin — the fate of the one house rising while the other fell is a mirror of the age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 126 (records of Tufa Wugu), ch. 126 (records of Tufa Nutan) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 北凉武宣王 · 主要事迹

沮渠蒙逊，临松卢水胡人，「博涉群史，颇晓天文」。龙飞二年，与兄男成等拥立段业为凉州牧，反后凉；永安元年，蒙逊杀段业自立，称凉州牧、张掖公——北凉实始。蒙逊旋迁都姑臧，称河西王，据有河西走廊之大部分。

蒙逊之业，以灭西凉为高峰：玄始十年，率军破敦煌，西凉李歆战死，李氏西凉亡，河西遂为一统。北凉全盛时，「东据金城，西控敦煌」，与北魏、南朝宋通使往来，又迎昙无谶译经，佛教大兴。义和三年，蒙逊崩，其子牧犍继位；承平七年，北魏太武帝亲征，牧犍出降，北凉亡——五凉之局，至此而终。

史家评蒙逊：「性雄杰，有勇略，善权变。」其以胡人之身，弑主自立，权变有余而信义不足；然其经营河西三十余年，保境安民、兴文倡佛，为五凉诸国中命祚最长者。北凉之亡，亦标志五胡十六国之局渐入尾声。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷129《沮渠蒙逊载记》、卷099《沮渠牧犍传》及《魏书·沮渠蒙逊传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Juqu Mengxun was a Lushui Hu of Linsong, "learned in the histories and versed in astronomy." In the 2nd year of Longfei, with his brother Nancheng, he pushed Duan Ye to the governorship of Liangzhou against Later Liang; in the 1st year of Yong'an he slew Duan Ye and stood himself, styling himself Governor of Liangzhou and Duke of Zhangye — the real beginning of Northern Liang. He moved the capital to Guzang, took the title King of Hexi, and held most of the Hexi corridor.

His crowning deed was the destruction of Western Liang: in the 10th year of Xuanshi he broke Dunhuang, Li Xin fell in battle, and the Li house's Western Liang perished — Hexi was one. At its height Northern Liang "held Jincheng in the east and Dunhuang in the west," sent envoys to Northern Wei and to the Song court of the south, and welcomed the translator Tan Wuchen, so that Buddhism flourished. He died in the 3rd year of Yihe; his son Mujian succeeded, and in the 7th year of Chengping Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei campaigned in person, Mujian surrendered, and Northern Liang was no more — the five Liangs ended.

The historians say of him: "bold of nature, of real courage, skilled in shifts." A Hu who slew his lord to take power, he had cunning in plenty and faith in little; yet he held Hexi more than thirty years, kept his borders and his people, and furthered letters and the faith — the longest-lived of the Five Liang states. Its fall also sounded the end of the Sixteen States age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 129 (records of Juqu Mengxun), and the *Weishu*, biography of Juqu Mengxun (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 西凉太祖 · 主要事迹

李暠字玄盛，陇西成纪人，自称西汉李广之后。「少而好学，通涉经史」，为北凉段业之敦煌太守。庚子元年，据敦煌自立，称凉公，改元庚子——西凉始。建初元年，迁都酒泉，「以图东向」，欲争河西。

李暠之治，重文教：立泮宫（学校），增高门学生五百人；劝课农桑，教民稼穑；又「以文教致治」，河西文风为之一振。然西凉地狭力弱，介于北凉、柔然之间，境土日蹙。嘉兴元年，李暠崩，谥武昭王；其子李歆继位，与沮渠蒙逊战于蓼泉，兵败身死，西凉亡。

史家评李暠：「英姿杰出，有雄武之略」，然「地不盈百郡，众不过数万」，终非蒙逊之敌。西凉享国二十一年而亡，其政绩虽可观，然处于强邻之间，文治终不敌武功。李氏后裔归北魏、入隋唐，唐高祖李渊自称凉武昭王之后——西凉之亡，而李唐之祖系自此绵延。
