bio_parts_en.value:
Li Gao, styled Xuansheng, was a man of Chengji in Longxi, claiming descent from the Han general Li Guang. "Studious from youth, learned in the classics and histories," he served as Duan Ye's governor of Dunhuang. In the 1st year of Gengzi he held Dunhuang and styled himself Duke of Liang, opening the era Gengzi — the beginning of Western Liang. In the 1st year of Jianchu he moved the capital to Jiuquan, "looking eastward," to contend for Hexi.

His rule honored letters: he founded an academy, enlarged the students to five hundred, encouraged farming and mulberries, and taught the people husbandry; "governing by culture," he made the letters of Hexi flourish. But Western Liang was cramped and weak, set between Northern Liang and the Rouran, its borders shrinking. He died in the 1st year of Jiaxing, posthumously King Wuzhao; his son Xin succeeded, fought Juqu Mengxun at Liaoquan, fell in battle, and Western Liang perished.

The historians say of him: "of outstanding bearing, with the air of a hero," yet "his land was not a hundred commanderies, his host not ten thousand men" — no match for Mengxun. Western Liang lasted twenty-one years; its government was admirable, but between strong neighbors culture could not hold against arms. His descendants served Northern Wei and passed into the Sui and Tang — the Tang founder Li Yuan claiming descent from King Wuzhao of Liang: the state died, but the Li line ran on to an empire.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 87 (biography of the Martial King of Liang), ch. 129 (records of Juqu Mengxun) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 夏世祖 · 主要事迹

赫连勃勃，匈奴铁弗部人，刘卫辰之子，原名刘勃勃。其父为北魏所灭，勃勃奔后秦，仕姚兴。龙升元年，勃勃叛后秦，自称天王、大单于，国号大夏——「胡夏」始。勃勃以「帝王系天，当以赫连为氏」之义，改姓赫连。

凤翔元年，勃勃发民夫十万筑统万城：以蒸土筑城，锥入一寸，即杀筑者；「筑城之人，无不殒命」。昌武元年，乘刘裕北伐后秦、刘裕南还之机，勃勃取长安，即皇帝位，建都统万。胡夏全盛时，「南据长安，北临大漠」，然其暴政，为十六国之最：史载勃勃「常以所造器械，验其工拙，射甲不入者斩弓人，入则斩甲匠」，日杀工匠数千。

真兴七年，勃勃崩，子赫连昌继位。承光三年，北魏太武帝破统万，昌被擒；其后定胜四年，胡夏为北魏所灭。史家评勃勃：「雄武过人，残忍好杀，虽匈奴之暴，未有甚于此者。」统万城今犹矗立于陕北沙漠中，为其暴政之纪念碑。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷130《赫连勃勃载记》、卷131《赫连昌载记》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Helian Bobo, originally Liu Bobo, was a Tie Fu Xiongnu, son of Liu Weichen. His father was destroyed by Northern Wei, and Bobo fled to serve Yao Xing of Later Qin. In the 1st year of Longsheng he turned against Later Qin, styled himself Heavenly King and Great Chanyu, and founded the realm Great Xia — "Xia" to history. Taking the surname Helian — "the Son of Heaven, linked to Heaven" — he built his state on war.

In the 1st year of Fengxiang he drove a hundred thousand laborers to build Tongwan: the earth was steamed and pounded, and if an awl could pierce it a finger's depth, the builder was slain — "of the builders, none escaped death." In the 1st year of Changwu, riding Liu Yu's withdrawal south after taking Chang'an, Bobo seized the city and the imperial throne, with Tongwan as his seat. At its height Xia "held Chang'an in the south and faced the great desert in the north"; and its tyranny was the worst of the age: the records say he tested his weapons by their workmanship — if an arrow failed to pierce armor the bowyer died, if it pierced, the armorer — killing thousands of craftsmen a day.

He died in the 7th year of Zhenxing; his son Helian Chang succeeded, and in the 3rd year of Cheng'guang Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei broke Tongwan and took Chang. Xia, fleeing west, was finally destroyed in the 4th year of Dingsheng. The historians say: "of more than common ferocity, cruel and loving slaughter — among the Xiongnu there was none worse." Tongwan's walls still stand in the northern Shaanxi sands — the monument of his tyranny.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 130 (records of Helian Bobo), ch. 131 (records of Helian Chang) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 北燕文成帝 · 主要事迹

冯跋，长乐信都人，汉人。后燕末，慕容熙暴虐，太平元年，冯跋与高云等杀熙，推高云为帝；旋云为离班等所杀，跋即天王位，都龙城——北燕始，为十六国中唯一汉人建立的政权。

冯跋之治，宽和安民：省徭薄赋，劝课农桑，「人皆称便」；又安集流民，赋税宽简；与柔然和亲，稳定北边；兴学校，尊儒学。北燕虽局促辽西，然在十六国后期乱世中，其治实属可观。太平二十二年，冯跋病笃，其弟冯弘杀太子冯翼自立；后弘为北魏所逼，奔高句丽，北燕亡。

史家评冯跋：「宽仁厚德，务存节俭」，然「保境安民，不能进取中原」。北燕以汉人政权立于胡族环伺之中，享国二十余年，赖其宽政与和亲；然终因国力微弱，为北魏所并。北燕之亡，五胡十六国之局亦近尾声。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷125《冯跋载记》、卷125《冯弘载记》及《魏书·冯跋传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Feng Ba was a Han of Xindu in Changle. In the last years of Later Yan the emperor Murong Xi was a tyrant; in the 1st year of Taiping Ba and Gao Yun and the others slew Xi and set up Yun; when Yun was slain by Li Ban and the rest, Ba took the heavenly throne himself, with his capital at Longcheng — the beginning of Northern Yan, the one Han-founded state of the Sixteen.

His rule was lenient and pacific: he lightened corvée and taxes, encouraged farming and mulberries, "and the people praised it"; he gathered the refugees and made the levies easy; he married peace with the Rouran, steadying the northern border; he founded schools and honored Confucian learning. Cramped in Liaoxi though it was, Northern Yan's government was among the most admirable of the later Sixteen States. In the 22nd year of Taiping, as Ba lay ill, his brother Feng Hong slew the heir Feng Yi and took the throne; pressed by Northern Wei, Hong fled to Goguryeo, and Northern Yan was no more.

The historians say of Ba: "benevolent and generous, careful in economy," yet "he held his borders and cared for his people, but could not press into the Central Plains." A Han regime ringed by barbarian states, Northern Yan held on over twenty years by its lenient rule and its marriages of peace; and with its fall, the Sixteen States age itself drew to its end.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 125 (records of Feng Ba), ch. 125 (records of Feng Hong), and the *Weishu*, biography of Feng Ba (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前凉武王 · 主要事迹

张轨字士彦，安定乌氏人，「明敏好学，有器望」。永宁元年，八王之乱方炽，轨请为凉州刺史，遂据河西。时中原大乱，轨保境安民，劝课农桑，立学校，「凉州自轨以来，号为乐土」——西晋士民避乱者，多归凉州。

张轨之治：讨破鲜卑若罗拔能，威行河西；以周玘等为谋主，兴文教、置学官；「忠于晋室」，贡献不绝，受西晋封爵。建兴二年，张轨病卒，谥武公，子寔继位。张氏世守凉州，历九主七十六年（301-376），为十六国中命祚最长者——前凉虽未称帝，然其据河西自守，实为一方之政权。

史家评张轨：「怀抚羌胡，化行河右。」在中原板荡之际，凉州独保太平，衣冠南渡之外，更有士人西走凉州——「凉州之畜为天下饶」，张轨之治，为乱世中之净土。其子孙后为前秦所灭，然前凉之德，犹为后世所称。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷86《张轨传》、卷86《张寔传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts.value:
张轨字士彦，安定乌氏人，「明敏好学，有器望」。永宁元年，八王之乱方炽，轨请为凉州刺史，遂据河西。时中原大乱，轨保境安民，劝课农桑，立学校，「凉州自轨以来，号为乐土」——西晋士民避乱者，多归凉州。

张轨之治：讨破鲜卑若罗拔能，威行河西；以周玘等为谋主，兴文教、置学官；「忠于晋室」，贡献不绝，受西晋封爵。建兴二年，张轨病卒，谥武公，子寔继位。张氏世守凉州，历九主七十六年（301-376），为十六国中命祚最长者——前凉虽未称帝，然其据河西自守，实为一方之政权。

史家评张轨：「怀抚羌胡，化行河右。」在中原板荡之际，凉州独保太平，衣冠南渡之外，更有士人西走凉州——「凉州之畜为天下饶」，张轨之治，为乱世中之净土。其子孙后为前秦所灭，然前凉之德，犹为后世所称。

> 本地参考：点校本《晋书》卷86《张轨传》、卷86《张寔传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Zhang Gui, styled Shiyan, was a man of Wushi in Anding, "sharp and studious, of high repute." In the 1st year of Yongning, with the War of the Eight Princes blazing, he asked for the governorship of Liangzhou and held Hexi. While the Central Plains collapsed he kept his borders and his people, encouraged farming and mulberries, and founded schools — "Liangzhou, since Gui, was called the land of delight" — and the gentry and refugees of the Jin fled west to him.

His rule: he broke the Xianbei Ruoluo Baneng and his name ran through Hexi; with Zhou Qi and the others as counselors he furthered letters and established academies; "loyal to the Jin house," he never ceased tribute and received Jin's titles. He died of illness in the 2nd year of Jianxing, posthumously Duke Wu, and his son Shi succeeded. The Zhang house held Liangzhou through nine rulers and seventy-six years (301–376), the longest-lived of the Sixteen States — though it never took the imperial title, its self-ruling Hexi was a true power.

The historians say of him: "he cherished the Qiang and the Hu, and carried civilization through the river lands." While the Central Plains went under, Liangzhou alone kept its peace; besides the caps and gowns crossing south, there was a westward flight of scholars — "Liangzhou's cattle were the realm's wealth" — and Gui's rule was a refuge in the storm. His descendants were later swept away by Former Qin, but the virtue of Former Liang was long remembered.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 86 (biography of Zhang Gui), ch. 86 (biography of Zhang Shi) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 代王 · 主要事迹

拓跋什翼犍，拓跋鲜卑首领，拓跋郁律之子。幼年质于后赵，见识中原制度。建国元年，什翼犍即代王位，建元建国，都云中盛乐——代国自此有年号、有都城，渐脱部落之习。

什翼犍之治，为拓跋部由部落联盟向国家过渡之关键：始制法律，「法令明整」；分土定居，「分筑城郭」；又置百官，仿晋制。军事上，屡北征高车、西击刘卫辰，代北强盛。建国三十九年，前秦苻坚遣军大举来攻，代国诸部溃散，什翼犍为其庶子寔君所杀（一说为苻坚所害），代国亡。

代国虽亡，然拓跋之根未绝：什翼犍之孙拓跋珪，于淝水之战后复国，改称魏，是为北魏道武帝。北魏追尊什翼犍为昭成皇帝。史家论什翼犍：立法建国，开北魏之先河——五胡诸国多旋兴旋亡，而拓跋氏历亡而不绝，终统一北方，其奠基之功，实自什翼犍始。

> 本地参考：点校本《魏书》卷1《序纪》、卷113《官氏志》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Tuoba Shiyijian was a chief of the Tuoba Xianbei, son of Tuoba Yulü. In his youth he was a hostage in Later Zhao and saw the institutions of the Central Plains. In the 1st year of Jianguo he took the throne as King of Dai, opened the era Jianguo, and made Shengle in Yunzhong his capital — the Dai realm now had its own era and capital, and began to leave the tribal way behind.

His reign marks the passage of the Tuoba from tribal league to state: he first fixed the laws, "clear and strict"; he allotted the lands for settlement and "built walled towns"; he installed his officials on the Jin model. In arms he campaigned north again and again against the Gaoche and west against Liu Weichen, and the north grew strong under him. In the 39th year of Jianguo, Fu Jian of Former Qin came against him in force; the tribes scattered, and Shiyijian was slain by his own son Shijun (or, some say, by Fu Jian's men) — the Dai realm was no more.

But the Tuoba root was not cut: his grandson Tuoba Gui, after the Fei River defeat, restored the state under the name Wei — Emperor Daowu of Northern Wei. Northern Wei honored Shiyijian as Emperor Zhaocheng. The historians see in him the maker of the laws and statehood of the Tuoba, the forerunner of Northern Wei: of all the barbarian states, only the Tuoba fell and rose again to unite the north — and the foundation was laid by Shiyijian.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Weishu*, ch. 1 ("Prefatory Annals"), ch. 113 (treatise on official clans) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.summary_en: The founding ruler of Western Xia, who proclaimed himself emperor of Great Xia in 1038, created the Tangut script and a dual Tangut–Han official system, defeated Song armies three times, and stood as a third power alongside Song and Liao.

emperors.bio_md:
# 西夏景宗 · 主要事迹

李元昊是西夏实际的开国之主。1032 年父李德明卒，他袭夏王位，随即加速去宋化与民族国家建构；1038 年在兴庆府即皇帝位，国号大夏，改元天授礼法延祚，正式与宋、辽并立。本页以《宋史·卷485·夏国传》为年表主线，《辽史》相关纪为二手入口。

称帝前后，他完成了一整套国族符号与制度建构：命野利仁荣等造番书（西夏文），改服饰官制，又设中书、枢密等机构，番汉分号。这套"强化主体性"的路线，与[[n-wei-xiaowen|北魏孝文帝]]的汉化改革恰好方向相反，对读可见中古北方政权处理自身身份的两种极端路径。

武功方面，约 1036 年他攻取瓜、沙、肃等河西走廊要地，奠定称帝版图——这条走廊正是[[han-wu-di|汉武帝]]时代开通的西北命脉，千年之后成为大夏立国的根基。1040 年三川口、1041 年好水川、1042 年定川寨，夏军连续三年重创宋军，确立了西夏的军事地位；好水川一役尤为宋夏战争的名场面（互见《宋史》任福等列传）。

连战之后是外交收尾。1044 年宋夏达成庆历和议：元昊对宋称臣而自帝其国，以名实分离换取岁赐与边境稳定；同年与辽冲突后言和，在宋、辽、夏三角之间周旋得体。文治、武功、韬略三线，至此把一个河西政权立成了鼎立之一极。

1048 年，元昊在宫廷斗争中被刺死，幼主谅祚继立，外戚没藏氏掌权——国祚并未随他个人终结，西夏转入后续诸帝。需要说明的是，宋、辽史书对西夏站位偏贬，本项目月旦取中；西夏文创制等细节仍待专书补证。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Yuanhao was the de facto founder of Western Xia. In 1032 his father Li Deming died and he succeeded as Prince of Xia, at once accelerating de-Songification and nation-building; in 1038 he proclaimed himself emperor at Xingqing, took the dynastic name Great Xia, and changed the era to Tianshou Lifa Yanzuo, formally standing alongside Song and Liao. This page takes 《宋史·卷485·夏国传》 as the backbone of its chronology, with the relevant annals of 《辽史》 as a secondary entry point.

Around his proclamation he completed a whole set of national symbols and institutions: he ordered Yeli Renrong and others to devise the Tangut script, reformed dress and officialdom, and established organs such as the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs under separate Tangut and Han designations. This line of "asserting distinctiveness" ran in exactly the opposite direction from the sinicization of

; read together, they show the two extreme paths by which medieval northern regimes handled their own identity.

On the military side, around 1036 he seized Gua, Sha, Su, and other key points of the Hexi Corridor, laying the territorial foundation for his imperial claim—the very corridor opened in the age of

as the northwest lifeline, which a thousand years later became the ground on which Great Xia was founded. At Sanchuankou in 1040, Haoshuichuan in 1041, and Dingchuanzhai in 1042, Xia forces mauled the Song armies three years running and established Western Xia's military standing; Haoshuichuan in particular is the famous set piece of the Song–Xia war (cross-referenced in the biographies of Ren Fu and others in 《宋史》).

After the string of victories came the diplomatic wrap-up. In 1044 Song and Xia reached the Qingli settlement: Yuanhao styled himself a subject toward Song while reigning as emperor within his own realm, trading the split between name and fact for annual payments and a stable border; the same year, after clashes with Liao, he made peace, maneuvering deftly within the Song–Liao–Xia triangle. Civil construction, military success, and statecraft together had by now raised a Hexi regime into one pole of a tripartite standoff.

In 1048 Yuanhao was stabbed to death amid palace struggles; the child ruler Liangzuo succeeded, and the consort clan Mozang took power—the dynasty did not end with his person, and Western Xia passed to its later rulers. It should be noted that Song and Liao historiography is biased against Western Xia, so this project's appraisal takes a middle position; details such as the creation of the Tangut script still await confirmation from specialized scholarship.

emperors.summary_en: A man of Hefei in Luzhou; in the late Tang he held Huainan as military governor with his seat at Yangzhou; in mid-Qianning he destroyed Sun Ru and fixed the Jiang-Huai; in the 2nd year of Tianfu Tang made him King of Wu; he kept his borders and rested his people, and the Jiang-Huai knew modest peace. He died in the 2nd year of Tianyou.

# 吴太祖 · 主要事迹

杨行密，庐州合肥人。唐末群雄并起，行密以「庐州八营」起家，景福中为淮南节度使，都扬州——杨吴政权之基。乾宁中，与孙儒争江淮，破孙儒，定淮南，「兵精粮足，为东南之最」；又广纳贤士，用袁袭、高勖等，保境息民，江淮之间，「农桑颇兴，市井晏然」，为乱世中之小康。

天复二年，唐封行密为吴王。行密在位十余年，养士爱民，又兴修水利、劝课农桑，「淮南之民，颇获休息」；然其卒后，子渥、隆演相继，皆不能制徐温——杨氏之权，渐移徐氏。

天祐二年，行密卒，年五十四。史评行密：「保境息民，江淮小康。」五代十国之中，杨吴地广兵强，为南方大国；行密之治，虽不及钱镠之「满城桃李」，然「江淮底定」，实开杨吴、南唐两代之基。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷061《吴世家》、旧五代史卷134《杨行密传》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yang Xingmi, a man of Hefei in Luzhou, rose in the late-Tang chaos from the "eight camps of Luzhou"; in mid-Jingfu he became military governor of Huainan with his seat at Yangzhou — the foundation of the Yang Wu realm. In mid-Qianning he contended with Sun Ru for the Jiang-Huai, destroyed him, and fixed the Huainan: "soldiers fine and grain ample, the finest of the southeast." He drew in the worthy — Yuan Xi, Gao Xun, and the rest — kept his borders, and rested his people; farming flourished and the markets were quiet, a modest peace in the storm.

In the 2nd year of Tianfu Tang made him King of Wu. Over a decade he nourished his officers and loved his people, mending the waterways and urging the plough, "the people of Huainan gaining rest." But after his death his sons Wo and Longyan in turn could not check Xu Wen — the power of the Yang house passed to the Xu.

He died in the 2nd year of Tianyou, aged fifty-four. The histories say: "he kept his borders and rested his people — the Jiang-Huai knew modest peace." Of the Ten Kingdoms, Yang Wu was broad and strong, the great state of the south; and Xingmi's rule, fixing the Jiang-Huai, opened the two generations of Yang Wu and Southern Tang.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 61 ("Annals of Wu"), and the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 134 (biography of Yang Xingmi) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 吴睿帝 · 主要事迹

杨溥，杨行密第四子。武义二年（920），兄隆演卒，溥即位——此时杨吴之政，已尽在徐温、徐知诰父子之手。乾贞元年（927），徐知诰欲行禅代，先使溥即皇帝位，徐氏之谋渐露。

溥在位十七年，为徐氏傀儡：徐温卒后，徐知诰（李昪）执政，进封齐王，加九锡；天祚三年（937），知诰逼溥禅位，建国号齐（旋改唐），杨吴亡——自杨行密天复二年封吴王，杨氏传四主三十六年而绝。溥禅后居润州，数月而卒。

史评杨溥：「拱手让国。」杨吴之亡，非亡于溥之昏，而亡于徐氏之强——徐温以养子之身夺杨氏之权，其「代吴」之势，自行密卒后已成。溥以傀儡之君，「拱手」而已；南唐之兴，实为杨吴之延续。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷061《吴世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yang Pu, fourth son of Yang Xingmi, took the throne in the 2nd year of Wuyi (920) after his brother Longyan's death — by then the government of Yang Wu lay wholly with Xu Wen and his adopted son Xu Zhigao. In the 1st year of Qianzhen (927), moving toward the abdication, Zhigao first had Pu take the imperial title; the Xu design was plain.

Seventeen years he reigned as the Xu's puppet: after Xu Wen's death, Xu Zhigao (Li Bian) governed, was made Prince of Qi, and given the nine gifts; in the 3rd year of Tianzuo (937) Zhigao forced the abdication, founding the realm Qi (soon renamed Tang) — the Yang Wu was no more, four rulers and thirty-six years from Xingmi's kingship. Pu, settled at Runzhou, died within months.

The histories say of Pu: "he ceded the realm with folded hands." Yang Wu fell not to Pu's dullness but to the Xu's strength — Xu Wen, an adopted son, took the Yang power, and the "taking of Wu" was already fixed from Xingmi's death. Pu, a puppet sovereign, only folded his hands; the rise of Southern Tang was the continuation of Yang Wu.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 61 ("Annals of Wu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 南唐烈祖 · 主要事迹

李昪（原名徐知诰），徐州人，杨吴权臣徐温之养子。昇元元年（937），受杨溥禅让即帝位，国号齐，旋改唐，都金陵——南唐始。昇元中，复姓李，改名昪，自称唐宪宗之后，「绍唐之志」自此立。

李昪之治，以「息兵保境」为务：与吴越、楚等邻国通好，不轻启战端；劝农桑、兴学校、轻赋税，「江淮之间，晏然无事」；又建「昇元阁」藏图籍，文治之盛，冠于江南。南唐立国之初，「中外寝兵，境内以安」，实赖烈祖之规模。

昇元七年，李昪崩，年五十六，子李璟即位。史评烈祖：「开国有规，享国短。」南唐以金陵为都，承杨吴之地，据江南富庶之区；烈祖以养子之身得国，而能行仁政、定规模——南唐之所以为十国中文治最盛者，实自烈祖始。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷062《南唐世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Bian, originally Xu Zhigao, was a man of Xuzhou, adopted son of the Yang Wu regent Xu Wen. In the 1st year of Shengyuan (937) he received Yang Pu's abdication, taking the throne as the realm Qi, soon renamed Tang, with its capital at Jinling — Southern Tang began. In mid-Shengyuan he resumed the surname Li, took the name Bian, and claimed descent from Emperor Xianzong of Tang — the "successor of Tang" from that day.

His government aimed at peace within the borders: he made friends with Wuyue and Chu rather than war; he urged farming and mulberries, founded schools, and lightened the taxes, "the Jiang-Huai quietly at ease"; he raised the Shengyuan library of books, and the culture of the south outshone all. In the early years of the realm "the armies rested and the borders were at peace," the work of the Ancestor Lie's ordering.

He died in the 7th year of Shengyuan, aged fifty-six; his son Jing (the Yuan Zong) succeeded. The histories say: "his founding was well-ordered; his reign was brief." Southern Tang, seated at Jinling over the rich lands of the Yang Wu, became the most cultivated of the Ten Kingdoms — and the pattern was the Ancestor Lie's.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 62 ("Annals of Southern Tang") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 南唐元宗 · 主要事迹

李璟，李昪长子。保大元年（943）即位。元宗「风度高雅，好文学」，与冯延巳、冯延鲁、韩熙载等词臣相善，「吹皱一池春水」之词，传为美谈——南唐词学之盛，自元宗始。

然元宗「好大喜功」：保大中，乘闽国内乱出兵灭闽（部分），又与楚争衡，拓地虽广，而「兵连祸结，国用日蹙」；交泰元年（958），周世宗南伐，南唐大败，元宗去帝号称「江南国主」，割江北十四州——南唐由盛转衰，自此而始。建隆二年（961），元宗迁都洪州，寻崩，年四十六，子李煜即位。

史评元宗：「承业守成而好文，拓地开疆而失策。」南唐之衰，衰于元宗之拓地：江北既失，国势已弱；李煜承之，「四十年来家国」，终为宋灭。元宗之词与元宗之失，同为南唐之写照。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷062《南唐世家》、南唐书（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Jing, eldest son of Li Bian, took the throne in the 1st year of Baoda (943). The Yuan Zong was "of high bearing, a lover of letters," at ease with the ci poets Feng Yansi, Feng Yanlu, Han Xizai, and the rest — "stirring a spring pond's water" passing into the talk of the age: the glory of Southern Tang ci began with him.

But he was "fond of great designs": in mid-Baoda, riding Min's internal wars, he sent armies to destroy part of Min, and contended with Chu — the borders widened while "the wars dragged on and the state's purse shrank." In the 1st year of Jiaotai (958) Emperor Shizong of Zhou campaigned south; Southern Tang was shattered, Jing dropped the imperial title for "ruler of the south of the river," and ceded the fourteen prefectures north of the Yangzi — the turn of Southern Tang from strength to decline. In the 2nd year of Jianlong (961) he moved the capital to Hongzhou and died, aged forty-six; his son Yu (Li Yu) succeeded.

The histories say: "he inherited and held, loving letters; he widened the borders and lost by misjudgment." The decline of Southern Tang began with his widening: the north of the river lost, the state's strength ebbed — and Li Yu, inheriting, "forty years of home and realm," fell to Song at last. The Yuan Zong's ci and the Yuan Zong's loss are the two faces of Southern Tang.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 62 ("Annals of Southern Tang"), and the *Nantangshu* (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 南唐后主 · 主要事迹

李煜是南唐末主。宋建隆二年（961），中主李璟卒，李煜继位于金陵，此时南唐对宋已处劣势。本页以《宋史·卷478·南唐世家》为年表主线，《宋史·太祖纪》编年互见（本地参考库已备）。

开宝前后（971），他去帝号、称江南国主，对宋称臣以求苟安；在位间倾力于书画音律词章，文艺成就远超君道事功。

开宝七年（974），曹彬等率宋师南下伐江南，兵临长江；开宝八年（975）宋军破金陵，后主出降，南唐亡。此役出自[[n-song-tai-zu|宋太祖]]朝平江南的部署，可与宋方本纪对读。

开宝九年（976）他北迁汴京，封违命侯，软禁中词多故国之思。太平兴国三年（978）卒于京师，时宋太宗在位；民间有七夕赐牵机药传说，正史记载简略，此处作待考处理。

他的后效在文学：二主词为词史入口，君道失败与词人成就分离，后世月旦常带同情分。与南唐元宗（中主李璟）对读，可见南唐自中主至后主两代而终的格局。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Yu was the last ruler of the Southern Tang. In the second year of the Song Jianlong era (961), the Middle Ruler Li Jing died, and Li Yu succeeded to the throne at Jinling, with Southern Tang already at a disadvantage against the Song. This page takes 《宋史·卷478·南唐世家》 as the chronological backbone, cross-checked against the annals in 《宋史·太祖纪》 (available in the local reference library).

Around the Kaibao era (971), he renounced the imperial title, styled himself Ruler of Jiangnan, and submitted to the Song as a vassal in search of a precarious peace; throughout his reign he poured his energy into painting, calligraphy, music, and verse, and his literary achievement far outran his record as a sovereign.

In the seventh year of Kaibao (974), Cao Bin and others led the Song army south against Jiangnan and brought it to the banks of the Yangtze; in the eighth year (975) Song forces breached Jinling, the Last Ruler came out and surrendered, and Southern Tang fell. This campaign grew out of the Jiangnan strategy of

's court and can be read against the Song-side basic annals.

In the ninth year of Kaibao (976) he was moved north to Bianjing and enfeoffed as the Marquis of Weiming; in confinement his ci poems dwelled on longing for his lost realm. He died at the capital in the third year of Taiping Xingguo (978), while Emperor Taizong of Song was on the throne; a folk legend holds that poison was granted to him on the Double Seventh night, but the standard histories record little, and the matter is treated here as unverified.

His afterlife lies in literature: the ci of the Two Rulers are an entryway into the history of the genre, his failure as a sovereign is read apart from his achievement as a poet, and later judgment has often carried a measure of sympathy. Read alongside Southern Tang Yuanzong (the Middle Ruler Li Jing), the page shows the shape of a Southern Tang that ran its course in two generations, from the Middle Ruler to the Last Ruler.

emperors.bio_md:
# 吴越太祖 · 主要事迹

钱镠，杭州临安人。开平元年（907），后梁封钱镠为吴越王，据两浙——吴越国之始。钱镠出身盐贩，「起自寒微」，而治两浙数十年，政绩卓著：筑钱塘江捍海塘，「以石为堤，以御潮患」，杭州遂成东南都会；又广建城郭、兴修水利、劝课农桑，「满城桃李，夹道花木」。

钱镠之政，以「事大保境」为纲：对中原五代政权，一律称臣纳贡，不称帝、不争霸——「钱氏之祚，赖事大以延」。吴越以两浙弹丸之地，在五代纷争中保境安民八十余年，百姓「安居乐业」，为十国中政局最稳者。

长兴三年，钱镠卒，年八十一。史评钱镠：「有功于浙，民到于今称之。」吴越虽偏安一隅，然钱镠之筑塘、治杭、保境，为杭州成为「人间天堂」奠定根基；钱氏后裔于太平兴国三年纳土归宋，「以善终」，亦为乱世中难得之结局。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷067《吴越世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Qian Liu, a man of Lin'an in Hangzhou, was made King of Wuyue by Later Liang in the 1st year of Kaiping (907), holding the two Zhe — the beginning of Wuyue. A salt-dealer who "rose from the meanest," he governed the two Zhe for decades with real achievement: he built the Qiantang sea wall, "stone for the dike to hold the tide," and Hangzhou became the great city of the southeast; he raised walls, mended the waterways, and urged farming — "the streets full of peach and plum, the ways lined with flowers."

His rule ran on "serving the great and keeping the borders": to every dynasty of the Central Plains he was a vassal, never emperor, never contending — "the fortunes of the Qian were prolonged by serving the great." On the sliver of the two Zhe, amid the wars of the Five Dynasties, Wuyue kept its borders and its people for over eighty years, the most stable state of the Ten.

He died in the 3rd year of Changxing, aged eighty-one. The histories say: "he served Zhe well; the people praise him to this day." Wuyue hugged one corner, but Qian Liu's wall, his Hangzhou, and his peace laid the base of the "earthly paradise" of Hangzhou; and his heirs, surrendering their lands to Song in the 3rd year of Taiping Xingguo, ended well — a rare ending in that age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 67 ("Annals of Wuyue") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 闽太祖 · 主要事迹

王审知，光州固始人。随兄王潮、王绪入闽，乾宁中继兄潮为威武军节度使，据福州。开平三年（909），后梁封审知为闽王，都福州——闽国始。审知「为人俭约，好礼下士」，兴学校、建开元寺，又招徕海商，「闽中物产，通于海舶」，福州遂为东南海港。

审知之政，轻徭薄赋：史称其「躬节俭，与民休息」，「招蛮夷商贾，广市海舶」；又辟甘棠港，通海上贸易。十国之中，闽之文教、商业并盛，实赖审知之经营。同光三年（925），审知卒，闽人称其「忠懿」。

史评审知：「开国贤主，闽人称忠懿。」然审知卒后，诸子争立：延翰、延钧相继，骨肉相残，闽政遂乱；至 945 年为南唐所灭。闽之兴，兴于审知之宽仁；闽之亡，亡于王氏子孙之相残——「开国贤主，后嗣不肖」，为十国常见之命运。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷068《闽世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Wang Shenzhi, a man of Gushi in Guangzhou, entered Min with his brother Wang Chao and Wang Xu; in mid-Qianning he succeeded his brother Chao as military governor of the Weiwu army, holding Fuzhou. In the 3rd year of Kaiping (909) Later Liang made him King of Min with his seat at Fuzhou — the beginning of Min. Frugal and courteous to the worthy, he founded schools, raised the Kaiyuan temple, and drew in the sea merchants — "the produce of Min reaching the ships," Fuzhou becoming the port of the southeast.

His government was light-levied: "he was frugal himself and rested the people," "drew the barbarian merchants and widened the sea trade"; he opened the Gantang harbor and the sea commerce flourished. Of the Ten Kingdoms, Min's letters and trade stood together at their height — the work of Shenzhi's ordering. He died in the 3rd year of Tongguang (925); the people of Min call him "the loyal and good."

The histories say: "a worthy founder; the people of Min call him loyal and good." But after his death his sons contended — Yanhan, Yanjun in turn, kin slaying kin, the government of Min falling into disorder until Southern Tang destroyed it in 945. Min rose on Shenzhi's benevolence and fell to his descendants' slaughter — "a worthy founder, unworthy heirs," the common fate of the Ten Kingdoms.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 68 ("Annals of Min") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 闽惠宗 · 主要事迹

王延钧，王审知次子。天成元年（926），兄延翰被杀，延钧继立；天成中改名王鏻。龙启元年（933），延钧称帝，国号闽，改元龙启——闽国始有帝号。然延钧「好神仙，大兴土木」：作宝皇宫、度民为僧，又崇信道士陈守元，「政事一决于巫祝」。

永和元年（935），延钧之子王昶与皇城使李仿等密谋，弑延钧于宫中，年约四十。延钧在位约九年，闽政由「审知之治」转入「诸子之乱」。

史评延钧：「称帝而政乱。」闽国自延钧称帝后，帝位传承悉出骨肉相残：延钧弑兄而立，子昶弑父而继——「闽政之乱，自延钧始」。其后王昶、王延羲、王延政相继，闽国内乱不止，终于 945 年为南唐所灭。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷068《闽世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Wang Yanjun, second son of Wang Shenzhi, succeeded in the 1st year of Tiancheng (926) after his brother Yanhan was slain; in mid-Tiancheng he took the name Wang Lin. In the 1st year of Longqi (933) he took the imperial title, the realm of Min — Min first bore the emperor's name. But he "loved the immortals and raised great works": he built the Baohuang Palace, made monks of the people, and trusted the Daoist Chen Shouyuan, "the government decided by shamans and prayers."

In the 1st year of Yonghe (935) his son Wang Chang, with the palace commander Li Fang and the others, slew him in the palace, around forty. About nine years he reigned, and the government of Min passed from Shenzhi's ordering into the sons' wars.

The histories say: "he took the imperial title, and the government fell into disorder." From Yanjun's title on, the throne of Min passed by kin slaying kin: Yanjun slew his brother to rise, and his son Chang slew him — "the disorders of Min began with Yanjun." Wang Chang, Wang Yanxi, Wang Yanzheng followed, and Min, torn within, was destroyed by Southern Tang in 945.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 68 ("Annals of Min") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 楚武穆王 · 主要事迹

马殷，许州鄢陵人。乾宁中，随孙儒余部入湖南，据潭州；开平元年（907），后梁封马殷为楚王，据湖南——楚国始。马殷「为人宽厚」，以许德勋、高郁为谋主：兴茶商，「听民自采茶卖，北客收之，岁得百万」；又铸铅铁钱，内用外不用，商贾之利尽归于楚——楚之富，实自茶商起。

马殷在位二十余年，保境通商：北事梁、唐，南抚溪洞，「湖南之民，颇得休息」。然马殷晚年，诸子争立之祸已萌：长兴元年（930）马殷卒，年七十九，诸子相攻，楚国遂衰。

史评马殷：「保境通商，湖南安之。」楚国以茶商立国，为十国中最「务商」者；然马殷卒后，「诸子争立，兄弟相残」，楚祚仅传二代而内乱，951 年为南唐所灭。楚之兴在通商，其亡在失和——「兴于商而败于家」，为十国之一例。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷066《楚世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Ma Yin, a man of Yanling in Xuzhou, entered Hunan in mid-Qianning with Sun Ru's remnant and held Tanzhou; in the 1st year of Kaiping (907) Later Liang made him King of Chu, holding Hunan — the beginning of Chu. Ma Yin was "generous by nature"; with Xu Dexun and Gao Yu as his counselors he promoted the tea trade — "the people free to gather and sell tea, the northern merchants taking it, a million a year" — and minted iron coins that worked within the realm only, so that the merchants' profit fell to Chu: the wealth of Chu rose from tea.

Over twenty years he kept his borders and opened his commerce: serving Liang and Tang in the north, soothing the cave peoples in the south, "the people of Hunan gaining rest." But in his last years the sons' contention was already seeded; he died in the 1st year of Changxing (930), aged seventy-nine, and his sons fell to fighting — Chu declined.

The histories say: "he kept his borders and opened the trade, and Hunan was at peace." Chu, a realm built on tea, was the most commercial of the Ten; but after Ma Yin's death "the sons contended, brothers slaying brothers," and within two generations Chu fell to Southern Tang in 951. Chu rose on commerce and fell on discord — one lesson of the age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 66 ("Annals of Chu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 南汉高祖 · 主要事迹

刘䶮（yǎn），上蔡人。乾化中，继兄刘隐为清海节度使，据岭南；乾亨元年（917），于番禺称帝，国号大越，旋改汉——南汉始。刘䶮「有并岭南之功」：西并邕、容，南抚交趾，岭南之地，尽归南汉。

然刘䶮「刑政惨毒」：史载其作「烧、煮、剥、剔、刀山、剑树」等刑，「以水银灌鼻，以铁床烙体」，残忍为十国之最；又好奢侈，「琼宫玉殿，穷极壮丽」；晚年崇佛，「浮屠之费，日以万计」。大有十五年（942），刘䶮卒，年五十四。

史评刘䶮：「有并岭南之功，而刑政惨毒。」南汉以岭南立国，据有「富庶之区」；然刘䶮之暴政、其后嗣之昏庸（殇帝、中宗、后主），使南汉「政刑日坏」，971 年为宋所灭。南汉之亡，亡于刘氏之暴——「岭南之富，不足以救其酷」。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷065《南汉世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Yan, a man of Shangcai, succeeded his brother Liu Yin in mid-Qianhua as military governor of Qinghai, holding Lingnan; in the 1st year of Qianheng (917) he took the throne at Panyu as the realm Great Yue, soon renamed Han — Southern Han began. He "united Lingnan by merit": absorbing Yong and Rong in the west, soothing Jiaozhi in the south, all Lingnan passed to Southern Han.

But his "punishments and government were cruel beyond measure": the records tell of his tortures — "burning, boiling, flaying, excising, the knife-hill, the sword-tree," "mercury poured up the nose, iron beds to sear the flesh" — the cruelest of the Ten Kingdoms; he loved luxury, "jade halls and palaces of the utmost splendor," and in his last years doted on Buddhism, "the monks' cost ten thousand a day." He died in the 15th year of Dayou (942), aged fifty-four.

The histories say: "he united Lingnan by merit, but his punishments and government were poison." Southern Han stood on the rich lands of Lingnan; but Liu Yan's tyranny and his heirs' folly — the Shang, Zhongzong, and Last Sovereign — rotted the government, and Song destroyed it in 971. The fall of Southern Han was the fall of the Liu's cruelty — "the wealth of Lingnan could not save its cruelty."

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 65 ("Annals of Southern Han") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前蜀高祖 · 主要事迹

王建，许州舞阳人，少为「饼师」（卖饼者），后为忠武军卒，「以功升迁」。大顺中，攻陈敬瑄，据成都，遂有两川；天复中，唐封王建为蜀王。天复七年（907），朱温篡唐，王建「以唐室之臣，义不臣梁」，即皇帝位于成都，国号蜀——前蜀始。

王建「为人雄猜，善抚将士」：用韦庄等唐室旧臣，礼贤下士，蜀中文物之盛，为十国之最；又开科取士，蜀中「衣冠文物，甲于西南」。光天元年（918），王建崩，年七十二，子王衍即位。

史评王建：「盗贼起家，能有蜀土。」前蜀据两川之险、天府之富，为十国中之强国；然王建晚年猜忌功臣，后嗣王衍「童騃佚乐」——前蜀二世而亡，为后唐所灭（925）。「其兴也勃，其亡也忽」，前蜀之命运，亦十国之缩影。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷063《前蜀世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Wang Jian, a man of Wuyang in Xuzhou, was a pie-seller in his youth, then a soldier of the Zhongwu army, "rising by merit." In mid-Dashun he attacked Chen Jingxuan, took Chengdu, and held the two Chuan; in mid-Tianfu Tang made him King of Shu. In the 7th year of Tianfu (907), when Zhu Wen usurped Tang, Wang Jian, "a minister of the Tang house, would not bow to Liang," took the imperial throne at Chengdu as the realm Shu — Former Shu began.

He was "bold and suspicious, good at handling his soldiers": he employed the old Tang ministers like Wei Zhuang, honored the worthy, and the culture of Shu was the finest of the Ten; he held examinations, and "the caps and gowns of Shu outshone the southwest." He died in the 1st year of Guangtian (918), aged seventy-two; his son Yan succeeded.

The histories say: "a bandit who rose to hold the lands of Shu." Former Shu stood on the shield of the two Chuan and the wealth of the heavenly prefecture, a strong state of the Ten; but Wang Jian's last years distrusted his meritorious men, and his heir Wang Yan was "a child at ease" — Former Shu fell in two generations, destroyed by Later Tang (925). "Swift to rise, swift to fall" — the fate of Former Shu is the Ten Kingdoms in miniature.

emperors.bio_md:
# 前蜀后主 · 主要事迹

王衍，王建幼子。光天元年（918）即位。王衍「童騃佚乐」：好为「小词」，与韩昭、潘炕等狎客游宴无度，「作怡神亭，与诸狎客宴饮其中」；又微服出游，荒于政事——「前蜀之政，自此日坏」。

咸康元年（925），后唐庄宗遣郭崇韬、魏王继岌伐蜀；唐军入蜀，王衍出降，前蜀亡——自王建称帝至此，历二主十八年。王衍被送往洛阳，同光中，行至秦川驿，为庄宗所诛（一说赐死），年二十八。

史评王衍：「童騃亡国。」前蜀据天府之国，本有自保之资；然王衍「以佚乐亡其国」，十余年基业，一朝而尽。庄宗灭蜀而「函梁君臣之首」之志得伸，然其后庄宗亦以佚乐亡身——「王衍之亡国，庄宗之亡身，同一『佚乐』二字」。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷063《前蜀世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Wang Yan, youngest son of Wang Jian, took the throne in the 1st year of Guangtian (918). He was "a child at ease": he loved his little verses, feasting without limit with Han Zhao, Pan Kang, and the other companions, "raising the Yishen Pavilion to drink with them"; he went abroad in secret dress, careless of government — "the government of Former Shu decayed from that day."

In the 1st year of Xiankang (925) Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang sent Guo Chongtao and the Prince of Wei to invade; the Tang army entered Shu, Wang Yan surrendered, and Former Shu was no more — eighteen years from Wang Jian's title, two rulers. Sent toward Luoyang, he was slain at the Qinchuan post station in mid-Tongguang (some say by decree), aged twenty-eight.

The histories say: "a child who lost the realm." Former Shu held the heavenly prefecture, with the means to stand; but Wang Yan "lost his realm to ease," and a decade's enterprise was spent in a day. Zhuangzong, who "cased the heads of the Liang lords," destroyed Shu — and then lost himself to the same ease: "the fall of Wang Yan's realm and the fall of Zhuangzong's self, the same two words: ease and pleasure."

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 63 ("Annals of Former Shu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 后蜀高祖 · 主要事迹

孟知祥，邢州人。同光三年（925），后唐灭前蜀，知祥为成都尹、西川节度使——前蜀之地，转归后唐。长兴中，知祥与朝廷生隙，据蜀自固；又并东川，破董璋，「有两川之地」。

应顺元年（934）……明德元年，知祥称帝，国号蜀（史称后蜀），都成都。然知祥即位仅数月而崩，年六十一，子孟昶即位。

史评知祥：「开国草创，享国极短。」后蜀之立，为后唐内乱之产物：知祥以节度使之身，乘中原之乱据蜀称帝——与前蜀王建之兴同其轨迹。知祥虽享国极短，然其开国规模、用人之道，为孟昶之「升平文治」奠定基础。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷064《后蜀世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Meng Zhixiang, a man of Xingzhou, was military governor of Xichuan under Later Tang. When Tang destroyed Former Shu in the 3rd year of Tongguang (925), Zhixiang became governor of Chengdu and Xichuan — the lands of Former Shu passed to Later Tang. In mid-Changxing, at odds with the court, he held Shu for himself; he destroyed Dong Zhang of the East Chuan and held both Chuan.

In the 1st year of Mingde (934) he took the imperial throne as the realm Shu (Later Shu to history), with its capital at Chengdu. But he reigned only months, dying at sixty-one; his son Meng Chang succeeded.

The histories say: "a rough founding; his reign was the briefest." Later Shu was a child of the Later Tang disorders: a governor seizing Shu from the chaos of the Central Plains, on the same road as Wang Jian of Former Shu. Brief as his reign was, his ordering and his choice of men laid the base of Meng Chang's age of culture and peace.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 64 ("Annals of Later Shu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后蜀后主 · 主要事迹

孟昶，孟知祥第三子。明德元年（934）即位，时年十六。孟昶在位三十一年，为十国中在位最久者之一：蜀中「承平无事」，孟昶好文学，「与花蕊夫人游宴赋词」，又刻《论语》《尔雅》等石经于成都学宫——后蜀文治之盛，「不减中原」。

然「承平日久，佚乐日滋」：孟昶晚年，「骄奢淫佚」，任用王昭远等庸臣，「军政不修」。乾德三年（965），宋太祖遣王全斌伐蜀；宋军自剑门入，孟昶出降，后蜀亡——自知祥称帝至此，历二主三十二年。孟昶被送至开封，封秦国公，同年卒。

史评孟昶：「佚乐亡国。」后蜀据两川之险、天府之富，「锦江春色」，本可自守；然「生于忧患，死于安乐」——孟昶之亡，非亡于宋之强，而亡于「佚乐」二字。后蜀之降，为十国覆亡之序曲：此后南汉、南唐、吴越相继入宋。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷064《后蜀世家》、宋史卷479《西蜀孟氏》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Meng Chang, third son of Meng Zhixiang, took the throne in the 1st year of Mingde (934) at sixteen. Thirty-one years he reigned — among the longest of the Ten Kingdoms: Shu "at peace," and Chang, a lover of letters, feasting and writing verses with his Consort Huarui; he had the stone classics of the *Analects* and the *Erya* cut in the Chengdu academy — the culture of Later Shu "not behind the Central Plains."

But "long peace bred ease and pleasure": in his last years he "grew luxurious and idle," trusting the incapable Wang Zhaoyuan, "the army and the government unrepaired." In the 3rd year of Qiande (965) Emperor Taizu of Song sent Wang Quanbin to invade; the Song army came through the Jianmen Pass, Meng Chang surrendered, and Later Shu was no more — thirty-two years from Zhixiang's title, two rulers. Brought to Kaifeng, he was made Duke of Qin and died that same year.

The histories say: "he lost the realm to ease and pleasure." Later Shu held the shield of the two Chuan and the wealth of the heavenly prefecture, "the spring of the Jinjiang"; but "born in ease, dead in ease" — Chang fell not to Song's strength but to the two words "ease and pleasure." His fall began the closing of the Ten: Southern Han, Southern Tang, and Wuyue followed into Song.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 64 ("Annals of Later Shu"), and the *Songshi*, ch. 479 (the Meng of Xishu) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 南平武信王 · 主要事迹

高季兴，陕州硖石人，本为汴州富人李让之仆，后事朱温，以军功起家。开平元年（907），后梁以季兴为荆南节度使，镇江陵——荆南（南平）国之始。同光二年（924），后唐封季兴为南平王。

南平据江陵弹丸之地，「地狭兵寡」，为十国中最弱者；季兴以「事大」为生：梁、唐、晋、汉、周五代更迭，季兴父子「随所胜者而臣之」，又拦截诸国商贾，「诸国商贾过境，无不抽税」，史称「高赖子」——十国之讥，莫此为甚。

天成三年（928），季兴卒。南平虽弱小无足道，然其「赖事大以存」，历高氏五主四十余年，至 963 年为宋所灭——「高赖子」之讥虽刻，然「苟全性命于乱世」，亦有其生存之道。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷069《南平世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷069《南平世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Gao Jixing, a man of Xiashi in Shanzhou, began as a servant of a rich man of Bianzhou, then served Zhu Wen and rose by merit. In the 1st year of Kaiping (907) Later Liang made him military governor of Jingnan, holding Jiangling — the beginning of Jingnan (Nanping). In the 2nd year of Tongguang (924) Later Tang made him King of Nanping.

Nanping held the sliver of Jiangling, "the land narrow and the soldiers few," the weakest of the Ten Kingdoms; Jixing lived by "serving the great": through Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, and Zhou he and his sons "served whichever won," and they stopped the merchants of every state, "taxing all the merchants who passed" — the histories call him the "Gao rascal," the mockery of the age at its sharpest.

He died in the 3rd year of Tiancheng (928). Small and contemptible as Nanping was, "it lived by serving the great," through five Gao rulers and over forty years, until Song destroyed it in 963 — the "Gao rascal" mocked, yet "keeping whole one's life amid the storm" had its own way.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 69 ("Annals of Nanping") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 北汉世祖 · 主要事迹

刘崇（后改名刘旻），后汉高祖刘知远之弟，河东节度使。乾祐四年（951），郭威代汉建周，刘崇于太原称帝，国号汉（史称北汉），沿用乾祐年号——后汉之余绪，退守河东一隅。

北汉地狭兵弱，刘崇「借契丹以拒周宋」：自称「侄皇帝」于契丹，岁贡金帛，求援自保。乾祐七年（954），周世宗新立，刘崇以为有机可乘，联契丹大举攻周；高平之战，周世宗亲临督战，北汉军大败，「契丹之兵，不战而走」——刘崇仅以身免，逃回太原，旋忧愤而卒，年六十。

史评刘崇：「借契丹以拒周宋。」北汉之立，为五代十国中之「孤岛」：其北倚契丹、南拒周宋，苟存二十八年（至 979 年宋太宗灭之）。刘崇以「汉室宗亲」之名抗周，然其「儿皇帝」石敬瑭之续——「借外力以自固，终为外力所制」。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷070《东汉世家》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Chong, later renamed Liu Min, was the younger brother of Liu Zhiyuan, the Gaozu of Later Han, and governor of Hedong. In the 4th year of Qianyou (951), when Guo Wei took the Zhou throne from Han, Chong took the throne at Taiyuan as the realm Han (Northern Han to history), keeping the Qianyou era — the remnant of Later Han, holding the one corner of Hedong.

Northern Han was narrow and weak, and Chong "borrowed the Khitan to hold out against Zhou and Song": he called himself the Khitan's "nephew emperor," paying yearly tribute for support. In the 7th year of Qianyou (954), judging the new Shizong of Zhou an easy mark, he attacked Zhou in force with the Khitan; at Gaoping, with Shizong urging his army in person, the Northern Han host was shattered — "the Khitan horsemen fled without a fight." Chong escaped with his life alone, fled back to Taiyuan, and died of grief and rage, aged sixty.

The histories say: "he borrowed the Khitan to hold out against Zhou and Song." Northern Han was an island of the age: leaning on the Khitan in the north, defying Zhou and Song in the south, it lingered twenty-eight years (until Taizong of Song destroyed it in 979). Chong, "a scion of the Han house" defying Zhou, was yet the successor of the "son emperor" Shi Jingtang — "borrowing the outsider to stand, in the end bound by the outsider."

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 70 ("Annals of the Eastern Han") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 北汉睿宗 · 主要事迹

刘钧（原名刘承钧），刘崇次子。乾祐七年（954），刘崇高平之败后卒，钧即位。北汉自高平战后，精锐尽丧，钧「事辽益恭」：岁贡契丹，换取辽之支援；又「以刘氏宗室自任」，与后周、北宋相抗。

宋太祖立国后，屡攻太原：开宝年间，宋军数围太原，北汉倚辽之援，坚守不破——「太原之城，天下之坚」。天会十二年（968），刘钧卒，年约四十三；养子刘继恩、刘继元相继，国祚延至太平兴国四年（979），宋太宗亲征，辽援不至，北汉降，五代十国之局终。

史评刘钧：「能守而不能拓。」北汉以河东弹丸之地，抗周、宋三十余年，赖「太原之坚」与契丹之援；然「北汉之存，存于宋辽之对峙」——宋太宗灭北汉后即攻辽，「北汉既灭，宋辽之争始」。刘钧之守成，虽无功业，然北汉之顽强，为五代之尾声。

> 本地参考：点校本《新五代史》卷070《东汉世家》、宋史卷482《北汉刘氏》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Jun, originally Liu Chengjun, was the second son of Liu Chong. After Chong's death following the Gaoping defeat in the 7th year of Qianyou (954), Jun took the throne. With the elite of Northern Han spent at Gaoping, Jun "served Liao ever more humbly": yearly tribute to the Khitan for support; and, "holding himself a scion of the Liu house," he defied Later Zhou and Song.

After the Song founder took the throne, the Song armies attacked Taiyuan again and again: in the Kaibao years they besieged it several times, and Northern Han, leaning on Liao's aid, held — "the city of Taiyuan, the strongest under heaven." Jun died in the 12th year of Tianhui (968), around forty-three; his adopted sons Ji'en and Jiyuan followed, and the realm lingered until the 4th year of Taiping Xingguo (979), when Taizong of Song campaigned in person, the Liao relief failed, and Northern Han surrendered — the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms were at an end.

The histories say: "he could hold, but not extend." Northern Han defied Zhou and Song for over thirty years on the sliver of Hedong, by the strength of Taiyuan and the Liao alliance; but "Northern Han lived on the standoff of Song and Liao" — and with its fall the Song–Liao struggle began in earnest. Jun's stewardship, though without glory, was the stubborn tail of the Five Dynasties.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 70 ("Annals of the Eastern Han"), and the *Songshi*, ch. 482 (the Liu of Northern Han) (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 隋文帝 · 主要事迹

杨坚以受禅方式代北周建隋，改元开皇。新朝初立，一面以政治手段清除北周宗室隐患、稳住局面，一面营迁大兴城，重定都城格局——开国的前几步，走得谨慎而彻底。

开皇七年，江陵后梁亡，南进之门洞开；开皇九年平陈，自东晋以来近三百年的南北分裂宣告结束，史称「混一戎夏」。次年江南反隋势力被平定，统一局面真正巩固。灭陈一役虽由诸将执行，战略决断皆出朝廷。

混一之外，开皇间三省六部成型、统一货币度量、检括户口，奠定此后数百年的政制底盘，后效极高。论文治的制度遗产，隋文帝在历代开国之主中位置很靠前。

晚年却是另一番走向：开皇二十年废太子勇、改立晋王广，储位之争自此埋下国祚风险。仁寿四年，文帝崩于仁寿宫，遗命与继位过程史有异说。其子[[sui-yang|隋炀帝]]即位，统一遗产与二世风险同时交接——废立争议与「二世而亡」的结局，压低了后世对这场开国之局的评价。与[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]对读：二者皆在长期分裂后完成混一，又皆在二代迅速陷入危局，是读统一帝国史绕不开的一对对照。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yang Jian replaced Northern Zhou and founded the Sui through an abdication, changing the era name to Kaihuang. With the new dynasty just established, he used political means to remove the lingering threat of the Northern Zhou royal house and steady the situation, while building and moving to Daxing and redesigning the capital's layout — the founding's first steps were taken with caution and thoroughness.

In Kaihuang 7, the Later Liang at Jiangling fell and the gate to the southern advance swung open; in Kaihuang 9 Chen was pacified, ending the nearly three-hundred-year division of north and south since the Eastern Jin — known in history as "the unification of the realm". The following year the anti-Sui forces in Jiangnan were suppressed, and the unified order was truly consolidated. Though the destruction of Chen was executed by his generals, every strategic decision came from the court.

Beyond unification, the Kaihuang era saw the Three Departments and Six Ministries take shape, currency and weights and measures unified, and households registered and checked — laying the institutional foundation of government for centuries to come, with exceptionally far-reaching aftereffects. In terms of institutional legacy, Emperor Wen ranks near the very front among the founding rulers of successive dynasties.

His later years took a different course: in Kaihuang 20 he deposed Crown Prince Yang Yong and installed the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, in his place — and the struggle over the succession thereafter planted a risk to the dynasty's fortunes. In Renshou 4, Emperor Wen died at Renshou Palace; the historical record diverges on his dying orders and the succession process. His son

took the throne, and the legacy of unification was handed over together with the risk of a second-generation collapse — the controversy over the change of heir and the ending of "falling in the second generation" lowered later generations' appraisal of this founding. Read alongside
: both completed reunification after long division, and both quickly plunged into crisis in the second generation — an unavoidable pair for anyone reading the history of unified empires.

emperors.bio_md:
# 隋炀帝 · 主要事迹

杨广本为晋王，开皇九年（589）参与平陈立功，开皇二十年（600）被立为太子，仁寿四年（604）即帝位，后改元大业。本页以《隋书·炀帝纪》为年表主线，辅以《资治通鉴·隋纪》编年对照。

大业年间他接连启动超大规模的工程与行动：大业元年（605）营建东都洛阳，开通济渠等运河段，贯通南北水运；大业四年（608）又开永济渠北通涿郡；大业五年（609）西巡张掖，西域胡商前来朝会，一时呈现盛世表象。东都与运河构成他最重要的后效遗产，但征发之巨也同步消耗着帝国的根本。

转折出现在大业八年（612）一征高句丽：大举东征，丧师费财，国内矛盾激化。次年（613）再征辽东，杨玄感起兵，崩坏加速。大业十二年（616）他三幸江都，中原随之失控；大业十三年（617）群雄并起，中枢名存实亡；大业十四年（618），宇文化及等发动江都之变，炀帝身死，隋亡。

后世对他月旦极低，而运河、东都与沟通南北的后效深远。与[[sui-wen|隋文帝]]对读，可见开皇一朝的积累如何在大业年间被推向极致并耗尽；与[[tang-tai-zong|唐太宗]]对读，可见唐承隋制的承接与反拨。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yang Guang was originally the Prince of Jin. In Kaihuang 9 (589) he took part in the pacification of Chen and earned merit; in Kaihuang 20 (600) he was made crown prince; in Renshou 4 (604) he ascended the throne, later changing the era name to Daye. This page follows the Annals of Emperor Yang in the Book of Sui as its chronological spine, cross-checked against the Sui chapters of the Zizhi Tongjian.

During the Daye era he launched one outsized project and operation after another: in Daye 1 (605) he built the Eastern Capital at Luoyang and dug the Tongji Canal and other canal sections, linking north-south water transport; in Daye 4 (608) he dug the Yongji Canal, reaching Zhuo Commandery in the north; in Daye 5 (609) he toured west to Zhangye, where Hu merchants from the Western Regions came to court, presenting for a time the appearance of a flourishing age. The Eastern Capital and the canals form his most important lasting legacy, yet the sheer scale of conscription was simultaneously consuming the empire's foundations.

The turning point came in Daye 8 (612) with the first campaign against Goguryeo: a massive eastern expedition that lost armies and drained wealth, intensifying domestic tensions. The following year (613) he campaigned in Liaodong again, and Yang Xuangan rose in revolt, accelerating the collapse. In Daye 12 (616) he went to Jiangdu for the third time, and the Central Plains slipped from control; in Daye 13 (617) warlords rose on all sides and the central authority existed in name only; in Daye 14 (618), Yuwen Huaji and others launched the Jiangdu coup, Emperor Yang was killed, and the Sui fell.

Later generations judged him extremely harshly, yet the lasting effects of the canals, the Eastern Capital, and the linking of north and south run deep. Read alongside
, one can see how the accumulation of the Kaihuang era was pushed to the extreme and exhausted during the Daye years; read alongside
, one can see how the Tang both inherited and reacted against Sui institutions.

emperors.bio_md:
# 隋恭帝 · 主要事迹

杨侑，元德太子杨昭之子，炀帝之孙。大业十三年，李渊太原起兵西进，克长安，立侑为帝，改元义宁，遥尊江都之炀帝为太上皇——隋之实权，已在李渊之手。时东都洛阳，越王杨侗亦被王世充等立为帝，史称皇泰主：隋室二帝并立，皆权臣掌中之物。

义宁二年三月，炀帝在江都为宇文化及所弑；五月，李渊受禅称帝，国号唐，杨侑逊位，封鄜国公。武德二年，杨侑薨，年十五——隋自文帝开皇建国，历三帝三十八年而亡。

恭帝之立、之禅、之薨，皆身不由己：以幼冲之君，当隋末大乱，为李渊「挟天子以令诸侯」之工具。史家论隋之亡：亡于炀帝之暴政与征伐，恭帝不过承其祸而已。图鉴以其名分存于隋统而列为准帝。隋亡而唐兴，中国历史进入大唐三百年之局。

> 本地参考：点校本《隋书》卷005《恭帝纪》、旧唐书卷001《高祖纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yang You, son of the Crown Prince Zhao, was a grandson of Emperor Yang. In the 13th year of Daye, Li Yuan, risen at Taiyuan and marching west, took Chang'an and set up You, changing the era to Yining and honoring Emperor Yang at Jiangdu as Grand Emperor from afar — the real power of Sui was already Li Yuan's. At the eastern capital, the Prince of Yue, Yang Tong, was in turn set up by Wang Shichong and the others as the "Huangtai Sovereign": two emperors of Sui at once, both toys of strong ministers.

In the third month of the 2nd year of Yining, Emperor Yang was slain at Jiangdu by Yuwen Huaji; in the fifth month Li Yuan received the abdication and founded Tang, and You, made Duke of Fu, stepped down. In the 2nd year of Wude he died, aged fifteen — Sui, thirty-eight years from Wen's founding, was no more.

His enthronement, his abdication, and his death were none of his choosing: a child on the throne in the great chaos, the instrument of Li Yuan's "holding the emperor to command the lords." The historians say Sui fell to Emperor Yang's tyranny and his wars; Gong only inherited the disaster. The gazetteer keeps him in the Sui line as quasi-emperor. Sui fell and Tang rose, and the three hundred years of the Tang opened.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Suishu*, ch. 5 ("Benji of Emperor Gong"), and the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 1 ("Benji of Emperor Gaozu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

After the Xuanwu Gate incident he yielded the throne to Emperor Taizong and styled himself Grand Emperor.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐高祖 · 主要事迹

李渊字叔德，陇西成纪人，唐国公李昞之子。出身北周关陇贵族，「七岁袭封唐国公」，隋末为太原留守。大业十三年，天下大乱，渊在次子李世民等推动下太原起兵，西向关中；克长安后，立代王杨侑为帝，自为大丞相、唐王——「挟天子以令诸侯」，隋之实权尽归李氏。

武德元年，恭帝禅位，李渊即皇帝位，国号唐，改元武德，定都长安。武德年间，唐室平定群雄：武德四年，李世民破王世充、窦建德于洛阳，河南河北粗定；其后又平刘黑闼、萧铣、辅公祏等，天下渐归一统。李渊立国规模：定租庸调制、均田制、府兵制，皆武德年间草创。

武德九年，玄武门之变，李世民杀太子建成、齐王元吉，李渊被迫传位世民，自称太上皇。贞观九年，李渊崩于太安宫，年七十。史评高祖：「草创唐室，定都关中」；然「优柔寡断，传位事与玄武门相联」。大唐三百年基业，实自高祖之武德创之；而其让位太宗，亦成贞观之治之始。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷001《高祖纪》、新唐书卷001《高祖纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

武德九年，玄武门之变，李世民杀太子建成、齐王元吉，李渊被迫传位世民，自称太上皇。贞观九年，李渊崩于太安宫，年七十。史评高祖：「草创唐室，定都关中」；然「优柔寡断，传位事与玄武门相联」。大唐三百年基业，实自高祖之武德创之；而其让位太宗，亦成贞观之治之始。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷001《高祖纪》、新唐书卷001《高祖纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Yuan, styled Shude, was a man of Chengji in Longxi, son of the Duke of Tang, Li Bing. Of the Guanzhong aristocracy of Northern Zhou, he "succeeded to the dukedom at seven," and in the last years of Sui held Taiyuan. In the 13th year of Daye, with the realm in chaos, Yuan rose at Taiyuan — urged on by his second son Shimin and the others — and turned west toward Guanzhong; taking Chang'an, he set up the Prince of Dai, Yang You, as emperor, and made himself grand chancellor and King of Tang — "holding the emperor to command the lords," the power of Sui passing to the Li house.

In the 1st year of Wude, Emperor Gong abdicated; Yuan took the throne, styled the realm Tang, changed the era, and fixed his capital at Chang'an. The Wude years pacified the heroes: in the 4th year Shimin broke Wang Shichong and Dou Jiande at Luoyang, and Henan and Hebei were roughly settled; Liu Heita, Xiao Xian, Fu Gongshi, and the rest fell in turn, and the realm drew toward unity. The institutions of the Tang — the equal-field and tax systems, the garrison system — were roughed out in the Wude years.

In the 9th year of Wude came the Xuanwu Gate: Shimin slew the heir Jiancheng and the Prince of Qi, Yuanji, and Yuan, compelled, yielded the throne to Shimin, styling himself Grand Emperor. He died in the Tai'an Palace in the 9th year of Zhenguan, aged seventy. The histories say he "founded the Tang house with its capital in Guanzhong," yet "irresolute, his yielding of the throne bound up with the Xuanwu Gate." The three hundred years of Tang were laid open by Gaozu's Wude; and his yielding made Taizong's reign possible.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 1 ("Benji of Emperor Gaozu"), and the *Xin Tangshu*, ch. 1 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐高宗 · 主要事迹

李治字为善，太宗第九子，长孙皇后所生。贞观二十三年太宗崩，治即位，改元永徽。永徽年间，承贞观之遗风：「永徽之治，政尚宽简」，长孙无忌、褚遂良等辅政，法制修明，《永徽律》颁行——为唐律之代表作。

永徽六年，废王皇后，立武昭仪为皇后——「废王立武」一事，为唐室政局之大转折：自此武后渐预朝政，高宗之权日削。显庆五年，高宗「苦风眩」，百司奏事，或令武后参决，「天下大权，悉归中宫」。然高宗之世武功仍盛：显庆二年灭西突厥，总章元年李勣平高丽，置安东都护府——唐之疆域，至高宗时最为辽阔。

弘道元年，高宗崩于东都贞观殿，年五十六。史评高宗：「永徽有贞观遗风；中年以后，政归武后。」高宗仁弱，然承贞观之基、开武后之局：其朝为唐由盛转「周」之枢纽。武周之兴，虽武后之野心，亦高宗之委政有以成之。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷004、005《高宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Zhi, styled Weishan, was the ninth son of Taizong by Empress Zhangsun. On Taizong's death in the 23rd year of Zhenguan he took the throne, changing the era to Yonghui. The Yonghui years carried on the Zhenguan legacy: "the government of Yonghui favored leniency and simplicity," with Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, and the others as regents and the law in good order — the *Yonghui Code* was issued, the masterpiece of Tang law.

In the 6th year of Yonghui he deposed Empress Wang and made the Consort Wu his empress — the "deposition for Wu" was the great turn of the Tang court: from that day Wu entered the government, and the emperor's power ebbed. In the 5th year of Xianqing, plagued by vertigo, he had the offices report to Wu for decision, "all the power of the realm passing to the inner palace." Yet the arms of his reign were strong: in the 2nd year of Xianqing the Western Turks were destroyed, and in the 1st year of Zongzhang Li Ji subdued Goguryeo, setting up the Protectorate of Andong — the widest borders of Tang came in Gaozong's reign.

He died in the Zhenguan Hall at the eastern capital in the 1st year of Hongdao, aged fifty-six. The histories say: "Yonghui carried the Zhenguan air; after his middle years the government passed to Empress Wu." Gentle and weak, he inherited the Zhenguan foundations and opened the way for Wu: his reign was the hinge from Tang to the Zhou — the rise of the Wu Zhou was Wu's ambition, but also the fruit of his delegation.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 4 and 5 ("Benji of Emperor Gaozong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐中宗（首次） · 主要事迹

李显（后改名哲），高宗第七子，武后所生。弘道元年高宗崩，显即位，改元嗣圣——其在位仅五十五日。中宗欲以皇后之父韦玄贞为侍中，又欲授韦玄贞之父韦玄贞以刺史之官（一说欲以韦后之父为侍中），武后以「天下者，武氏之天下」为由，废中宗为庐陵王，迁于房州。

被废后，中宗在房州「备尝艰险」，「每闻敕使至，辄惶恐欲自杀」，其妻韦氏劝之：「祸福倚伏，何常之有！」圣历元年，武后立储之议，召还中宗，复立为皇太子——「自房州还」，为神龙复位之张本。武周之世，中宗以太子之位居东都，战战兢兢。

中宗首次在位月余而废，史评：「在位月余，权在武后。」武后以母临朝、以帝废立，开中国唯一女帝之局；而中宗之废立，正为武周之过渡。其复位之事，见「唐中宗（复位）」之纪。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷007《中宗纪》、卷006《则天皇后纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Xian, later renamed Zhe, was the seventh son of Gaozong by Empress Wu. On Gaozong's death in the 1st year of Hongdao he took the throne, changing the era to Sisheng — his reign lasted fifty-five days. Seeking to make his wife's father Wei Xuanzhen chamberlain, he was deposed by Wu as Prince of Luling and moved to Fangzhou, Wu declaring "the realm belongs to the Wu house."

In exile at Fangzhou he "tasted every peril," and "at every edict-bearer's coming he would start and think of suicide," until his wife Wei comforted him: "fortune and misfortune lean on each other — what is constant?" In the 1st year of Shengli, in the matter of the succession, Wu recalled him and made him crown prince again — the return from Fangzhou, the prelude to the restoration. Through the Wu Zhou years he sat at the eastern capital as heir, in constant fear.

A month on the throne and deposed, the histories say: "a month in office, the power with Empress Wu." Wu, a mother holding court and deposing emperors, opened the way to the only female sovereign of China; and Zhongzong's deposition was the transition to the Zhou. His restoration is recorded under "Emperor Zhongzong of Tang (Restored)."

# 唐睿宗（首次） · 主要事迹

李旦（初名旭轮），高宗第八子，武后所生。嗣圣元年，中宗被废，武后立豫王旦为帝，改元文明——睿宗首次在位。睿宗「恭俭退让」，即位时「政事皆决于武后」，帝拱手而已；光宅元年，徐敬业起兵扬州讨武，旋败——武后之权威，由此益固。

垂拱、永昌、载初年间，武后渐行禅代之实：载初元年，武后称帝，改国号周，睿宗降为皇嗣，赐姓武氏——「降为皇嗣」，唐之帝统中断，武周之局成。睿宗首次在位六年，实为武后临朝之过渡：其名分虽存唐统，然「傀儡皇帝，身当武周前夜」。

睿宗之让位与降为皇嗣，皆身不由己；然其恭默退让，得以保全。唐隆政变后睿宗复位之事，见「唐睿宗（复位）」之纪。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷007《睿宗纪》、卷006《则天皇后纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Dan, first named Xulun, was the eighth son of Gaozong by Empress Wu. After Zhongzong's deposition in the 1st year of Sisheng, Wu set up the Prince of Yu, Dan, changing the era to Wenming — Ruizong's first reign. Dan was "frugal and yielding": on the throne "every matter was decided by Empress Wu," and the emperor folded his hands; in the 1st year of Guangzhai, Xu Jingye rose at Yangzhou against Wu and was soon destroyed — Wu's authority was fixed.

Through the Chuigong, Yongchang, and Zaichu years Wu moved toward the reality of abdication: in the 1st year of Zaichu she took the throne, renamed the realm Zhou, and Dan was reduced to heir of the line, given the surname Wu — "reduced to heir," the Tang imperial line interrupted and the Zhou established. Six years of his first reign, in truth the transition of Wu's regency: in name he held the Tang line, but "a puppet emperor on the eve of the Wu Zhou."

His enthronement and his reduction were none of his choosing; his quiet yielding kept him safe. His restoration after the Tanglong coup is recorded under "Emperor Ruizong of Tang (Restored)."

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 7 ("Benji of Emperor Ruizong"), ch. 6 ("Benji of Empress Zetian") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 武则天 · 主要事迹

武则天是中国史上唯一正式称帝的女皇帝。本页以《旧唐书·则天皇后本纪》为年表主线，辅以《新唐书》与《资治通鉴·唐纪》编年（本地参考库已备）。她贞观十一年入宫为[[tang-tai-zong|唐太宗]]才人，历感业寺环节后重返宫廷，永徽六年由昭仪立为皇后——废王立武之争中，长孙无忌等元老反对派相继贬死，她由此进入权力中枢。

显庆五年后高宗多病，天后参决政务，朝中形成"二圣"格局。弘道元年高宗崩于洛阳，中宗即位，她临朝称制；次年即废中宗为庐陵王，改立睿宗而实掌朝政。垂拱四年洛阳明堂建成，铜匦告密与酷吏政治并行，恩威双轨的统治术于此成型。

天授元年，她在神都洛阳加尊号、改国号为周，正式称帝，女主称制由事实变为名分。在位期间破格用人、发展科举殿试，神功元年狄仁杰入相成为能吏政治的代表节点；文治实绩与酷吏之治始终并存，构成武周的一体两面。

神龙元年，张柬之等发动政变拥中宗复位，武周终结，则天迁宫。旧史多以"女祸"叙事贬抑，今人则更重估其制度与人事遗产——本图鉴月旦中性偏下，留给读者对读：从入宫才人到革唐为周，再到还政李唐，与[[tang-xian-zong|唐宪宗]]的中兴对照，可见唐室中衰与重建的完整弧线。

bio_parts_en.value: Wu Zetian is the only woman in Chinese history to have formally taken the imperial title. This page builds its chronology on the "Basic Annals of Empress Zetian" in the Old Book of Tang, supplemented by the New Book of Tang and the Tang chronicle of the Zizhi Tongjian (all held in the local reference library). She entered the palace in Zhenguan 11 as a cairen consort of

and, after the Ganye Temple episode, returned to the court; in Yonghui 6 she was raised from zhaoyi to empress. In the struggle over deposing Empress Wang for Wu, veteran opponents such as Zhangsun Wuji were demoted and died one after another, and through this she entered the center of power.

After Xianqing 5, as Gaozong fell frequently ill, the Heavenly Empress joined in deciding state affairs and a "Two Sages" arrangement took shape at court. In Hongdao 1 Gaozong died in Luoyang; Zhongzong succeeded and she ruled from behind the screen. The very next year she deposed Zhongzong to Prince of Luling, installed Ruizong instead, and held real power over the court. In Chuigong 4 the Bright Hall in Luoyang was completed, while copper-box informant reports and the politics of harsh officials ran in tandem: her dual-track statecraft of favor and fear took form here.

In Tianshou 1, at the Divine Capital Luoyang, she took a new honorific title, changed the dynastic name to Zhou, and formally assumed the throne; rule by a female sovereign passed from fact into name. During her reign she broke conventions in appointing talent and developed the palace examination within the imperial examinations, and in Shengong 1 Di Renjie's entry as chancellor became the representative node of capable-official politics. Solid civil achievements and the rule of harsh officials coexisted throughout, forming the two faces of Wu Zhou.

In Shenlong 1, Zhang Jianzhi and others launched a coup that restored Zhongzong; Wu Zhou ended and Zetian moved to another palace. The old histories mostly belittled her through the "female calamity" narrative, while today her institutional and personnel legacy is being revalued. This atlas's appraisal is neutral to mildly negative, left for readers to weigh against the evidence: from palace cairen to changing Tang into Zhou and then returning power to the Li Tang house, read alongside the restoration of
, one can see the full arc of the Tang house's mid-course decline and rebuilding.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐中宗（复位） · 主要事迹

李显，神龙元年复位。武后晚年，张柬之、崔玄暐、敬晖、桓彦范、袁恕己等五人发动神龙政变，逼武后退位，迎中宗复位，复国号唐——武周十五年之局，至此而终。中宗复位后，上武后尊号为「则天大圣皇帝」，武后旋崩；中宗还都长安。

然中宗「复位而不能振」：武三思等武氏余党用事，勾结韦后；安乐公主「卖官鬻爵，斜封授官」，政纲紊乱。景龙元年，太子李重俊（节愍太子）起兵，杀武三思，旋败死。中宗在位五年，政事一决于韦后，「天下怨之」。

景龙四年六月，中宗暴崩于神龙殿，年五十五——史多以为韦后与安乐公主毒杀。韦后临朝，立温王李重茂（殇帝）；月余，李隆基发动唐隆政变，诛韦后，唐室复归于睿宗、玄宗。中宗两度在位，皆不能自振：首次为武后所废，复位为韦后所制——唐室中衰，自中宗始。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷007《中宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Xian, restored in the 1st year of Shenlong. In Empress Wu's last years, Zhang Jianzhi, Cui Xuanwei, Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and Yuan Shuji staged the Shenlong coup, forced Wu to abdicate, and restored Zhongzong; the realm reverted to Tang — the fifteen years of the Wu Zhou were at an end. He honored Wu as "Grand Saintly Emperor Zetian," and she died soon after; the capital returned to Chang'an.

But he was "restored and unable to revive the court": the Wu remnants like Wu Sansi held power, linking with Empress Wei; the Princess Anle "sold offices by slanted letters," and the government fell into disorder. In the 1st year of Jinglong the heir Li Chongjun rose, slew Wu Sansi, and fell and died. Five years on the throne, every matter decided by Empress Wei — "the realm resented it."

In the sixth month of the 4th year of Jinglong Zhongzong died suddenly in the Shenlong Hall, aged fifty-five — the histories suspect Empress Wei and the Princess Anle of poison. Wei took the regency and set up the Prince of Wen, Li Chongmao (Emperor Shang); within a month Li Longji staged the Tanglong coup, slew Empress Wei, and the throne passed back to Ruizong and Xuanzong. Twice on the throne, twice unable to stand: deposed by Wu the first time, ruled by Wei the second — the decline of the Tang house began with Zhongzong.

# 唐殇帝 · 主要事迹

李重茂，中宗第四子，封温王。景龙四年六月，中宗暴崩，韦后临朝，立重茂为帝，改元唐隆——殇帝即位时年十六，为韦后掌中之傀儡。

同年六月二十日，临淄王李隆基（玄宗）与太平公主等发动唐隆政变，诛韦后及其党；政变之日，李隆基拥睿宗入宫，殇帝让位于叔父睿宗，退封温王。其后殇帝徙房州，开元二年（一说约开元二年）卒，年约二十——史或称「殇帝」「少帝」，新唐书以「殇帝」入本纪。

殇帝在位不足一月，史评：「幼冲傀儡，身当宫廷政变。」唐代宫廷政变之频繁，于中宗、殇帝之世为最：神龙政变、景龙之乱、唐隆政变，十余年间三变其局。殇帝不过其间一过渡人物；图鉴以其名分存于唐统而列为准帝。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷007《中宗纪》、新唐书卷004《中宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Chongmao, fourth son of Zhongzong, was enfeoffed Prince of Wen. In the sixth month of the 4th year of Jinglong, Zhongzong died suddenly; Empress Wei took the regency and set up Chongmao, changing the era to Tanglong — sixteen years old, the puppet of Wei.

That same day in the sixth month, the Prince of Linzi, Li Longji (Xuanzong), with the Princess Taiping and the others, staged the Tanglong coup and slew Empress Wei and her party; Ruizong was brought in, Chongmao yielded the throne to his uncle, and was reduced to Prince of Wen. Later moved to Fangzhou, he died around the 2nd year of Kaiyuan, about twenty — the histories call him Emperor Shang or the Young Emperor, and the *Xin Tangshu* gives him a benji.

Less than a month on the throne; the histories say: "a child puppet caught in the palace coup." The palace coups of the Tang came thickest in the Zhongzong–Shang years: the Shenlong coup, the Jinglong disorders, the Tanglong coup — three changes within a decade. Shang was but a passing figure; the gazetteer keeps him in the Tang line as quasi-emperor.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 7 ("Benji of Emperor Zhongzong"), and the *Xin Tangshu*, ch. 4 ("Benji of Emperor Zhongzong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐睿宗（复位） · 主要事迹

李旦，唐隆政变后复位。景云元年，李隆基诛韦后，拥睿宗复位，改元景云——睿宗第二次在位。复位之初，睿宗立平韦之功的隆基为皇太子；然政事又受制于太平公主（武后之女、睿宗之妹）：「公主所欲，上无不听」，睿宗「犹以公主故，未能自决」。

先天元年，睿宗传位太子隆基（玄宗），自称太上皇——「让位贤子」，为睿宗一生之亮点。然太平公主势炽，劝睿宗「不必传位」不成，遂谋废玄宗；先天二年，玄宗先发制人，赐死太平公主，太上皇完全归政。开元四年，睿宗崩于百福殿，年五十五。

史评睿宗复位：「能让位贤子，史有令名。」睿宗两度为帝，皆傀儡（武后、太平公主）；然其知子莫若父，决然传位隆基，遂有开元盛世。唐之转机，正在睿宗之让位——「知进退」三字，为其一生写照。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷007《睿宗纪》、卷008《玄宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Dan, restored after the Tanglong coup. In the 1st year of Jingyun, Li Longji slew Empress Wei and brought Ruizong back to the throne, changing the era to Jingyun — his second reign. At the restoration he made Longji, whose merit had put down Wei, crown prince; but the government fell again under the Princess Taiping (Wu's daughter, Ruizong's sister): "whatever the princess wished, the emperor granted," and he "could not decide for the princess's sake."

In the 1st year of Xiantian he yielded the throne to the heir Longji (Xuanzong) and styled himself Grand Emperor — "yielding to his worthy son," the one bright deed of his life. But the Princess Taiping's power was great; she had urged him not to abdicate, and now plotted against Xuanzong; in the 2nd year of Xiantian the emperor struck first, had the princess put to death, and the Grand Emperor gave up the government entirely. He died in the Baifu Hall in the 4th year of Kaiyuan, aged fifty-five.

The histories say of his restoration: "he yielded to his worthy son — a good name in history." Twice on the throne, twice a puppet (of Wu, of the princess); but he knew his son, and his yielding opened the Kaiyuan golden age. The turn of Tang was his abdication — "knowing when to withdraw" is the whole of his life.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 7 ("Benji of Emperor Ruizong"), ch. 8 ("Benji of Emperor Xuanzong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐玄宗 · 主要事迹

李隆基，睿宗第三子。唐隆元年，隆基与太平公主等发动唐隆政变，诛韦后，「唐室再造」之功，归于隆基；先天元年，睿宗传位，隆基即位；开元元年，赐死太平公主，改元开元，始真正亲政。

开元年间，玄宗励精图治：姚崇、宋璟、张说、张九龄等名相相继，「开元之治」，史称盛世——「忆昔开元全盛日，小邑犹藏万家室」（杜甫），唐之文治武功，于斯为极：府兵、均田、租庸调制度臻于完备，文化灿烂，万国来朝。

然天宝年间，玄宗渐骄：「恃承平日久，渐肆奢欲，怠于政事」，宠杨贵妃，「从此君王不早朝」；任李林甫、杨国忠为相，养安禄山于范阳。天宝十四载，安史之乱爆发，安禄山陷洛阳称帝；至德元载，潼关失守，玄宗幸蜀，马嵬兵变，赐死贵妃——「天长地久有时尽，此恨绵绵无绝期」。太子即位灵武（肃宗），尊玄宗为太上皇。

宝应元年，玄宗崩于神龙殿，年七十八。史评玄宗：「开元励精，天宝骄怠，一身盛衰。」以一人之身，兼盛世与乱世之始——开元天宝之盛，与安史之乱之衰，皆系于玄宗一身，为历代君主盛衰之最典型之鉴。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷008、009《玄宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Longji, third son of Ruizong. In the 1st year of Tanglong he staged the Tanglong coup with the Princess Taiping and the others, slaying Empress Wei — the "re-founding of the Tang house" was his work; in the 1st year of Xiantian Ruizong yielded the throne; in the 1st year of Kaiyuan he had the Princess Taiping put to death, changed the era, and ruled in truth.

The Kaiyuan years he governed with vigor: Yao Chong, Song Jing, Zhang Yue, Zhang Jiuling — chancellor after chancellor — and the "Kaiyuan recovery" the histories call a golden age: "Remember the full days of Kaiyuan, when even the little towns held ten thousand households" (Du Fu). The institutions of Tang — the garrisons, the equal fields, the tax system — stood complete; the culture shone, and the ten thousand states came to court.

But in the Tianbao years he grew complacent: "trusting the long peace, he gave himself to luxury and slackened in government," doted on Consort Yang — "from this sovereign the court was no longer held at dawn" — made Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong chancellors, and nursed An Lushan at Fanyang. In the 14th year of Tianbao the An–Shi rebellion broke; An Lushan took Luoyang and styled himself emperor. In the 1st year of Zhide Tongguan fell; the emperor fled to Shu; at Mawei the soldiers mutinied and the consort was put to death — "though heaven and earth have their ends, this regret has none." His heir took the throne at Lingwu (Suzong), honoring him as Grand Emperor.

He died in the Shenlong Hall in the 1st year of Baoying, aged seventy-eight. The histories say: "Kaiyuan diligent, Tianbao complacent — one life, a whole age's rise and fall." In one man met the golden age and the beginning of the ruin: the splendor of Kaiyuan–Tianbao and the disaster of the An–Shi rebellion were both his — the classic mirror of a sovereign's rise and fall.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐肃宗 · 主要事迹

李亨，玄宗第三子。天宝十五载（756）安史之乱中，玄宗幸蜀，太子亨在马嵬与玄宗分道，北上灵武，即皇帝位，改元至德，遥尊玄宗为太上皇——唐室中兴，自灵武始。肃宗以「平叛」为第一要务：至德二载，郭子仪、李光弼等借回纥之兵，收复长安、洛阳两京；然「借兵回纥，遗患无穷」，回纥之骄横，为后日之祸。

乾元元年，肃宗以九节度使围安庆绪于邺城，诸军无统帅，相州一役大溃，史思明乘势再起、杀安庆绪，安史之乱复炽。上元、宝应之际，肃宗病笃，张皇后与李辅国争权，宫闱之乱未已；宝应元年，肃宗崩于长生殿，年五十二。

史评肃宗：「艰难即位，两京虽复而河北未靖。」肃宗以太子之身，于乱中即位，其功在「再造唐室」；然用李辅国、张后，宦官之祸自此始盛；河北藩镇割据之局，亦成于其朝——安史之乱虽平，而唐室之衰，不可复振。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷010《肃宗纪》、资治通鉴卷218-222（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Heng, third son of Xuanzong. In the 1st year of Zhide (756), in the An–Shi rebellion, Xuanzong fled to Shu; the heir Heng, parting from Xuanzong at Mawei, went north and took the throne at Lingwu, changing the era to Zhide and honoring Xuanzong as Grand Emperor from afar — the restoration of the Tang began at Lingwu. Suzong's first task was the rebellion: in the 2nd year of Zhide Guo Ziyi, Li Guangbi, and the others, with the Uyghur cavalry, recovered the two capitals; but "borrowing the Uyghurs left a lasting plague," and the Uyghurs' arrogance was a disaster to come.

In the 1st year of Qianyuan he sent nine commissioners to besiege An Qingxu at Ye; without a supreme commander, the host was routed at Xiangzhou, and Shi Siming rose again, slew Qingxu, and the rebellion flared anew. In the Shangyuan and Baoying years Suzong lay ill while Empress Zhang and Li Fuguo contended — the palace disorders unended; he died in the Changsheng Hall in the 1st year of Baoying, aged fifty-two.

The histories say: "a hard-won throne: the two capitals recovered, but Hebei unquiet." Suzong, a heir enthroned in the storm, restored the Tang house; but his use of Li Fuguo and Empress Zhang opened the age of eunuch power, and the feudatory division of Hebei was fixed in his reign — the rebellion ended, but the decline of Tang could not be reversed.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 10 ("Benji of Emperor Suzong"), and the *Zizhi Tongjian*, ch. 218–222 (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐代宗 · 主要事迹

李豫（初名俶），肃宗长子。宝应元年肃宗崩，豫即位。代宗即位之初，安史之乱将平：宝应元年，其子雍王适（德宗）为天下兵马元帅，与仆固怀恩等讨史朝义，安史之乱历时八年，至此大致结束。然怀恩「养寇自重」，河北降将田承嗣等仍据藩镇，割据之局自此成。

代宗之世，外患频仍：广德元年，吐蕃入长安，代宗幸陕州，郭子仪以数千骑收复京师；永泰元年，仆固怀恩引回纥、吐蕃入寇，郭子仪单骑见回纥可汗，盟而退兵——「子仪之忠勇，唐室之干城」。然代宗好佛，「群臣承风，皆言报应」，佛教之盛、元载之专权，皆为史家所讥。

大历十四年，代宗崩，年五十三。史评代宗：「平乱守成，而藩镇坐大。」代宗朝为安史之乱后之过渡：武功赖郭子仪等，而「藩镇之祸、宦官之权、佛寺之费」，皆其朝所积——唐之中衰，自代宗而渐显。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷011《代宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Yu, first named Chu, was the eldest son of Suzong. On Suzong's death in the 1st year of Baoying he took the throne. The rebellion was ending: in that same year his son, the Prince of Yong, Kuo (Dezong), as supreme commander, with Pugu Huaien and the others, destroyed Shi Chaoyi — the eight-year An–Shi rebellion was roughly over. But Huaien "nourished the rebels to keep himself in power," and the surrendered generals of Hebei, Tian Chengsi and the rest, kept their garrisons: the feudatory division was fixed.

His reign was full of external troubles: in the 1st year of Guangde the Tibetans entered Chang'an and the emperor fled to Shan, Guo Ziyi recovering the capital with a few thousand riders; in the 1st year of Yongtai Pugu Huaien drew in the Uyghurs and Tibetans, and Guo Ziyi rode alone to the Uyghur khan, made peace, and the invaders withdrew — "Ziyi's loyalty and valor were the shield of the Tang." But Daizong doted on Buddhism, "the courtiers following the wind, all speaking of retribution," and the monks' estates and Yuan Zai's tyranny drew the historians' censure.

He died in the 14th year of Dali, aged fifty-three. The histories say: "he ended the rebellion and held the realm, while the feudatories grew great." His reign was the transition after the An–Shi storm: the arms were Guo Ziyi's and the rest, and the feudatories, the eunuchs, and the monasteries all gathered strength in his years — the decline of Tang became visible under Daizong.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 11 ("Benji of Emperor Daizong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐德宗 · 主要事迹

李适，代宗长子。大历十四年即位，改元建中。德宗初政，锐意有为：建中元年，用杨炎议行两税法——以「量出制入」定税额，分夏秋两征，税制之大变革，行用至明；又欲削藩，裁抑藩镇。建中二年，成德、魏博、淄青诸镇连兵抗命，唐廷讨伐失利。

建中四年，泾原兵变：泾原军过长安，因无犒赏而哗变，拥朱泚为主，朱泚据长安称帝。德宗仓皇出奔奉天，史称「奉天之难」；朱泚围奉天月余，赖浑瑊等坚守。兴元元年，德宗下罪己诏，「朕实不德，以至此祸」，天下感动，李晟收复长安，朱泚败死。然「削藩之志，自此而挫」。

贞元年间，德宗「猜忌日甚，聚敛愈急」，宦官掌禁军（神策军）之制自其朝始，宫市之弊、进奉之陋，皆为其政。贞元二十一年，德宗崩，年六十四。史评德宗：「初欲削藩，中遭播迁，晚多猜忌聚敛。」两税法与奉天之难，皆其朝之大事——唐由「盛」入「衰」之过渡，德宗实为关键。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷012、013《德宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Kuo, eldest son of Daizong, took the throne in the 14th year of Dali, changing the era to Jianzhong. His first years were full of purpose: in the 1st year of Jianzhong, on Yang Yan's counsel, he introduced the two-tax system — the tax fixed by expenditure, levied in summer and autumn, a transformation of the tax order that lasted into the Ming; and he meant to cut the feudatories. In the 2nd year of Jianzhong the garrisons of Chengde, Weibo, and Ziqing joined in revolt, and the court's campaigns failed.

In the 4th year of Jianzhong came the Jingyuan mutiny: the Jingyuan troops, passing through Chang'an without their pay, mutinied and raised Zhu Ci, who took the capital as emperor. Dezong fled in haste to Fengtian — the Fengtian crisis; Zhu Ci besieged the town for over a month, held by Hun Zhen and the rest. In the 1st year of Xingyuan Dezong issued the edict of self-blame — "I have truly been wanting in virtue, and brought this calamity" — and the realm was moved; Li Sheng recovered Chang'an and Zhu Ci fell. But "the will to cut the feudatories was broken from that day."

In the Zhenyuan years he "grew daily more suspicious and ever keener on revenue": the eunuch command of the imperial armies began in his reign, and the market-depredations and the tribute-seeking were his government's ways. He died in the 21st year of Zhenyuan, aged sixty-four. The histories say: "he would cut the feudatories at first, suffered exile in the middle, and grew suspicious and grasping at the last." The two-tax system and the Fengtian crisis are his reign's great deeds — the hinge of Tang's passage from height to decline.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 12 and 13 ("Benji of Emperor Dezong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.
