emperors.bio_md:
# 唐顺宗 · 主要事迹

李诵，德宗长子。贞元二十一年正月德宗崩，诵即位，改元永贞。顺宗即位前已中风失音，「不能言」，然其志在除弊：以东宫旧臣王叔文、王伾为用，柳宗元、刘禹锡、韦执谊等参预，谋夺宦官兵权、罢宫市、废五坊小儿、追还进奉——史称「永贞革新」。

然宦官俱文珍等与藩镇相结，拥太子纯（宪宗）逼顺宗禅位：永贞元年八月，顺宗禅位太子，自称太上皇，「永贞革新」仅一百四十六日而败，王叔文赐死，王伾贬死，柳宗元等八人被贬为州司马——「二王八司马」之祸。元和元年正月，太上皇顺宗崩，年四十六。

史评顺宗：「在位日浅，志在除弊而未成。」顺宗以病躯即位，其革新之志、用人之明，本可再造唐室；然宦官之强、积弊之深，非一日可革。永贞革新虽败，然其「抑宦官、罢宫市」之议，为文宗甘露之变的先声——唐代宦官专权之局，至此已不可破。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷014《顺宗纪》、韩愈《顺宗实录》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Song, eldest son of Dezong, took the throne in the first month of the 21st year of Zhenyuan, changing the era to Yongzhen. Already struck by paralysis and unable to speak, he yet meant to clear the abuses: with his eastern-palace men Wang Shuwen and Wang Pi, joined by Liu Zongyuan, Liu Yuxi, Wei Zhiyi, and the rest, he plotted to take the eunuchs' armies, abolish the market-depredations and the five-teams kennels, and return the tribute — the "Yongzhen reform."

But the eunuch Ju Wenzhen and the rest, linking with the feudatories, pressed the heir Chun (Xianzong) to demand the abdication: in the eighth month of the 1st year of Yongzhen Shunzong yielded to the heir and styled himself Grand Emperor — the reform died after a hundred and forty-six days; Wang Shuwen was ordered to die, Wang Pi died in exile, and the eight others, Liu Zongyuan and the rest, were banished as prefectural marshals — the "Two Kings and Eight Marshals." In the first month of the 1st year of Yuanhe the Grand Emperor died, aged forty-six.

The histories say: "his reign was brief; he meant to clear the abuses and could not finish." A sick man on the throne, his will to reform and his choice of men might have restored the Tang; but the eunuchs' strength and the depth of the old abuses were beyond one reign. The reform failed, yet its program — check the eunuchs, abolish the market-depredations — was the forerunner of Wenzong's Ganlu attempt: the eunuch domination of Tang was by then unbreakable.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 14 ("Benji of Emperor Shunzong"), and Han Yu's *Shunzong Shilu* (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐宪宗 · 主要事迹

李纯在位十五年（805—820），年号元和，是安史之乱后唐朝最有振作气象的皇帝。本页以《旧唐书·宪宗纪》为年表主线，辅以《新唐书·宪宗纪》与《资治通鉴》编年对照（本地参考库已备）。他的一生主线只有两个字：削藩。

元和元年（806）是他开局的手笔：先是讨平夏绥杨惠琳，继而讨平西川刘辟——两战皆捷，向天下藩镇展示了朝廷不再姑息的决心。但元和四年（809）讨伐成德王承宗一役成果有限，也让他看清河朔藩镇根深蒂固、硬啃不易的现实。

真正的考验在淮西。元和十年（815），平卢李师道竟遣刺客在长安街头杀死主战宰相武元衡，朝野震动，而朝廷用兵之志未移。元和十二年（817），宰相裴度亲赴淮西宣慰督师，名将李愬雪夜奇袭入蔡州，生擒吴元济——这是元和削藩的高潮，也是中唐最著名的一场奇袭。次年（818）前后，成德等河朔强藩一度听命于朝，史称"元和中兴"。

晚年他迎法门寺佛骨入长安，韩愈上表极谏而被贬，留下君臣关系与信仰政策的另一面相。元和十五年（820），他在长安暴崩，史载此事笼罩着与宦官相关的疑云；唐穆宗即位后，削藩成果迅速回落，河朔此后复叛。从唐顺宗的永贞内禅开局，到暴崩落幕，"元和中兴"是否可持续，正是读宪宗一朝最值得停下来的问题；与[[tang-tai-zong|唐太宗]]的贞观范式对读，也可见盛唐与中唐之间帝国处境的巨大落差。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Chun reigned for fifteen years (805–820) under the era name Yuanhe and was the most revitalizing emperor of the Tang after the An Lushan Rebellion. This page builds its chronology on the "Annals of Xianzong" in the Old Book of Tang, checked against the "Annals of Xianzong" in the New Book of Tang and the Zizhi Tongjian (all held in the local reference library). The main line of his life comes down to two words: reducing the provinces.

Yuanhe 1 (806) showed his opening hand: first he suppressed Yang Huilin of Xia-Sui, then Liu Pi of Xichuan. Two victories in a row announced to every military province that the court would no longer be lenient. But the campaign against Wang Chengzong of Chengde in Yuanhe 4 (809) achieved limited results, and it taught him how deeply entrenched the Heshuo provinces were and how hard they would be to crack.

The real test was Huaixi. In Yuanhe 10 (815), Li Shidao of Pinglu sent assassins who killed the pro-war chancellor Wu Yuanheng in the streets of Chang'an, shocking court and country, yet the court's will to use force did not waver. In Yuanhe 12 (817) the chancellor Pei Du went in person to Huaixi to reassure and direct the armies, and the renowned general Li Su made a surprise entry into Caizhou on a snowy night and captured Wu Yuanji alive: the climax of Yuanhe province reduction and the most celebrated surprise attack of the mid-Tang. Around the following year (818), powerful Heshuo provinces such as Chengde for a time obeyed the court, in what the histories call the "Yuanhe Restoration."

In his later years he received the Buddha's relic from Famen Temple into Chang'an; Han Yu submitted a memorial of utmost remonstrance and was banished, leaving another face of ruler-minister relations and religious policy. In Yuanhe 15 (820) he died suddenly in Chang'an, an event the histories record as wrapped in suspicions involving eunuchs. After Emperor Muzong of Tang took the throne, the gains of province reduction quickly receded and Heshuo rebelled again. From the Yongzhen abdication of Shunzong at the opening to the sudden death at the close, whether the "Yuanhe Restoration" could have lasted is the question most worth pausing over in Xianzong's reign; read against the Zhenguan model of
, it also shows the enormous gap in the empire's circumstances between the High Tang and the mid-Tang.

emperors.summary_en: Third son of Xianzong; on Xianzong's death in the 15th year of Yuanhe — by the eunuchs' hand, some say — Heng took the throne, changing the era to Changqing; in the 1st year of Changqing the three garrisons of Hebei rose again, and the gains of Yuanhe were lost; in the 2nd year the debate over disbanding the armies let the feudatories grow. He played and feasted, neglecting government, and died in the 4th year of Changqing.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐穆宗 · 主要事迹

李恒，宪宗第三子。元和十五年，宪宗暴崩（史多以为宦官陈弘志所弑），宦官拥立恒即位，改元长庆。穆宗即位之初，即「销兵」之议：以「天下已平」为由，罢诸镇兵额，崔植、杜元颖等议销兵——「销兵」之策，使藩镇之骄兵悍卒无所归，反成祸源。

长庆元年，卢龙、成德、魏博三镇相继复叛，朝廷讨伐无功——元和年间宪宗所收复之藩镇，一朝尽失；长庆二年，河北遂成「河朔故事」，割据之局自此不可复挽。穆宗「游宴怠政」，好击球、宴乐，「不亲政事」，政事委于宦官、权臣。

长庆四年，穆宗因服饵之疾崩，年三十。史评穆宗：「销兵误国，河北再乱。」元和之削藩，为唐室中兴之顶点；穆宗之销兵，为唐室中衰之转折——「销兵」二字，遂为史家之戒。穆宗以宴乐之君，承中兴之业而自毁之，唐室之衰，自穆宗而不可止。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷016《穆宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

Li Heng, third son of Xianzong. In the 15th year of Yuanhe Xianzong died suddenly — the histories suspect the eunuch Chen Hongzhi — and the eunuchs set up Heng, changing the era to Changqing. His opening act was the "disbanding the armies": deeming the realm at peace, he cut the garrisons' strengths, Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying debating the reduction — and the disbanded troops, with nowhere to go, became the very seed of disaster.

In the 1st year of Changqing the three garrisons of Lulong, Chengde, and Weibo rose again, and the court's campaigns failed — the feudatories recovered under Xianzong's Yuanhe reign were lost at a stroke; in the 2nd year Hebei settled into its "old story," and the division could not be mended. Muzong "played and feasted, neglecting government," loving polo and banquets, leaving affairs to the eunuchs and the ministers.

He died in the 4th year of Changqing of an elixir-sickness, aged thirty. The histories say: "disbanding the armies misled the realm, and Hebei rose again." The Yuanhe cutting of the feudatories was the summit of the restoration; Muzong's disbanding was the turn of the decline — "disbanding the armies" became the historians' warning. A pleasure-loving sovereign who threw away a restored realm: the decline of Tang could no longer be stopped from his reign.

# 唐敬宗 · 主要事迹

李湛，穆宗长子。长庆四年穆宗崩，湛即位，年十六，改元宝历。敬宗「童心未化」，好击球、手搏、角抵，「日晏坐朝」，又夜出游猎，「游戏无度」；政事委于宦官王守澄等，「政在宦官」之势，自此愈固。

宝历二年，敬宗夜猎还宫，与宦官刘克明、苏佐明等饮，酒酣，为苏佐明等所弑，年十八——唐代皇帝为宦官所弑，自敬宗始。宦官王守澄等又杀刘克明，迎立江王李涵（文宗）。

史评敬宗：「童心未化，身死阉寺。」唐代宦官之祸，至敬宗而极：立君、弑君、废君，皆出宦官之手。敬宗以游戏之君，当宦官之世，其死固其自取；然「甘露之变」后文宗之受制，亦皆此局之延续。唐代皇权之衰，自敬宗见弑而昭然。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Zhan, eldest son of Muzong, took the throne on his father's death in the 4th year of Changqing at sixteen, changing the era to Baoli. Jingzong was "a child at heart": he loved polo, wrestling, and cockfighting, sat late at court, hunted by night, "playing without limit"; the government fell to the eunuchs, Wang Shoucheng and the rest, and "the government lay with the eunuchs" was ever more fixed.

In the 2nd year of Baoli, returning from a night hunt, he drank with the eunuchs Liu Keming and Su Zuoming, and, drunk, was slain by Su Zuoming and the others, aged eighteen — the first Tang emperor slain by eunuchs. The eunuchs under Wang Shoucheng in turn slew the murderers and brought in the Prince of Jiang, Li Han (Wenzong).

The histories say: "a child at heart, he died by the eunuchs' hand." The eunuch disaster of Tang reached its height with Jingzong: enthroning, slaying, deposing emperors — all the eunuchs' work. A playing sovereign in the eunuch age, his death was his own making; but the binding of Wenzong after the Ganlu incident was the same pattern continued. The decline of the Tang throne was plain from Jingzong's slaying.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 17a ("Benji of Emperor Jingzong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 唐文宗 · 主要事迹

李昂（初名涵），穆宗第二子。宝历二年，敬宗被弑，宦官王守澄等迎立昂，改元大和。文宗「恭俭儒雅」，读史而叹「汉献帝受制于强臣，朕受制于家奴」——其志在除宦官，然「左右皆宦竖」，谋事屡泄。

大和五年，宰相宋申锡谋诛宦官，事泄，贬死开州——「宋申锡案」，为除宦之第一次失败。大和九年，文宗与李训、郑注谋：诈称天降甘露于左金吾厅，欲诱宦官仇士良等入内诛之——「甘露之变」。然事机不密，仇士良等先发制人，杀李训、郑注及朝士千余人，「血流成河」；文宗自此受制于宦官，「虽天子，而不能保其左右」。

开成五年，文宗崩，年三十二。史评文宗：「恭俭好文，有意除宦而败。」唐代宦官专权，甘露之变为其顶点：自此「天子废立，皆出阉寺」。文宗以仁弱之君，欲除积年之祸，其志可嘉，其败可哀——「甘露之变」后，唐室之政，尽归北司。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Ang, first named Han, was the second son of Muzong. In the 2nd year of Baoli, after Jingzong's slaying, the eunuch Wang Shoucheng and the others brought in Ang, changing the era to Dahe. Wenzong was "frugal and scholarly," and, reading history, sighed that "Emperor Xian of Han was bound by strong ministers, and I am bound by my own servants" — his aim was the eunuchs; but "all about him were eunuchs," and every plot leaked.

In the 5th year of Dahe the chancellor Song Shenxi plotted against the eunuchs, the plot leaked, and he died in exile at Kaizhou — the first failure. In the 9th year of Dahe, Wenzong with Li Xun and Zheng Zhu plotted: they feigned sweet dew falling on the left offices of the Guard, to lure the eunuch Qiu Shiliang and the rest within for slaughter — the Ganlu incident. But the secret broke; Qiu Shiliang and the others struck first, slaying Li Xun, Zheng Zhu, and over a thousand courtiers — "the blood ran in rivers"; and from that day Wenzong was bound by the eunuchs, "an emperor who could not keep even his own attendants."

He died in the 5th year of Kaicheng, aged thirty-two. The histories say: "frugal and fond of letters, his will to destroy the eunuchs defeated." The Ganlu incident was the summit of eunuch power: from it, "the enthroning and deposing of emperors came all from the inner court." A gentle sovereign seeking to sweep away the old plague — his will is to be honored, his failure mourned: after Ganlu, the government of Tang passed to the northern court of the eunuchs.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 17b ("Benji of Emperor Wenzong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐武宗 · 主要事迹

李炎（初名瀍），穆宗第五子。开成五年文宗崩，宦官仇士良等立炎，改元会昌。武宗即位后，任李德裕为相——「会昌中兴」之名，实赖德裕之才：会昌三年，讨平泽潞刘稹，藩镇一时夺气；又回鹘破灭，收抚其众；「德裕之政，最为大中以前之盛」。

会昌五年，武宗下令废佛：拆毁佛寺四千六百余所，僧尼还俗二十六万余人，史称「会昌法难」——与北魏太武帝灭佛并称「二武灭佛」。然武宗「好道术，服食丹药」，饵金石之药，疾发而崩，年三十三，会昌六年。

史评武宗：「任李德裕，有会昌中兴之称；好道服丹，不永其年。」武宗之世，为安史之乱后唐室武功、政事最振之时；然「会昌灭佛」之失、服丹暴崩之祸，使其中兴如昙花一现。武宗之才与德裕之能相得，而天不假年——唐室中兴之机，自此而绝。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Yan, first named Chan, was the fifth son of Muzong. On Wenzong's death in the 5th year of Kaicheng the eunuch Qiu Shiliang and the others set up Yan, changing the era to Huichang. Wuzong made Li Deyu chancellor — the "Huichang revival" was Deyu's work: in the 3rd year he destroyed Liu Zhen of Zelu, and the feudatories lost heart for a moment; the Uyghur khanate fell, and he gathered its people; "Deyu's government was the best before Dazhong."

In the 5th year of Huichang Wuzong proscribed Buddhism by edict: over 4,600 monasteries demolished, over 260,000 monks and nuns returned to lay life — the Huichang persecution, paired with Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei as the "two Wu persecutions." But he "loved Daoism and took the elixirs," and the drugs brought on his sickness and death at thirty-three, in the 6th year of Huichang.

The histories say: "with Li Deyu he won the name of the Huichang revival; he loved Daoism and the elixirs, and his years were not long." His reign was the strongest of Tang's arms and government since the An–Shi storm; but the persecution and the elixir-death made the revival a flash in the pan. The meeting of Wuzong's ability and Deyu's talent came too late and ended too soon — the chance of the restoration was gone.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 18a ("Benji of Emperor Wuzong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐宣宗 · 主要事迹

李忱（初名怡），宪宗第十三子。会昌六年武宗崩，宦官立忱，改元大中。宣宗「外貌怯弱，内实精察」：即位之初，贬李德裕于崖州，牛李党争之势大变；又「精于听断」，整顿吏治，抑宦者之权，唐室之政，一时稍振——史称「大中之治」，誉宣宗为「小太宗」。

大中三年，沙州人张议潮起兵归唐，收复河湟十一州——自安史之乱后陷于吐蕃的陇右之地，部分复归唐室；宣宗置归义军以镇之。然宣宗「察察为明」：猜忌大臣，「群臣奏事，不敢仰视」；又废立太子，晚年服食丹药。

大中十三年，宣宗崩，年五十。史评宣宗：「精于听断，察察为明，唐室小安。」大中之治，为唐末最后之小康；然宣宗之「小太宗」，止于守成，未能除藩镇、宦官之积弊。宣宗崩后，懿宗奢侈、僖宗播迁，唐室遂不可为——大中之治，实为唐之回光返照。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷018下《宣宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Chen, first named Yi, was the thirteenth son of Xianzong. On Wuzong's death in the 6th year of Huichang the eunuchs set up Chen, changing the era to Dazhong. "Outwardly weak, inwardly sharp of scrutiny," on accession he exiled Li Deyu to Yazhou and the Niu–Li factional balance shifted; he "judged sharply," disciplined the officials, and checked the eunuchs — the government of Tang was steadied for a moment, and the histories call his reign the Dazhong recovery, honoring him as the "Little Taizong."

In the 3rd year of Dazhong, Zhang Yichao of Shazhou rose and submitted to Tang, recovering eleven prefectures of the Hehuang — part of the Longyou lands lost to Tibet since the An–Shi rebellion returned; the Guiyi Army was set to hold it. But Xuanzong "saw clearly into everything": he distrusted his ministers — "the courtiers dared not look up when they spoke" — deposed his heir, and in his last years took the elixirs.

He died in the 13th year of Dazhong, aged fifty. The histories say: "he judged sharply, saw clearly, and the Tang house enjoyed a small peace." The Dazhong recovery was the last modest ease of the Tang's last years; but the "Little Taizong" only kept the realm, and could not root out the feudatories and the eunuchs. After his death came Yizong's extravagance and Xizong's flight — the Dazhong recovery was the Tang's last glow.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 18b ("Benji of Emperor Xuanzong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐懿宗 · 主要事迹

李漼（初名温），宣宗长子。大中十三年宣宗崩，漼即位，改元咸通。懿宗「奢侈无度」：好音乐、宴游，「后宫三千，更番直宿」；又崇佛教，咸通十四年迎法门寺佛骨，「导以禁军，鼓乐连天，绵延数十里」，耗费巨万——韩愈谏佛骨之「佛骨」故事，至懿宗而愈炽。

懿宗之世，民变渐起：咸通九年，桂林戍卒庞勋起义，北归徐州，攻陷州县，「唐室大震」——虽旋平，然「庞勋虽平，而黄巢之祸，已伏其端」。懿宗又委政于宰相路岩、韦保衡等，「政出多门，贿赂公行」。

咸通十四年，懿宗崩，年四十一。史评懿宗：「奢侈佞佛，盗贼始炽。」懿宗朝为唐末大乱之序幕：庞勋起义开其端，其后王仙芝、黄巢继之——唐室之亡，实自懿宗之奢侈失政始。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷019上《懿宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Cui, first named Wen, was the eldest son of Xuanzong. On his father's death in the 13th year of Dazhong he took the throne, changing the era to Xiantong. Yizong was "extravagant without limit": he loved music and pleasure, "three thousand of the inner palace serving by turns"; and he doted on Buddhism — in the 14th year of Xiantong he welcomed the Famen Temple relic, "the imperial guards leading, drums and music stretching for tens of li," spending tens of millions — the relic that Han Yu had warned against, welcomed with more fervor than ever.

His reign saw the risings begin: in the 9th year of Xiantong the Guilin garrison rose under Pang Xun and marched north to Xuzhou, taking prefectures and counties, "shaking the Tang house" — suppressed in the end, but "though Pang Xun fell, the disaster of Huang Chao was already seeded." He left the government to the chancellors Lu Yan and Wei Baohang, "the government coming from many mouths, bribes running openly."

He died in the 14th year of Xiantong, aged forty-one. The histories say: "extravagant and Buddhist-mad, he let the bandits flame up." His reign was the prologue to the great disorders of the Tang's end: Pang Xun opened the way, and Wang Xianzhi and Huang Chao followed — the fall of Tang began with Yizong's extravagance and misrule.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 19a ("Benji of Emperor Yizong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐僖宗 · 主要事迹

李儇（初名俨），懿宗第五子。咸通十四年懿宗崩，宦官田令孜等立儇，年十二，改元乾符。僖宗「幼而嬉戏」，政事尽委田令孜，「阿父」之呼，史所罕见。乾符二年，王仙芝、黄巢相继起兵于曹、濮，天下大乱。

广明元年，黄巢渡淮北上，陷洛阳，入长安，僖宗幸蜀（成都）——「唐室之再播迁」。黄巢称帝于长安，国号大齐；中和三年，李克用等沙陀兵破巢，收复长安，僖宗还京。然乱后之唐：「藩镇相攻，宦官相争」，田令孜与王重荣交兵，僖宗再奔凤翔。

文德元年，僖宗还京后崩，年二十七。史评僖宗：「幼冲播迁，唐室将亡。」黄巢之乱，为唐亡之直接前奏：藩镇之权益强（朱温、李克用等皆巢部降将），宦官之祸益烈，「唐之亡，实亡于僖宗之世」。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷019下《僖宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Xuan, first named Yan, was the fifth son of Yizong. On Yizong's death in the 14th year of Xiantong the eunuch Tian Lingzi and the others set up Xuan, aged twelve, changing the era to Qianfu. Xizong "played from childhood," leaving everything to Tian Lingzi, whom he called "foster father" — a thing the histories rarely record. In the 2nd year of Qianfu, Wang Xianzhi and Huang Chao rose in succession in Cao and Pu, and the realm fell into chaos.

In the 1st year of Guangming, Huang Chao crossed the Huai, took Luoyang, and entered Chang'an; Xizong fled to Shu (Chengdu) — the second exile of the Tang house. Huang Chao took the capital as emperor of the Great Qi; in the 3rd year of Zhonghe Li Keyong and the Shatuo troops broke Chao and recovered Chang'an, and Xizong returned. But the Tang after the storm: "the feudatories fought each other, the eunuchs fought among themselves," and when Tian Lingzi clashed with Wang Chongrong, Xizong fled again to Fengxiang.

He died after returning to the capital in the 1st year of Wende, aged twenty-seven. The histories say: "a child in exile, the Tang near its fall." The Huang Chao rebellion was the direct prelude to the fall: the feudatories grew stronger than ever (Zhu Wen and Li Keyong were both rebel generals), the eunuch disaster worse — "the fall of Tang was truly prepared in Xizong's reign."

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 19b ("Benji of Emperor Xizong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 唐昭宗 · 主要事迹

李晔（初名杰），懿宗第七子。文德元年僖宗崩，杨复恭等宦官立晔，年二十二。昭宗「明敏有英气，喜文学」，以「王室浸微」为忧，欲重振唐室——然其世藩镇已强、宦官已固，屡与相争而屡败：乾宁年间，与李克用、李茂贞等交兵，长安两遭兵火。

天复元年，宦官韩全诲劫昭宗幸凤翔，依李茂贞；天复三年，朱全忠（朱温）攻凤翔，李茂贞请和，交出昭宗与宦官。全忠迎帝还京，「尽诛宦官」，宦官之祸虽除，然「唐廷寄命于汴军」——昭宗自宦官之手，转入朱全忠之手。

天祐元年，朱全忠逼昭宗迁都洛阳，并毁长安宫室；八月，全忠使蒋玄晖等弑昭宗于洛阳椒殿，年三十八——唐之末帝哀帝立。史评昭宗：「有意兴复，而卒为全忠所制。」昭宗之世，唐室已如累卵：其欲兴复之志可嘉，然「藩镇之强、积弊之深」，非一人所能挽。昭宗之死，唐亡已不可免。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Ye, first named Jie, was the seventh son of Yizong. On Xizong's death in the 1st year of Wende the eunuch Yang Fugong and the others set up Ye, aged twenty-two. Zhaozong "was sharp and spirited, a lover of letters," and, grieving that "the royal house was sinking," meant to restore the Tang — but his age had the feudatories strong and the eunuchs fixed, and his struggles failed again and again: in the Qianning years he warred with Li Keyong and Li Maozhen, and Chang'an burned twice.

In the 1st year of Tianfu the eunuch Han Quanhui carried Zhaozong to Fengxiang, to lean on Li Maozhen; in the 3rd year Zhu Quanzhong (Zhu Wen) attacked Fengxiang, Maozhen sued for peace and handed over the emperor and the eunuchs. Quanzhong brought the emperor back, "slaughtered the eunuchs" — the eunuch disaster was ended, but "the Tang court lived at the Bian army's mercy": Zhaozong passed from the eunuchs' hand to Zhu Quanzhong's.

In the 1st year of Tianyou Quanzhong forced the move to Luoyang, demolishing Chang'an's palaces; in the eighth month he had Jiang Xuanhui and the others slay Zhaozong in the Jiaodian Hall of Luoyang, aged thirty-eight — and Emperor Ai, the last of the Tang, was set up. The histories say: "he meant to restore the realm, and was in the end bound by Quanzhong." His realm was already like eggs piled: his will to restore is to be honored, but "the feudatories' strength and the depth of the old abuses" were beyond any one man. With his slaying, the fall of Tang was unavoidable.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 20a ("Benji of Emperor Zhaozong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 唐哀帝 · 主要事迹

李柷（初名祚），昭宗第九子。天祐元年，朱全忠弑昭宗，立柷，年十三。哀帝在位三年，实为朱全忠掌中之物：天祐二年，全忠杀朝士裴枢、独孤损等三十余人，投尸于白马驿黄河——「白马驿之祸」，清流之祸，唐室士大夫精英尽丧。

天祐四年，朱全忠逼哀帝禅位，唐亡，后梁建立——唐自高祖武德元年开国，历二十一帝二百九十年而终。哀帝降封济阴王，次年（开平二年）为朱全忠所害，年十七。

史评哀帝：「幼冲亡国，唐三百年终。」唐之亡，不亡于哀帝之世，而亡于安史之乱后藩镇、宦官、党争之积弊：僖宗之播迁、昭宗之被弑、白马驿之祸，皆其亡之序曲。哀帝不过承其祸而已。「唐亡」之日，中国历史进入五代十国之局。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧唐书》卷020下《哀帝纪》、新五代史卷001《梁本纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Zhu, first named Zuo, was the ninth son of Zhaozong. In the 1st year of Tianyou, Zhu Quanzhong slew Zhaozong and set up Zhu, aged thirteen. Three years he reigned, a thing of Quanzhong's: in the 2nd year of Tianyou Quanzhong slew the courtiers Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, and over thirty others, throwing their bodies into the Yellow River at the Baima relay — the Baimayi disaster, the "slaughter of the clear stream," the elite of the Tang court lost at a stroke.

In the 4th year of Tianyou Quanzhong forced the abdication: Tang fell, and the Later Liang arose — from Gaozu's founding in the 1st year of Wude, twenty-one emperors and two hundred and ninety years of Tang were at an end. Ai, reduced to Prince of Jiyin, was done to death by Quanzhong the next year (the 2nd of Kaiping), aged seventeen.

The histories say: "a child at the fall of the realm — the three hundred years of Tang were at an end." Tang did not fall in Ai's reign but to the long disease of feudatories, eunuchs, and factionalism since the An–Shi rebellion: Xizong's flight, Zhaozong's slaying, the Baimayi disaster were its funeral march. Ai only inherited the catastrophe. With "the fall of Tang," Chinese history entered the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Tangshu*, ch. 20b ("Benji of Emperor Ai"), and the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 1 ("Annals of Liang") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后梁太祖 · 主要事迹

朱温，宋州砀山人。少为乡里无赖，黄巢起兵后投入巢军，为部将；中和二年，降唐，赐名全忠，为宣武节度使——自黄巢之乱中崛起的降将，遂成唐末最强藩镇。此后二十余年，朱温吞并中原诸镇，挟天子以令诸侯：天祐元年，逼唐昭宗迁都洛阳，旋弑之；又杀朝士三十余人于白马驿，清流之祸。

开平元年，唐哀帝禅位，朱温即皇帝位，国号梁，都开封，改元开平——唐亡，五代始。朱温在位五年，「政事苛暴」，又「荒淫无度」，乾化二年，为其子朱友珪所弑，年六十一。

史评朱温：「起盗贼，代唐有国，残暴见史。」朱温以黄巢降将之身取唐室之天下，其残暴、荒淫，为五代开国者之最；然其「代唐」，亦为唐末藩镇割据之必然结局。五代之乱，自朱温始——「五代十国」之局，由此开篇。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷001-007《梁太祖纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Zhu Wen, a man of Dangshan in Songzhou, was a village rogue in his youth; when Huang Chao rose he joined the rebel host as a general, and in the 2nd year of Zhonghe surrendered to Tang, was renamed Quanzhong, and made military governor of Xuanwu — a surrendered rebel general who became the strongest warlord of the late Tang. For over twenty years he swallowed the warlords of the Central Plains, "holding the emperor to command the lords": in the 1st year of Tianyou he forced Zhaozong to Luoyang and slew him; and he drowned over thirty courtiers at the Baima relay — the slaughter of the clear stream.

In the 1st year of Kaiping Emperor Ai abdicated; Zhu Wen took the throne, founded Liang at Kaifeng, and changed the era — Tang fell, and the Five Dynasties began. Five years he reigned, "harsh and cruel in government," "lewd without limit," until in the 2nd year of Qianhua his son Zhu Yougui slew him, aged sixty-one.

The histories say: "a bandit who took the Tang throne; the histories record his cruelty." A surrendered rebel who took the Tang realm, his cruelty and lust were the worst of the Five Dynasties founders; but his "taking of Tang" was the inevitable end of the late-Tang warlordism. The chaos of the Five Dynasties begins with Zhu Wen — the age of Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms opens here.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 1–7 ("Annals of the Liang Taizu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后梁末帝 · 主要事迹

朱友贞，梁太祖第三子。乾化二年，太祖为友珪所弑，友珪自立；凤历元年，均王友贞与赵岩等密谋，联络禁军诛友珪，即帝位，复称乾化。末帝在位十年，为五代诸帝中在位最久者之一；然「性懦弱，不任军事」，河北之地，与晋王李存勖争夺连年——柏乡、杨刘诸战，梁军屡败，梁势渐蹙。

贞明、龙德年间，梁朝政事「政出多门」，段凝、赵岩等用事；龙德三年，李存勖称帝于魏州（后唐），亲率大军袭汴。末帝闻唐军将至，登建国楼，命皇甫麟杀己，「挥涕而受刃」，后梁亡，年三十六。

史评末帝：「不能制将帅，终亡于沙陀。」后梁自太祖受禅至末帝亡国，历二帝十七年——五代之最短者之一。梁之亡，亡于太祖之暴政与末帝之懦弱；而李存勖之兴，则开沙陀三朝（后唐、后晋、后汉）之局。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷008-010《梁末帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

史评末帝：「不能制将帅，终亡于沙陀。」后梁自太祖受禅至末帝亡国，历二帝十七年——五代之最短者之一。梁之亡，亡于太祖之暴政与末帝之懦弱；而李存勖之兴，则开沙陀三朝（后唐、后晋、后汉）之局。

bio_parts_en.value:
Zhu Youzhen, third son of the Liang Taizu. In the 2nd year of Qianhua Taizu was slain by Yougui, who took the throne; in the 1st year of Fengli the Prince of Jun, Youzhen, plotting with Zhao Yan and the rest, drew in the imperial guards, slew Yougui, and took the throne, restoring the era Qianhua. Ten years he reigned — among the longest of the Five Dynasties; but "weak and timid, no hand for war," he contended year after year with the King of Jin, Li Cunxu, for Hebei — at Baima, Yangliu, and the rest the Liang armies were beaten again and again, and Liang's strength ebbed.

In the Zhenming and Longde years "the government came from many mouths," Duan Ning and Zhao Yan in power; in the 3rd year of Longde Li Cunxu took the throne at Weizhou (Later Tang) and rode at once against Kaifeng. Learning the Tang army was at hand, the Last Sovereign climbed the Jianguo Tower, had Huangfu Lin kill him — "weeping, he received the blade" — and Later Liang was no more, aged thirty-six.

The histories say: "he could not control his generals, and fell to the Shatuo at last." From Taizu's abdication to the Last Sovereign's fall, two emperors and seventeen years — one of the briefest of the Five Dynasties. Liang fell to Taizu's tyranny and the Last Sovereign's weakness; and the rise of Li Cunxu opened the three Shatuo dynasties — Later Tang, Later Jin, Later Han.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 8–10 ("Annals of the Liang Last Sovereign") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 后唐庄宗 · 主要事迹

李存勖，沙陀部李克用长子，小字亚子。天祐五年（908）李克用卒，存勖嗣晋王位，与后梁争雄十余年——「三矢遗恨」之志，灭梁雪耻。同光元年（923），存勖称帝于魏州，国号唐（史称后唐），自居李唐正统；随即亲率大军奇袭开封，后梁亡——「灭梁之志，一朝而伸」。同年迁都洛阳。

同光三年，遣郭崇韬、魏王继岌等伐蜀，灭前蜀王衍。后唐疆域，兼有中原与巴蜀，为五代之最盛；然庄宗「勇而少礼」：宠信伶人（景进、史彦琼等）、宦官（张承业之外），「以伶人为刺史」，功臣离心；又任刘皇后，聚敛无度。

同光四年，魏州兵变，李嗣源（明宗）被拥南下；庄宗亲征无功，洛阳城中伶人郭从谦等作乱，庄宗中流矢崩，年四十二。史评庄宗：「勇而少礼，宠伶宦，胜而不久。」以武功取天下，以失德失天下——「数十年经营，一旦而败」，为五代兴亡之最典型者。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷027-034《庄宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Cunxu, eldest son of the Shatuo Li Keyong, childhood name Yazi. In the 5th year of Tianyou (908) Keyong died and Cunxu succeeded as King of Jin, contending with Later Liang for over a decade — the will of the "three arrows" to wipe out Liang. In the 1st year of Tongguang (923) he took the throne at Weizhou as the realm Tang (Later Tang to history), claiming the legitimacy of the Tang house, and at once rode against Kaifeng with his own hand — Later Liang fell: "the will to destroy Liang, stretched out in a day." That year he moved the capital to Luoyang.

In the 3rd year of Tongguang he sent Guo Chongtao and the Prince of Wei to conquer Shu — Former Shu fell. Later Tang, holding both the Central Plains and Bashu, was the greatest of the Five Dynasties; but Zhuangzong was "bold and wanting in rites": he doted on actors (Jing Jin, Shi Yanqiong) and eunuchs, "making actors prefects," and the meritorious fell away; with Empress Liu he hoarded without limit.

In the 4th year of Tongguang the Weizhou garrison mutinied, and Li Siyuan (Mingzong) was carried south by his troops; Zhuangzong's own campaign failed, and in Luoyang the actor Guo Congqian and the others rose, Zhuangzong fell to an arrow and died, aged forty-two. The histories say: "bold and wanting in rites, favoring actors and eunuchs — he won, and did not last." He won the realm by arms and lost it by misrule — "decades of labor, ruined in a day" — the most typical rise and fall of the Five Dynasties.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 27–34 ("Annals of Emperor Zhuangzong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后唐明宗 · 主要事迹

李嗣源，代北沙陀部人，本名邈佶烈，李克用养子。骁勇善战，为后唐开国名将。同光四年，庄宗以猜忌逼反，魏州兵变，嗣源被拥为帝；庄宗中流矢崩，嗣源入洛即位，改元天成。明宗即位后，「政治宽仁」：史称其「留心民事，赋役稍宽」，「于五代之君，最为仁厚」，史家以「五代少有的小康之主」评之。

明宗在位七年，与契丹、吴、蜀等并立，边境大体无事；又行「与民休息」之政，五季之乱中，中原百姓稍得喘息。然「藩镇难制、储嗣不明」：长兴四年，明宗病笃，皇子从荣争位被诛，从厚（闵帝）即位，明宗寻崩，年六十七。

史评明宗：「宽政息兵，五代小康。」明宗以养子之身得天下，能以宽仁守之，为五代诸帝中难得之贤者；然「积弊已深，非一人所能挽」——其崩后，后唐旋即内乱，闵帝、末帝相继，不过三年而亡。五代之乱，终非一君所能止。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷035-044《明宗纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Siyuan, a Shatuo of Daibei, originally Miaojiilie, was the adopted son of Li Keyong. A fierce warrior, he was a founding general of Later Tang. In the 4th year of Tongguang, driven to revolt by Zhuangzong's suspicion, he was carried by the Weizhou mutineers; Zhuangzong fell to an arrow, and Siyuan entered Luoyang and took the throne, changing the era to Tiancheng. His government was "lenient and humane": the histories say he "attended to the people's affairs and lightened the levies," "the most humane of the Five Dynasties' sovereigns," and call his reign "the one modest peace of the Five Dynasties."

Seven years he reigned, at peace with the Khitan, Wu, and Shu on his borders, resting the people of the Central Plains amid the storms. But "the feudatories were hard to control and the succession unclear": in the 4th year of Changxing, as he lay ill, his son Congrong contended for the succession and was slain, and Conghou (the Min emperor) took the throne as Mingzong died, aged sixty-seven.

The histories say: "lenient government, stilling the wars — the Five Dynasties' one peace." An adopted son who won the throne and kept it with benevolence, the rarest worthy of the age; but "the old abuses ran too deep for one man to mend" — after his death the realm fell at once into the Min and Mo emperors' wars, and Later Tang was gone within three years. The chaos of the age could not be stopped by one sovereign.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 35–44 ("Annals of Emperor Mingzong") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后唐闵帝 · 主要事迹

李从厚，明宗第三子。长兴四年明宗崩，从厚即位，年二十，改元应顺。闵帝「幼弱」，即位后诸王（潞王从珂等）与藩镇皆轻视之：朱弘昭、冯赟等执政，谋削潞王从珂之权——移镇之议，激成其变。

应顺元年（934），凤翔节度使李从珂起兵，声讨朱弘昭等；闵帝遣军讨伐，军心倒戈，从珂长驱入洛。闵帝出奔，途中为从珂所执，废为鄂王，旋遇害，年二十一——在位不过四月。

史评闵帝：「幼弱，不能制藩镇宗室。」五代之世，「兵强马壮者为天子」：闵帝以书生之质当藩镇之世，其废其死，皆五代「武人政治」之必然。后唐之亡，实自闵帝之废而加速——从珂得位不正，亦不过两年而自焚。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷045《闵帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Conghou, third son of Mingzong, took the throne on his father's death in the 4th year of Changxing at twenty, changing the era to Yingshun. The Min emperor was "young and weak," and on his accession the princes — the Prince of Lu, Congke, and the rest — and the feudatories held him in contempt: Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun, governing for him, plotted to strip the Prince of Lu of his garrisons — the transfer that provoked the storm.

In the 1st year of Yingshun (934) the Fengxiang governor Li Congke rose, denouncing Zhu Hongzhao and the rest; the emperor's armies went over to him, and Congke rode into Luoyang. The Min emperor fled, was seized, deposed as Prince of E, and soon done to death, aged twenty-one — four months on the throne.

The histories say: "young and weak, unable to control the feudatories and the princes." In the Five Dynasties, "whoever is strong in soldiers and horses is the Son of Heaven": a bookish sovereign in the warlord age, his deposition and death were the logic of the age. The fall of Later Tang quickened from his deposition — Congke, ill-gotten on the throne, burned himself within two years.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后唐末帝 · 主要事迹

李从珂，本姓王，明宗养子。清泰元年（934），以凤翔起兵，废闵帝自立，改元清泰。末帝以「兵变夺位」，得位不正；然其「有勇力，善骑射」，初政尚能任贤。然清泰二年，末帝猜忌河东节度使石敬瑭——「移镇、削兵」之议，激成石敬瑭之反。

清泰三年（936），石敬瑭在太原称帝，联契丹为援，认契丹主耶律德光为父，割幽云十六州；契丹大军南下，唐军屡败。同年十一月，契丹、晋军入洛阳，末帝登玄武楼，举火自焚，后唐亡，年五十二——自庄宗灭梁至末帝自焚，后唐历四帝十四年。

史评末帝：「得位不正，终亡于契丹。」后唐之亡，亡于石敬瑭之叛与契丹之强；而「幽云十六州」之割，更为中国此后四百余年之祸——自辽、金至于蒙元，北方之患，皆由此起。末帝以自焚殉国，虽亡国，犹有烈气。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷046-048《唐末帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Congke, originally of the Wang surname, was the adopted son of Mingzong. In the 1st year of Qingtai (934) he rose at Fengxiang, deposed the Min emperor, and took the throne, changing the era to Qingtai. His throne was won by mutiny and ill-gotten; but he was "strong and a fine rider and archer," and his early government could still employ the worthy. In the 2nd year of Qingtai, however, he came to distrust the Hedong governor Shi Jingtang — the transfers and stripping of garrisons that drove Jingtang to revolt.

In the 3rd year of Qingtai (936) Jingtang took the throne at Taiyuan, called on the Khitan, acknowledged the Khitan ruler Yelü Deguang as father, and ceded the Sixteen Prefectures of Yanyun; the Khitan host came south and the Tang armies were beaten again and again. That eleventh month the Khitan and Jin armies entered Luoyang; the Last Sovereign climbed the Xuanwu Tower and burned himself — Later Tang was no more, aged fifty-two. From Zhuangzong's destruction of Liang to the Last Sovereign's fire, four emperors and fourteen years.

The histories say: "his throne was ill-gotten, and he fell to the Khitan at last." Later Tang fell to Jingtang's revolt and the Khitan's strength; and the cession of the Sixteen Prefectures was a disaster for China for four hundred years — from Liao and Jin to the Mongols, the northern menace ran from this. The Last Sovereign, dying in his own fire, kept at least the fire of a fallen king.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 46–48 ("Annals of the Tang Last Sovereign") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 后晋高祖 · 主要事迹

石敬瑭，沙陀部人，后唐明宗之婿，河东节度使。清泰三年（936），末帝移镇削兵，敬瑭遂反：乞援于契丹，认契丹主耶律德光为「父皇帝」，自称「儿皇帝」，并许割幽云十六州——「儿皇帝」之名，遂为千古之讥。契丹出兵助敬瑭灭后唐，敬瑭即皇帝位于太原，国号晋，都开封。

天福三年（938），契丹改国号为大辽，石敬瑭遣使献幽云十六州图籍——自幽州（今北京）至云州（今大同）一线十六州之地，尽入契丹；此后「北边称臣岁贡」，后晋岁输金帛数十万。石晋立国，实为契丹之附庸。

天福七年，石敬瑭崩，年五十一。史评敬瑭：「以土地事契丹，史称儿皇帝。」石敬瑭之罪，不在称帝（五代武人皆可为天子），而在「割燕云、称儿臣」——燕云十六州之失，使中原失去长城之险，自此「天下之势，自北而南」；其祸延及宋、明，为历史之最大污点。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷075-080《晋高祖纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Shi Jingtang, a Shatuo, was the son-in-law of Mingzong and governor of Hedong. In the 3rd year of Qingtai (936), when the Last Sovereign moved and stripped his garrisons, Jingtang revolted: he begged aid of the Khitan, acknowledged the Khitan ruler Yelü Deguang as "father emperor," called himself "son emperor," and promised the Sixteen Prefectures of Yanyun — the name "son emperor" passing into the eternal mockery of history. The Khitan helped him destroy Later Tang; Jingtang took the throne at Taiyuan as the realm Jin, with its capital at Kaifeng.

In the 3rd year of Tianfu (938) the Khitan took the name Liao, and Jingtang sent the maps and registers of the Sixteen Prefectures — the lands from Youzhou (Beijing) to Yunzhou (Datong), sixteen prefectures in all, passed to the Khitan; from that day "the northern border was vassal and tribute," the Jin paying tens of thousands in gold and silk each year. The Jin realm was in truth Liao's dependency.

In the 7th year of Tianfu Jingtang died, aged fifty-one. The histories say: "he served the Khitan with his lands — the histories call him the son emperor." Jingtang's crime was not the throne (any warlord of the age might be emperor) but the cession of Yanyun and the vassal's name — with the Sixteen Prefectures, the Central Plains lost the shield of the Great Wall, and "the balance of the realm ran from north to south" from that day; the disaster ran on into Song and Ming, the greatest stain of the age.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 75–80 ("Annals of the Jin Gaozu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后晋出帝 · 主要事迹

石重贵，石敬瑭兄子，以侄立为嗣。天福七年高祖崩，重贵即位，改元开运。出帝「少而倨傲」，即位后，景延广等主战：遣使告契丹，「称孙而不称臣」——拒绝臣服之礼。契丹主耶律德光大怒，以为「晋背恩」，遂大举南伐。

开运年间，晋辽大战：契丹三度南下，晋军初胜（马家口、白团卫诸役），然将帅不和、粮饷不继；开运四年（947），契丹主德光率大军入汴，出帝欲战不能、欲守无地，肉袒出降，被俘北迁——后晋亡，历二帝十一年。出帝北迁后，卒于建州（契丹地）。

史评出帝：「既不能恭事契丹，又不能自立。」石晋以儿皇帝立国，出帝欲抗辽而力不逮——「欲战则力不足，欲和则名已裂」，终至国亡身虏。后晋之亡，为五代中亡国之最惨者：从此中原无主，契丹一度入主开封，刘知远乘机建汉。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷081-085《晋少帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Shi Chonggui, son of Jingtang's elder brother, was made heir. On Gaozu's death in the 7th year of Tianfu he took the throne, changing the era to Kaiyun. The Emperor Chu was "proud from youth," and on accession Jing Yangguang and the others urged war: envoys told the Khitan, "grandson, but not vassal" — refusing the rites of submission. The Liao ruler Yelü Deguang, in fury at the "ingratitude of Jin," marched south in force.

In the Kaiyun years Jin and Liao fought their great wars: the Khitan came south three times, and the Jin armies won at first (at Majiakou, at Baituanwei), but the generals quarreled and the supplies failed; in the 4th year of Kaiyun (947) Deguang led the Liao host into Kaifeng, and the Emperor Chu, unable to fight or hold, surrendered bare-armed and was taken north — Later Jin was no more, two emperors and eleven years. He died in exile at Jianzhou in Khitan lands.

The histories say: "he could neither serve the Khitan humbly nor stand on his own." A son-emperor's realm seeking to defy the Khitan with insufficient strength — "to fight, strength wanting; to make peace, the name already broken" — he ended in national ruin and personal captivity. The fall of Jin was the bitterest of the Five Dynasties: the Central Plains stood masterless, the Khitan entered Kaifeng for a time, and Liu Zhiyuan seized the chance to found Han.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 81–85 ("Annals of the Jin Young Emperor") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后汉高祖 · 主要事迹

刘知远，沙陀部人，仕后晋为河东节度使。开运四年（947），契丹灭晋，耶律德光入开封称帝（后北还）；知远时为河东节度使，拥兵观望——「静观契丹之变，乘机而有天下」。同年二月，知远称帝于太原，国号汉（史称后汉），沿用晋「天福」年号以收人心。

契丹北还，知远自太原南下，入开封，改元乾祐；即位后剪除不附：杀杜重威等，稳定汴洛。然知远在位仅一年：乾祐元年（948）正月，崩于开封，年五十四，子承祐（隐帝）即位。

史评知远：「静观契丹，乘机有国。」后汉以「捡漏」得国：契丹灭晋而不守，知远乘虚而入——五代之兴，未有如后汉之易者；然其祚亦最短，历二帝四年而亡。「其兴也易，其亡也速」，后汉为五代之最短者。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Zhiyuan, a Shatuo, served Later Jin as governor of Hedong. In the 4th year of Kaiyun (947) the Khitan destroyed Jin, and Yelü Deguang entered Kaifeng as emperor (withdrawing north soon after); Zhiyuan, holding Hedong with his armies, watched and waited — "watching the Khitan's changes quietly, taking his realm by the chance." That second month he took the throne at Taiyuan as the realm Han (Later Han to history), keeping the Jin era Tianfu to win men's hearts.

When the Khitan withdrew north, Zhiyuan came down from Taiyuan, entered Kaifeng, and changed the era to Qianyou; he cut away the disaffected — Du Zhongwei and the rest slain — and steadied Bian and Luo. But he reigned barely a year: in the first month of the 1st year of Qianyou (948) he died at Kaifeng, aged fifty-four, his son Chengyou (the Yin emperor) succeeding.

The histories say: "he watched the Khitan quietly and took his realm by the chance." Later Han was a realm picked up: the Khitan destroyed Jin and would not hold it, and Zhiyuan slipped in — no founding of the Five Dynasties came easier; and none fell faster, two emperors and four years. "Swift to rise, swift to fall" — Later Han was the briefest of the Five.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 99–100 ("Annals of the Han Gaozu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后汉隐帝 · 主要事迹

刘承祐，高祖第二子。乾祐元年高祖崩，承祐即位，年十八。隐帝「童騃」，即位后政事委于顾命大臣杨邠、史弘肇、王章等；乾祐二年，河中李守贞反，赵思绾、王景崇继之，三镇连叛，赖郭威讨平之——郭威之威望，自此日隆。

乾祐三年，隐帝听苏逢吉等谗言，于殿上杀杨邠、史弘肇、王章，又密令杀邺都留守郭威；郭威闻讯，起兵南下。隐帝遣军拒之，军心倒戈；郭威军入开封，隐帝出逃，为乱兵所杀，年二十——后汉亡，历二帝四年。

史评隐帝：「童騃听谗，自毁干城。」后汉之亡，亡于隐帝之轻信与滥杀：顾命大臣一朝尽诛，郭威被逼反——「自毁长城」之祸，五代之最。郭威入汴后，先立汉宗室刘赟（后废），旋自立为帝，国号周——五代转入后周之世。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷101-102《汉隐帝纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Liu Chengyou, second son of Gaozu, took the throne on his father's death in the 1st year of Qianyou at eighteen. The Yin emperor was "a child," and on accession left the government to the regents Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and Wang Zhang; in the 2nd year of Qianyou Li Shouzhen rose at Hezhong, with Zhao Siwan and Wang Jingchong following — three garrisons in league — put down by Guo Wei, whose prestige from that day rose daily.

In the 3rd year of Qianyou, heeding the slanders of Su Fengji and the rest, the Yin emperor slew Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and Wang Zhang in the palace, and sent secret orders against Guo Wei, garrison commander of Yedu; Guo Wei, learning of it, marched south. The emperor's armies went over to him; Guo Wei's host entered Kaifeng, and the Yin emperor, fleeing, was slain by the mutineers, aged twenty — Later Han was no more, two emperors and four years.

The histories say: "a child heeding slander, he destroyed his own shield." Later Han fell to the Yin emperor's credulity and slaughter: the regents destroyed in a day, Guo Wei driven to revolt — the age's worst "pulling down one's own wall." Guo Wei, entering Kaifeng, first set up the Han prince Liu Yun (later deposed) and then took the throne himself as the realm Zhou — the Five Dynasties passed to Later Zhou.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 101–102 ("Annals of the Han Yin Emperor") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后周太祖 · 主要事迹

郭威，邢州尧山人，字文仲。出身寒微，「起于卒伍」，以军功历仕后汉，官至枢密使、邺都留守。乾祐三年，隐帝杀顾命大臣，又密令杀郭威；郭威起兵南下，隐帝被杀，后汉亡。郭威入汴，先立汉宗室刘赟为帝，旋废之——广顺元年（951），郭威称帝，国号周，都开封，改元广顺。

郭威在位三年，以「革弊」为务：废营田务、减苛税、去酷刑，「宽仁爱民」，又罢进奉、禁奢侈——后周之基，自此始固。显德元年（954），郭威崩，年五十一；无子，养子柴荣（内侄）继位，是为周世宗——五代最后、最强之君。

史评郭威：「起卒伍，有天下之志。」郭威以武将之身取天下，而能行仁政、革积弊，为五代开国之君中最贤者；其养子柴荣之改革、北伐，皆承其基。后周虽仅三代十年，然「周之政，为五代之最」——赵宋代周，实承周之遗产。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷110-113《周太祖纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Guo Wei, a man of Yaoshan in Xingzhou, styled Wenzhong, rose "from the ranks" and served Later Han by merit, reaching the posts of commissioner of military affairs and garrison commander of Yedu. In the 3rd year of Qianyou the Yin emperor slew his regents and sent secret orders against Guo Wei; Guo Wei marched south, the Yin emperor was slain, and Later Han was no more. Entering Kaifeng, he first set up the Han prince Liu Yun and then deposed him — in the 1st year of Guangshun (951) Guo Wei took the throne as the realm Zhou, with its capital at Kaifeng, changing the era to Guangshun.

Three years he reigned, bent on reform: he abolished the military farms, lightened the harsh taxes, and removed the cruel punishments, "lenient and loving to the people," ending the tribute-seeking and forbidding luxury — the foundations of Later Zhou were laid. In the 1st year of Xiande (954) he died at fifty-one; without a son, his adopted son Chai Rong (his nephew) succeeded — Emperor Shizong, the last and strongest sovereign of the Five Dynasties.

The histories say: "he rose from the ranks with the ambition of the realm." A soldier who took the throne and ruled with benevolence, the worthiest of the Five Dynasties founders; his adopted son's reforms and northern campaigns stood on his base. Zhou lasted three generations and ten years, yet "the government of Zhou was the best of the Five Dynasties" — and the Song, taking Zhou's place, inherited Zhou's legacy.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 110–113 ("Annals of the Zhou Taizu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

# 后周世宗 · 主要事迹

柴荣在位不过六年，却是五代末局里承前启后的枢纽：上接养父后周太祖郭威的草创之业，下开[[n-song-tai-zu|宋太祖]]赵匡胤的统一之局。本页以《旧五代史·周书·世宗纪》为年表主线，辅以《新五代史·周本纪》与《资治通鉴》编年（本地参考库已备）。

显德元年，郭威崩，柴荣即位，沿用显德年号。北汉与契丹联军压境，他亲征迎战，败之于高平，战后整肃禁军，一战确立新君权威。内政上同样果决：显德二年限寺减僧、毁铜佛铸钱以充财政军备；显德间又选练禁军、均定田赋，使国力回升。

南方，他连年亲征南唐，显德三年起兵，四至五年间反复经略淮南，至显德五年南唐献出江北之地，周取十四州，把疆界推到长江北岸——这正是后来[[n-tang-houzhu|南唐后主]]一系被动局面的先声。显德六年，他转而北伐契丹，收复关南三关州县，兵锋直指幽州方向，却于军中病重，只得回师。

回到开封后，他托孤于范质等，旋即驾崩，子宗训年幼继位。次年陈桥兵变，周禅于宋，他未竟的混一之志由宋人接手完成。史家每论其英年早逝：若得永年，宋史的开局或许改写——这桩假设，正是读五代末史时最耐人寻味的关节。

bio_parts_en.value: Chai Rong reigned barely six years, yet he was the hinge between what came before and after at the close of the Five Dynasties: he inherited the newly founded enterprise of his adoptive father Guo Wei, Taizu of Later Zhou, and opened the way to the unification completed under

Zhao Kuangyin. This page builds its chronology on the "Annals of Shizong" in the Zhou shu of the Old History of the Five Dynasties, supplemented by the "Zhou Basic Annals" in the New History of the Five Dynasties and the Zizhi Tongjian (all held in the local reference library).

In Xiande 1 Guo Wei died and Chai Rong succeeded, keeping the Xiande era name. When the allied armies of Northern Han and the Khitans pressed the border, he campaigned in person and defeated them at Gaoping; after the battle he purged and reorganized the palace army, establishing a new ruler's authority in a single stroke. His domestic policy was equally decisive: in Xiande 2 he restricted temples, reduced the clergy, and melted bronze Buddha statues for coin to fund finances and armament; across the Xiande years he further selected and trained the palace army and equalized land taxes, bringing state power back up.

In the south he campaigned against Southern Tang year after year, raising armies in Xiande 3 and maneuvering repeatedly in Huainan through Xiande 4 and 5, until in Xiande 5 Southern Tang ceded the lands north of the river and Zhou took fourteen prefectures, pushing the frontier to the north bank of the Yangzi, the very precursor of the passive position later faced by the line of

bio_parts_en.label: Li Yu, last ruler of Southern Tang

bio_parts_en.value:
. In Xiande 6 he turned to a northern expedition against the Khitans, recovered the Three Passes and prefectures of Guannan with his spearhead pointed toward Youzhou, but fell gravely ill in the field and had to turn back.

Back in Kaifeng he entrusted his young heir to Fan Zhi and others and died soon after; his son Zongxun succeeded as a child. The next year came the Chenqiao Mutiny, and Zhou yielded to Song; his unfinished ambition of unification was taken up and completed by the Song. Historians often dwell on his early death: had he been granted long years, the opening chapter of Song history might have been rewritten. That counterfactual is the most thought-provoking knot in reading the history of the late Five Dynasties.

emperors.bio_md:
# 后周恭帝 · 主要事迹

柴宗训，周世宗第四子。显德六年（959），世宗崩于北伐途中，宗训即位，年七岁。恭帝幼冲，政事委于范质、王溥等宰相，及殿前都点检赵匡胤。

显德七年（960）正月，契丹、北汉联兵入寇（或云边报虚惊），赵匡胤率禁军北上御敌；军次陈桥驿，军中发动兵变，黄袍加身——「陈桥兵变」，为五代最后一次兵变。匡胤还汴，逼恭帝禅位，国号宋，改元建隆——后周亡，五代终，北宋始。

恭帝禅后降封郑王，迁房州；开宝六年（973）薨，年二十一（一说为宋所害）。史评恭帝：「幼冲禅代，五代终。」五代五十三年间，八姓十四帝，「兵强马壮者为天子」——陈桥兵变，为五代兵变夺位之最后一次，亦为宋太祖「杯酒释兵权」之直接教训。赵宋代周，中国历史进入两宋之世。

> 本地参考：点校本《旧五代史》卷120《周恭帝纪》、宋史卷001《太祖纪》（见 `HuangDiTujian-Ref`）。MVP 文稿供闭环演示，精修见史源卡。

bio_parts_en.value:
Chai Zongxun, fourth son of Emperor Shizong, took the throne on his father's death in the 6th year of Xiande (959) at seven. The Gong emperor was a child; the government fell to the chancellors Fan Zhi and Wang Pu, and to the commander of the palace guard, Zhao Kuangyin.

In the first month of the 7th year of Xiande (960), on word of a Liao–Northern Han invasion (perhaps a false alarm), Zhao Kuangyin led the imperial guard north against it; at the Chenqiao post station the army mutinied and robed him in yellow — the Chenqiao mutiny, the last mutiny of the Five Dynasties. Kuangyin returned to Kaifeng and forced the Gong emperor's abdication, founding Song and changing the era to Jianlong — Later Zhou was no more, the Five Dynasties ended, and Northern Song began.

The former emperor, made Prince of Zheng, was moved to Fangzhou and died in the 6th year of Kaibao (973), aged twenty-one (some say by Song's hand). The histories say: "a child in the abdication — the Five Dynasties ended." In the fifty-three years of the Five Dynasties, eight surnames and fourteen emperors, "whoever is strong in soldiers and horses is the Son of Heaven" — the Chenqiao mutiny was the last of the age's usurpations by mutiny, and the direct lesson behind the Song founder's "letting go of military power over wine." With Song taking Zhou's place, Chinese history entered the two Song dynasties.

> Local references: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jiu Wudaishi*, ch. 120 ("Annals of the Zhou Gong Emperor"), and the *Songshi*, ch. 1 ("Annals of Emperor Taizu") (see `HuangDiTujian-Ref`). This MVP text is for closed-loop demonstration; see the source cards for refinements.

emperors.bio_md:
# 宋太祖 · 主要事迹

赵匡胤本是后周禁军将领，为[[zhou-shi|后周世宗]]旧部。建隆元年（960），陈桥驿兵变黄袍加身，代周建宋，定都开封——一个立在五代积习之上的新朝，就此登场。兵变是否预谋，史有争议，此处只作悬置。

开国之后的第一道难题是兵权。建隆二年（961），以酒宴方式解除禁军宿将兵权，即所谓「杯酒释兵权」；其细节后世多有演绎，但收精兵、分事权的方向由此确定。配合抬高文官、分化兵权的安排，「强干弱枝」「重文抑武」成为宋代国势的长期路径，影响远超太祖一朝。

统一战争取「先南后北」之策：建隆四年（963）慕容延钊等平荆湖，乾德三年（965）王全斌等灭后蜀，开宝四年（971）潘美等灭南汉，开宝八年（975）曹彬平江南，[[n-tang-houzhu|南唐后主李煜]]降。南方诸国次第入宋，五代以来的分裂格局大体收束。

开宝九年（976），太祖崩于开封，其弟宋太宗即位。「烛影斧声」「金匮之盟」历来是这一交接的争议层，本页只点到，不作坐实。

bio_parts_en.value: Zhao Kuangyin was originally a general of the Later Zhou palace armies and an old subordinate of

. In the first year of Jianlong (960), the mutiny at Chenqiao Station draped him in the yellow robe; he replaced the Zhou and founded the Song, fixing the capital at Kaifeng — a new dynasty standing atop the accumulated habits of the Five Dynasties had made its entrance. Whether the mutiny was premeditated is disputed in the sources and is left open here.

The first hard problem after the founding was military command. In the second year of Jianlong (961), he relieved the veteran generals of the palace armies of their commands over a wine banquet — the so-called "release of military power over a cup of wine." Its details have been much embellished by later generations, but the direction of concentrating elite troops and dividing authority was set from then on. Together with arrangements that elevated civil officials and split up military power, "strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches" and "exalting the civil and restraining the military" became the Song dynasty's long-term path of state power, with an influence reaching far beyond Taizu's own reign.

The wars of unification followed a "south first, north later" strategy: in the fourth year of Jianlong (963), Murong Yanzhao and others pacified Jinghu; in the third year of Qiande (965), Wang Quanbin and others destroyed Later Shu; in the fourth year of Kaibao (971), Pan Mei and others destroyed Southern Han; and in the eighth year of Kaibao (975), Cao Bin pacified Jiangnan, where

bio_parts_en.label: Li Yu, Last Ruler of Southern Tang

bio_parts_en.value:
surrendered. The southern states entered the Song one after another, and the fragmentation left over from the Five Dynasties was largely brought to a close.

In the ninth year of Kaibao (976), Taizu died at Kaifeng, and his younger brother, Emperor Taizong of Song, took the throne. "The shadow of a candle and the sound of an axe" and the "Golden Coffer Pact" have long been the disputed layers of this succession; this page points to them without settling them as fact.

# 宋太宗 · 主要事迹

赵光义是[[n-song-tai-zu|宋太祖]]之弟，开宝九年（976）太祖猝崩后继位，改元太平兴国。兄弟相传在宋史上是极敏感的一环——「烛影斧声」的当夜传闻与「金匮之盟」的杜撰嫌疑历来聚讼，本页只点到，不作坐实。

太宗在位二十一年，最重要的武功是完成统一。太平兴国四年（979）亲征克太原，[[b-han-liu-jun|北汉]]亡，五代十国割据至此终结；同年挥师伐辽，却在高梁河（今北京附近）大败，帝中箭乘驴车遁走，此为宋辽战局之转折。雍熙三年（986）三路伐辽，曹彬岐沟关败绩，北伐之势自此寝息。

内政方面，太宗崇文右儒，重设科举、修纂类书，文官政治进一步定型；但猜忌之心亦重，打压皇弟、贬斥旧僚，兄弟子侄相继远祸。

# 宋真宗 · 主要事迹

赵恒为[[n-song-tai-zong|宋太宗]]第三子，至道三年（997）即位，改元咸平。继位初期任用李沆、王旦等，号称贤相辈出，「咸平之治」为史家所称。

bio_parts_en.value: Zhao Heng, third son of

, took the throne in 997 and changed the era to Xianping. His early years were served by chancellors Li Hang and Wang Dan; historians speak of a "Xianping golden age."

In 1004 Liao marched south in force. Chancellor Kou Zhun pressed the emperor to campaign in person; Zhenzong crossed the river to Chanzhou and concluded the Chanyuan Treaty: the two states became brothers, with Song paying an annual tribute of silver and silk. The treaty bought a century of peace, though the tribute system remained contested by later historians.

In his later years Zhenzong wearied of rule. In 1008 he fabricated a heavenly letter and performed the Fengshan sacrifices on Mount Tai; the lavish rites drained the treasury and governance slackened - summed up by historians as "Chanyuan settled, then the heavenly letter squandered."

# 宋仁宗 · 主要事迹

赵祯为[[n-song-zhen|真宗]]第六子，乾兴元年（1022）以十三岁即位，刘太后垂帘听政至明道二年（1033）崩后始亲政。

仁宗朝四十二年，是北宋文化最盛的时期：范仲淹、欧阳修、包拯、苏轼等一时并起，台谏活跃，直言成风。庆历三年（1043）范仲淹、富弼等条陈十事，推行「庆历新政」，然一年余即因权贵阻挠而罢，改革未竟；庆历四年（1044）与[[xixia-li-yuanhao|西夏元昊]]议和，元昊称臣，宋岁赐银绢茶。

仁宗为人宽仁容谏，宫女减膳、市井谣谚皆能上闻，身后号称「嘉祐之治」；然因循日久，冗官冗费、边备积弱诸弊未革，为王安石变法埋下伏笔。

嘉祐八年（1063）仁宗崩，无嗣，立濮王允让子赵曙为太子，是为[[n-song-ying|英宗]]。

赵曙为濮安懿王允让之子，嘉祐八年（1063）[[n-song-ren|仁宗]]崩后继位。仁宗三子早夭，晚年养宗室子于宫中，曙即其一，故以宗室入继大统。

Yingzong reigned only four years (1063-1067), and the entire reign was consumed by the "Puyi Dispute": whether to honor his birth father Prince Pu as imperial father. Censors and ministers fought for years; in the end Prince Pu was honored. Ostensibly a ritual question, it was in fact a clash between two principles of kinship - "serving as heir" versus "honoring the birth father" - played out through Song factional politics.

# 宋神宗 · 主要事迹

赵顼为[[n-song-ying|英宗]]长子，治平四年（1067）即位，时年二十，志在富国强兵。

熙宁二年（1069）起用王安石，设制置三司条例司，青苗、募役、保甲、均输等法次第施行，是为「熙宁变法」。新法理财整军，然扰民与夺利之议相随，朝中变法、保守两派缠斗不休；熙宁九年（1076）王安石再罢相，新法仍行而派内已裂。元丰年间更定官制，史称「元丰改制」，强干弱枝之势愈明。

, ascended in 1067 at twenty, determined to make the state rich and strong.

In 1069 he elevated Wang Anshi, established the Three-Service Finance Commission, and rolled out the green sprouts, hired service, militia, and equal transport laws - the Xining Reforms. They rebuilt finances and armies, but charges of burdening the people and seizing profits followed at once, and the court split into reform and conservative camps. Wang Anshi resigned for good in 1076; the reforms continued while the reform camp itself split. The Yuanfeng restructuring of offices completed the recentralization.

Militarily Shenzong dreamed of expansion: the Xining campaigns opened the Longyou lands of Western Xia, but in 1081 five columns invaded Xia and lost tens of thousands at Lingzhou and Yongle. The western war came to nothing, and the emperor mourned the Yongle disaster openly at court.

# 宋徽宗 · 主要事迹

赵佶为[[n-song-shen|神宗]]第十一子，元符三年（1100）即位。他是中国帝王中最杰出的艺术家之一：瘦金体书、花鸟工笔、宣和画院，艺事冠绝一代；但作为皇帝，其政绩却是北宋亡国之由。

崇宁元年（1102）任蔡京为相，立元祐党人碑，禁锢旧党；「花石纲」搜罗东南奇花异石，民怨沸腾。宣和二年（1120）方腊起于睦州，东南大震。外交上徽宗联金灭辽，宣和五年（1123）收回燕京空城，纳岁币而开衅端，实为引狼入室。

bio_parts_en.value: Zhao Ji, eleventh son of

, ascended in 1100. He is among the greatest artists ever to sit on a Chinese throne: the slender-gold calligraphic script, bird-and-flower painting, the Xuanhe Painting Academy - his artistry crowned the age. As an emperor, however, his record is the ruin of Northern Song.

In 1102 he made Cai Jing chancellor, erected the stele proscribing the Yuanyou faction, and launched the Flower-and-Rock Network that stripped the southeast of its finest stones and plants, breeding seething resentment. In 1120 Fang La rose in Muzhou and shook the southeast. Abroad he allied with the Jin to destroy Liao, recovering the empty city of Yanjing in 1123 on tribute terms - in reality inviting the wolf into the house.

In 1125, with Jin armies advancing, Huizong abdicated hastily to his son Zhao Huan,
, and became retired emperor. In 1127 both emperors were seized and taken north; Huizong died at Wuguocheng in 1135.

Li Gang organized the defense and rejected peace terms, but was soon sidelined by the chancellors; the court veered between war and peace, and relief armies lost their chance through indecision. # 宋高宗 · 主要事迹

赵构为[[n-song-hui|徽宗]]第九子，封康王。靖康二年（1127）二帝北掳后，即位于南京应天府（今商丘），改元建炎，是为南宋之始。

建炎年间高宗一度流徙海上：苗傅、刘正彦之变逼其退位旋复；金兵南下，高宗航海避敌，漂荡于浙东沿海。绍兴八年（1138）定行在临安（今杭州），驻跸东南，江南立国之局始定。绍兴十年（1140）岳飞等北伐连捷，郾城大捷后高宗却以「十二道金牌」召回诸将，绍兴十一年（1141）与金订「绍兴和议」：称臣划淮，岁贡银绢各二十五万，岳飞下狱遇害。和议换得宋金二十年相安，然「莫须有」之狱为千古之憾。

绍兴三十二年（1162）高宗内禅，养子赵眘即位，是为[[s-song-xiao|孝宗]]；高宗称太上皇二十五年，淳熙十四年（1187）崩。

bio_parts_en.value: Zhao Gou, ninth son of

, held the title Prince Kang. After the two emperors were taken north in 1127 he was enthroned at Yingtian (modern Shangqiu), era Jianyan - the founding of Southern Song.

The Jianyan years were a desperate flight. The Miao-Liu mutiny forced his temporary abdication; when Jin troops advanced he fled to sea, drifting along the Zhejiang coast. In 1138 he fixed the temporary capital at Lin'an (modern Hangzhou), settling the southern state. In 1140 Yue Fei and others won victories at Yingchang and Yancheng - until Gaozong recalled the armies with "twelve gold edicts." In 1141 the Shaoxing Treaty made Song a vassal along the Huai River with annual tribute; Yue Fei was imprisoned and executed. The treaty brought twenty years of peace, but the "trumped-up charge" remains an eternal grievance.

# 辽太祖耶律阿保机 · 主要事迹

耶律阿保机（872—926），契丹迭剌部人，是契丹由部落联盟走向国家的关键人物。他逐步统一契丹诸部，唐天祐四年（907）被推为可汗，此后连任三届而不让位，神册元年（916）称帝建元，国号契丹（后改大辽）。

阿保机大量重用汉人，韩延徽等为之定制度、营宫室；他创制契丹大字，设南北面官——北面官治契丹，南面官治汉人，这一双轨体制成为辽朝一代的制度基石。天赞四年（925）亲征渤海国，次年灭之，俘其王大諲撰，改称东丹国，以长子突欲镇之。

天显元年（926）阿保机崩于扶余，述律太后摄政定策，次子耶律德光即位，是为[[liao-tai-zong|辽太宗]]。

bio_parts_en.value:
Yelü Abaoji (872-926) of the Diela tribe of the Khitan was the figure who carried the Khitan from tribal confederation to statehood. Having united the tribes, he was raised to the khagan throne in 907, held the office through successive terms, and in 916 assumed the imperial title with era names, founding the state of Khitan (later renamed Liao).

Abaoji relied heavily on Han advisers such as Han Yanhui, who built his institutions and palaces; he created the Khitan script and established the dual administration - northern offices for the Khitan, southern offices for the Han - the institutional cornerstone of the Liao. In 925 he campaigned against Balhae in person and destroyed it the next year, renaming it Eastern Dan under his eldest son.

# 辽太宗耶律德光 · 主要事迹

耶律德光（902—947），[[liao-tai-zu|辽太祖]]次子，述律太后定策即位，是为辽太宗。

太宗一朝最大的事功是取燕云：天显十一年（936）亲征，助石敬瑭灭后唐，册立其为「儿皇帝」，换取燕云十六州，岁纳贡币。从此中原北门大开，辽据长城之险，为宋辽百年之局定了格局。会同九年（946）又出兵灭后晋，次年入汴，改国号大辽，然军纪不整、纵兵「打草谷」，中原民怨沸腾，不得已北返，途中崩于栾城。

太宗在位期间继续推进南北面官制，以汉法治汉地，辽之汉化由是渐深。他死后述律太后立其侄耶律阮，是为[[liao-shi-zong|辽世宗]]。

耶律阮（918—951），[[liao-tai-zu|太祖]]长孙，[[liao-tai-zong|太宗]]之侄。大同元年（947）太宗崩于栾城，阮在军中被立为帝，述律太后欲立其子李胡，祖孙兵争几起，终以太后让步告结。

世宗在位五年（947—951），改元天禄。他倾向汉化，重用汉臣，又屡兴南伐：天禄年间亲征后汉，掠河北州县，与中原战事不断。天禄五年（951）在祭父途中为宗室察割所弑，年三十四。其遇弑之速、享国之短，实为辽室内争之缩影。

Shizong reigned five years (947-951), era Tianlu. He favored Sinicization and Han ministers, and repeatedly campaigned south against Later Han, plundering Hebei. In 951 he was assassinated by the clansman Chage on the way to a sacrifice for his father, at thirty-four - a short reign that mirrored the Liao court's inner strife.

# 辽穆宗耶律璟 · 主要事迹

耶律璟（931—969），[[liao-tai-zong|太宗]]之子。天禄五年（951）[[liao-shi-zong|世宗]]被弑后即位，改元应历。

穆宗在位十九年，史称「嗜酒酣饮，不恤国事」：日晏不朝、昼夜宴饮，政事多废，人主失体。应历年间辽宋关系相持，北汉依辽抗周，边境小战不断。应历十九年（969）二月，近侍小哥等愤其暴虐，弑之于怀州行宫。

穆宗之政与[[liao-jing-zong|景宗]]形成对照——景宗即位后整饬纲纪、用萧绰预政，辽势复振，可见穆宗一朝之失。

Muzong reigned nineteen years, remembered as "loving wine and long sleep, careless of state affairs": he missed court, drank day and night, and let government decay. During his reign Song-Liao relations held in equilibrium while Northern Han leaned on Liao against Zhou. In 969 his attendants, exasperated by his brutality, killed him at the Huaizhou palace.

His reign contrasts sharply with that of
, who restored order and shared power with Xiao Chuo - evidence of what Muzong's years had cost.

# 辽景宗耶律贤 · 主要事迹

耶律贤（948—982），[[liao-shi-zong|世宗]]之子。应历十九年（969）[[liao-mu-zong|穆宗]]被弑后即位，改元保宁。

景宗体弱而志于有为：他用室昉、耶律休哥等，整饬吏治，又任皇后萧绰（萧燕燕）预政，后族同心，为后来圣宗朝之盛奠基。乾亨元年（979），宋太宗亲征幽州，景宗遣耶律休哥等迎战，高梁河一战大破宋军，宋帝仅以身免——这是宋辽关系的关键一战，辽自此在战略上转守为攻。

Frail but purposeful, he employed ministers such as Shi Fang and Yelü Xiuge, and gave his empress Xiao Chuo (Xiao Yanyan) a share in government - a partnership that laid the ground for Shengzong's golden age. In 979, when Emperor Taizong of Song campaigned in person against Youzhou, Jingzong sent Yelü Xiuge and others to meet him; the rout at the Gaoliang River left the Song emperor fleeing for his life, a decisive turn that put Liao on the strategic offensive.

He died at Yunzhou in 982; his eldest son Yelü Longxu succeeded under Xiao Chuo's regency as

# 辽圣宗耶律隆绪 · 主要事迹

耶律隆绪（971—1031），[[liao-jing-zong|景宗]]长子，乾亨四年（982）以十二岁即位，萧太后（萧绰）摄政二十七年。

# 辽兴宗耶律宗真 · 主要事迹

耶律宗真（1016—1055），[[liao-sheng-zong|圣宗]]长子，太平十一年（1031）即位，改元景福，次年重熙。

兴宗好文艺、慕汉学，诗文书画俱佳，然政事平平。重熙十一年（1042）乘宋夏交战之机，向宋索关南十县之地，宋增岁币以和；重熙十三年（1044）亲征西夏，河曲之役不果而还。晚年与弟重元构隙，留下储位隐患。

重熙二十四年（1055）兴宗崩，长子耶律洪基即位，是为[[liao-dao-zong|辽道宗]]。辽之势由盛转平，实始于兴宗。

Xingzong loved letters - poetry, painting, calligraphy - but governed flatly. In 1042, taking advantage of the Song-Xia war, he pressed Song for the ten Guannan counties and received increased tribute instead. In 1044 he campaigned against Western Xia in person; the Hequ campaign came to nothing. His later years bred suspicion against his brother Chongyuan, leaving a succession fault line.

He died in 1055; his eldest son Yelü Hongji became
. Liao's slide from its peak began under Xingzong.

# 辽道宗耶律洪基 · 主要事迹

耶律洪基（1032—1101），[[liao-xing-zong|兴宗]]长子，重熙二十四年（1055）即位，改元清宁。

道宗在位四十六年，是辽朝享国最久的皇帝。清宁九年（1063）平重元之乱；大康年间宠信耶律乙辛，乙辛构陷皇后萧观音、废杀太子浚，史称「乙辛之祸」，储位遂绝。道宗崇佛，建寺饭僧无度；又好儒术，劝学兴教，然政以贿成，纲纪日坏。

寿昌七年（1101）道宗崩，孙耶律延禧即位，是为[[liao-tianzuo|天祚帝]]。辽之衰亡，道宗时已伏其根。

Daozong reigned forty-six years, the longest in Liao. He put down Chongyuan's revolt in 1063; in the Dakang years he trusted Yelü Yixin, who framed Empress Xiao Guanyin to death and destroyed Crown Prince Jun - the "Yixin catastrophe" that cut off the line of succession. Daozong revered Buddhism, feeding monks and building temples without measure, and honored Confucian learning besides; yet offices were bought, discipline decayed.

He died in 1101; his grandson Yelü Yanxi succeeded as

# 天祚帝耶律延禧 · 主要事迹

耶律延禧（1075—1128），[[liao-dao-zong|道宗]]之孙，太子浚之子。寿昌七年（1101）即位，改元乾统。

天祚帝纵情畋猎、拒听谏言，朝政日坏；恰逢女真完颜部崛起，天庆四年（1114）[[jin-tai-zu|完颜阿骨打]]起兵反辽，宁江州、出河店诸役辽军连败，一蹶不振。此后中京、南京相继陷落，天祚西奔夹山，保大五年（1125）于应州为金将完颜娄室所俘，辽亡。

天祚帝被俘后降封海滨王，天会六年（1128）卒于金地。女真之兴虽在阿骨打之强，实亦辽政之朽——一个政权的崩塌，往往先自内部开始。

# 金太祖完颜阿骨打 · 主要事迹

完颜阿骨打（1068—1123），女真完颜部人，统一诸部后成为女真联盟首领。天庆四年（1114）聚众誓师反辽，克宁江州，出河店一战大破辽军十万，收国元年（1115）称帝建国号大金，定都上京会宁（今哈尔滨阿城）。

阿骨打以「以寡击众」著称：灭辽之战由他开创，天辅四年（1120）亲取辽上京临潢，辽之根本动摇。他又创女真文字，与宋约「海上之盟」夹攻辽国。

天辅七年（1123）阿骨打崩于军中，弟完颜吴乞买即位，是为[[jin-tai-zong|金太宗]]。灭辽灭宋的功业，由其后人完成，而肇基之人实为阿骨打。

bio_parts_en.value:
Wanyan Aguda (1068-1123) of the Wanyan clan united the Jurchen tribes and became their leader. In 1114 he swore the tribesmen to revolt against Liao, took Ningjiangzhou, and routed a hundred-thousand-strong Liao army at Chuhedian. In 1115 he assumed the imperial title, founding the Great Jin with the Shouguo era, and fixed the capital at Huining (modern Acheng, Harbin).

Aguda was famed for winning against overwhelming odds. He opened the war that destroyed Liao, taking the Liao Upper Capital Linhuang in person in 1120 and shaking Liao to its roots. He created the Jurchen script and made the "Sea Alliance" with Song to attack Liao from two sides.

He died on campaign in 1123; his brother Wanyan Wuyimai succeeded as
. The conquests of Liao and Song were completed by his heirs, but the foundation was Aguda's.

完颜璟（1168—1208），[[jin-shi-zong|世宗]]之孙，大定二十九年（1189）即位，改元明昌。

章宗是金朝汉化最深的皇帝：他修礼乐、定礼仪、立官制、兴科举，金之文治至此极盛；泰和六年（1206）对宋之战获胜，宋函韩侂胄之首求和，加岁币而订「嘉定和议」。

# 金哀宗完颜守绪 · 主要事迹

完颜守绪（1198—1234），[[jin-xuan-zong|宣宗]]第三子，元光二年（1223）即位，改元正大。

哀宗是金朝末代皇帝，史称其勤政节俭、力图振作，然蒙古大势已定：天兴元年（1232）蒙古围汴京，城中粮尽，哀宗突围出走，天兴二年（1233）奔蔡州；天兴三年（1234）正月，宋蒙联军会攻蔡州，城破，哀宗自缢于幽兰轩，金亡。

金自太祖收国元年（1115）建国至此，凡一百二十年。哀宗之死不是昏君亡国，而是一个勤勉的末帝在时代洪流里的殉葬——「历代人主，未有亡国之恸如朕者」，遗言犹在。

bio_parts_en.value: Wanyan Shouxu (1198-1234), third son of

, ascended in 1223, era Zhengda.

Aizong, the last Jin emperor, is remembered as diligent and frugal, striving to restore the state - but the Mongol tide was beyond turning. In 1232 the Mongols besieged Bianjing; starving, he broke out and fled to Caizhou. In 1234 Song-Mongol forces converged on the city; as it fell, Aizong hanged himself at Youlan Pavilion. Jin perished.

From Aguda's founding in 1115 to this day, one hundred and twenty years. Aizong's death was not a wastrel's end but a diligent last sovereign's martyrdom to the age - "of all emperors past, none knew the grief of a fallen state as I do," his last words ran.

# 元太祖成吉思汗 · 主要事迹

孛儿只斤铁木真（1162—1227），蒙古乞颜部首领也速该之子。幼年丧父，部众星散，他与母亲弟妹在斡难河畔艰难度日，被泰赤乌部俘获、历经生死。他以坚忍和权谋逐步收拢部众，先后击败蔑儿乞、塔塔儿、克烈、乃蛮诸部，统一蒙古草原。

开禧二年（1206）于斡难河源召开忽里台，铁木真被推为「成吉思汗」，大蒙古国成立。此后他东征西讨：大安三年（1211）亲征伐金，野狐岭一战歼灭金军主力，此后连年攻掠河北河东；嘉定十二年（1219）亲率大军西征，灭花剌子模，哲别、速不台更越过高加索，横扫中亚与斡罗思南部。

西征归来，成吉思汗于宝庆二年（1226）攻西夏，次年灭之，他自己亦崩于六盘山军中。其临终遗策「借道宋境联宋灭金」为后世所遵。成吉思汗建立的帝国，是世界历史上疆域最大的连续帝国之始。

bio_parts_en.value:
Borjigin Temujin (1162-1227), son of the Qiyan chieftain Yesugei, lost his father in childhood and grew up in desperate hardship beside the Onon River, captured once by the Tayichiud and surviving by his wits. Through endurance and cunning he gathered the scattered tribes, defeating the Merkit, Tatar, Khereid, and Naiman in turn to unite the steppe.

In 1206 the kurultai at the source of the Onon raised him to the great khaganate with the title Genghis Khan. Then came the great campaigns: in 1211 he marched on Jin in person and annihilated its elite at Yehuling, raiding Hebei and Hedong year after year; in 1219 he led the western war that destroyed Khwarazm, while Jebe and Subutai crossed the Caucasus and swept Central Asia and the southern Rus.

Returning from the west, he attacked Western Xia in 1226 and destroyed it in 1227, dying in camp at Liupanshan that year. His deathbed strategy - passing through Song territory to destroy Jin - guided his heirs. The empire he founded was the beginning of the largest contiguous realm in world history.

emperors.summary: 太祖第三子，1229年即汗位；联宋灭金，重用耶律楚材行汉法，遣拔都西征，帝国达于极盛。
emperors.summary_en: Third son of Genghis Khan, he took the throne in 1229, destroyed Jin with Song help, employed Yelü Chucai for Chinese governance, and sent Batu west, bringing the empire to its height.

# 元太宗窝阔台 · 主要事迹

孛儿只斤窝阔台（1186—1241），成吉思汗第三子。成吉思汗崩后，拖雷监国二年，绍定二年（1229）忽里台推戴窝阔台即汗位，定都和林。

窝阔台一朝，帝国武功极盛：端平元年（1234）遣塔察儿等联宋灭金于蔡州，金亡；嘉熙元年（1237）遣拔都率军西征，灭钦察、破斡罗思诸公国，兵锋直抵波兰、匈牙利。其本人虽未亲至蔡州，灭金灭宋之局皆成于其朝。

内政上窝阔台重用耶律楚材，定赋税、立中书省、行汉法，蒙古由游牧帝国渐向统治农耕之地的王朝过渡。他还主持修筑和林城，遣使联络西方。

淳祐元年（1241）窝阔台崩于和林，乃马真后摄政。其后汗位之争渐起，蒙古帝国向心之势由此转弱。

bio_parts_en.value:
Borjigin Ogedei (1186-1241), third son of Genghis Khan, was raised to the throne by the kurultai in 1229 after his brother Tolui's two-year regency, and fixed the capital at Karakorum.

His reign saw the empire's greatest expansion: in 1234 his generals, with Song help, destroyed Jin at Caizhou; in 1237 he sent Batu west to break the Qipchaq and the Rus principalities, with raiding columns reaching Poland and Hungary. He himself never reached Caizhou, yet the ruin of Jin and the western marches both belong to his reign.

In governance he employed Yelü Chucai, setting taxes, founding the Secretariat, and applying Chinese institutions - the Mongol state turning from steppe empire toward a dynasty ruling settled lands. He also built up Karakorum and sent envoys westward.

He died at Karakorum in 1241; Empress Toregene ruled during the interval. Succession strife after his death began to fray the empire's cohesion.

emperors.summary: 太宗长子，乃马真后摄政四年后即位；在位仅两年，汗位再虚，帝国中枢渐有裂痕。
emperors.summary_en: Eldest son of Ogedei, he took the throne after Toregene's four-year regency and reigned only two years, leaving the succession vacant again and the empire's center cracking.

# 元定宗贵由 · 主要事迹

孛儿只斤贵由（1206—1248），窝阔台长子，曾随拔都西征，有战功。乃马真后摄政四年，淳祐六年（1246）忽里台推贵由即汗位。

贵由在位仅两年：他遣使欧洲教廷，东西交通益通；然与拔都积怨甚深，西巡欲讨拔都，途中崩于横相乙儿（今新疆青河一带）。

定宗崩后，汗位空虚三年，诸王各怀异志，蒙哥方以拖雷系之身份登位。贵由之短祚与汗位之争，实为蒙古帝国分裂之先声。

bio_parts_en.value:
Borjigin Guyuk (1206-1248), eldest son of Ogedei, had earned renown in Batu's western march. After Toregene's four-year regency, the kurultai of 1246 raised him to the khaganate.

Guyuk reigned only two years: he sent envoys to the papal court, opening east-west contact, yet his feud with Batu ran deep, and he was riding west to settle it when he died at Qum-Sengir in 1248.

His death left the throne vacant three years as the princes maneuvered, until Mongke of the Tolui line was raised. Guyuk's brief reign and the ensuing struggle foreshadowed the empire's division.

emperors.summary_en: Eldest son of Tolui, raised by the kurultai, he sent Hulegu west, conquered Dali in person, then campaigned against Song and died before Diaoyucheng at Hezhou.

# 元宪宗蒙哥 · 主要事迹

孛儿只斤蒙哥（1209—1259），拖雷长子，曾随拔都西征，有威名。定宗崩后汗位空虚三年，淳祐十一年（1251）忽里台推蒙哥即汗位。

蒙哥以严整著称，即位后清算窝阔台系异己，汗权复振。宝祐元年（1253）遣弟旭烈兀西征，亲征大理灭之，西南诸部入蒙古；宝祐六年（1258）亲率大军攻宋，入四川，围合州钓鱼城。

开庆元年（1259）蒙哥亲攻钓鱼城，城久不克，蒙哥崩于军中（史传为炮石所伤或病卒）。其一死，攻宋之局遂懈，弟忽必烈与阿里不哥之争随之而起。

bio_parts_en.value:
Borjigin Mongke (1209-1259), eldest son of Tolui, was famed from Batu's western march. After three vacant years, the kurultai of 1251 raised him to the khaganate.

Stern and disciplined, he purged the Ogedei-line rivals and restored khagan power. In 1253 he sent his brother Hulegu west while campaigning in person to destroy Dali, taking the southwest; in 1258 he led the armies against Song into Sichuan, besieging Hezhou and Diaoyucheng.

In 1259, before the unconquered fortress of Diaoyucheng, Mongke died in camp - by cannon wound or illness, as the histories differ. His death dissolved the Song campaign and opened the struggle between his brothers Khubilai and Ariq Boke.

# 元世祖 · 主要事迹

忽必烈是把蒙古汗国改写为中原式王朝、并完成唐亡以来再度大一统的皇帝。本页以《元史·世祖本纪》（卷004–017）为年表主线，平宋一段辅以《宋史·瀛国公纪》《二王本纪》对照（本地参考库已备）。

他的开局是一场汗位内战：中统元年（1260）即大汗位于开平，建元中统，随即与阿里不哥争位并胜出。此后汉地制度逐步推进：至元元年（1264）改元，至元八年（1271）取《易》「大哉乾元」之义建国号大元，至元九年（1272）改中都为大都，政治中心落定燕地。

灭宋是其在位中段的主线：至元十年（1273）襄阳破，打开南下关键节点；至元十三年（1276）伯颜入临安，宋廷降，残部入海；至元十六年（1279）崖山之战，宋亡，中国再度大一统于元。与[[qin-shi-huang|秦始皇]]对读，可见两次大一统之间的长线呼应；与[[n-song-tai-zu|宋太祖]]对读，则见赵宋开国与终结的首尾。

他的武功也有边界：至元十八年（1281）再征日本，东征舰队遇风灾而败，扩张受挫。真正影响后世更深的是制度遗产——行省制与站赤驿站网络塑造了后世的行政区划与交通格局。至元三十一年（1294）世祖崩于大都，成宗继立，混一格局延续。对这位征服王朝皇帝，正统与汉地治理的评价历来撕裂，本页取中性叙述，其历史后效则无可争议。

bio_parts_en.value:
Kublai was the emperor who rewrote the Mongol khanate into a Chinese-style dynasty and completed the first grand unification since the fall of the Tang. This page takes 《元史·世祖本纪》 (juan 004–017) as its chronological backbone, with the conquest of the Song cross-checked against 《宋史·瀛国公纪》 and 《二王本纪》 (available in the local reference library).

His opening act was a civil war over the khanship: in the first year of Zhongtong (1260) he took the throne as Great Khan at Kaiping and established the Zhongtong era, then immediately fought Ariq Böke for the succession and prevailed. Institutions for the Chinese territories advanced step by step thereafter: the era name changed in the first year of Zhiyuan (1264); in the eighth year of Zhiyuan (1271), taking the Yijing phrase "great is the qian origin," he proclaimed the dynastic name Great Yuan; and in the ninth year of Zhiyuan (1272) Zhongdu was renamed Dadu, fixing the political center in the land of Yan.

The destruction of the Song was the main thread of the middle of his reign: in the tenth year of Zhiyuan (1273) Xiangyang fell, opening the decisive gateway to the south; in the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan (1276) Bayan entered Lin'an, the Song court surrendered, and its remnants fled to the sea; and in the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan (1279) came the Battle of Yashan — the Song fell, and China was unified once more under the Yuan. Read against
, the page shows the long-range echo between two grand unifications; read against

, it shows the beginning and the end of the Zhao Song house.

His military reach also had its limits: in the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan (1281) he campaigned against Japan a second time, the eastern expedition fleet met a storm and was lost, and expansion suffered a check. What shaped later ages more deeply was the institutional legacy — the provincial (xingsheng) system and the zhanchi postal-relay network molded the administrative divisions and transport patterns of later dynasties. In the thirty-first year of Zhiyuan (1294) Shizu died at Dadu; Chengzong succeeded him, and the unified order continued. Assessments of this conquest-dynasty emperor — on legitimacy and on the governance of the Chinese territories — have long been sharply divided; this page adopts a neutral account, while his historical after-effects are beyond dispute.

He died in 1320. The broken pact ended the Yuan's middle peace.

# 元英宗硕德八剌 · 主要事迹

孛儿只斤硕德八剌（1303—1323），仁宗之子，延祐七年（1320）即位，改元至治。

英宗年轻有为，用拜住为相，行「至治新政」：罢冗费、减裁冗员、整饬吏治，又议修《大元通制》，锐意改革。然新政触犯权贵利益，至治三年（1323）秋，御史大夫铁失等发动政变，于南坡（今内蒙古正蓝旗）弑英宗及拜住，史称「南坡之变」。

英宗在位四年而亡，年仅二十一。其新政未竟，元朝由是进入皇位更迭频繁、权臣迭起的衰落期。

bio_parts_en.value:
Borjigin Shidibala (1303-1323), son of Renzong, took the throne in 1320, era Zhizhi.

Young and purposeful, he made Baiju chancellor and launched the Zhizhi reforms: cutting superfluous posts and expense, tightening discipline, and drafting the comprehensive code. The reforms struck at entrenched interests; in 1323 the censor-in-chief Tieshi and others rose at Nanpo and killed the emperor and Baiju - the Nanpo coup.

Yingzong died at twenty-one after four years of rule. His unfinished reforms ended the Yuan's bid at renewal, and rapid succession and ministerial usurpation followed.

# 泰定帝也孙铁木儿 · 主要事迹

孛儿只斤也孙铁木儿（1293—1328），世祖之孙，封晋王，镇守北边。至治三年（1323）南坡之变英宗被弑，也孙铁木儿即位于上都，次年改元泰定。

泰定帝在位五年，以守成为务：即位后即诛杀铁失等逆臣，任用旧臣，朝局粗安。然其为人宽纵，用人失察，财政积弊未革。

致和元年（1328）泰定帝崩于上都。子阿速吉八即位于上都（[[yuan-tian-shun|天顺帝]]），而武宗旧部拥立图帖睦尔（[[yuan-wen-zong|文宗]]）于大都，两都之战起，天顺败亡，元朝皇位之争愈演愈烈。

Borjigin Yesun Temur (1293-1328), grandson of Khubilai and Prince Jin, guarded the northern marches. After the Nanpo coup killed Yingzong in 1323 he took the throne at Shangdu, era Taiding.

His five years were consolidation: he executed the Nanpo conspirators, kept old ministers, and steadied the court. But he governed loosely, and the fiscal rot went uncured.

He died at Shangdu in 1328. His son Arigaba was enthroned there as
while the Wuzong faction raised Tugh Temur (
) at Dadu; the Two-Capital War followed, Tianshun fell, and the Yuan's succession wars began in earnest.

# 天顺帝阿速吉八 · 主要事迹

孛儿只斤阿速吉八（1320—1328），泰定帝之子。致和元年（1328）泰定帝崩于上都，倒剌沙等立阿速吉八即位于上都，改元天顺，是为天顺帝。

其时武宗旧臣燕铁木儿在大都拥立图帖睦尔，两都并立，遂开「两都之战」。天顺帝以辽东、上都之兵南下攻大都，为燕铁木儿所败，上都陷落，天顺帝下落不明（史传为被俘或不知所终）。

天顺帝在位仅一月余。《元史》未为其立本纪，正统归于大都一系；本图鉴以准帝收录。

bio_parts_en.value:
Borjigin Arigaba (1320-1328), son of Emperor Taiding. When Taiding died at Shangdu in 1328, Dawlat Shah and others enthroned Arigaba there, era Tianshun.

Meanwhile El Temur raised Tugh Temur at Dadu; two capitals, two emperors - the Two-Capital War. The Liaodong-Shangdu armies marched south and were beaten; Shangdu fell, and Tianshun vanished from history, taken or lost.

He reigned little more than a month. The Yuan History grants him no biography; legitimacy ran through the Dadu line, and this atlas admits him as a quasi-emperor.

emperors.summary_en: Second son of Wuzong, he took the throne at Dadu after the Two-Capital War, briefly yielded it to his elder brother Mingzong, and resumed it after Mingzong's sudden death; he founded the Kui-zhang Pavilion for letters, yet his brother's death remains an eternal mystery.

# 元文宗图帖睦尔 · 主要事迹

孛儿只斤图帖睦尔（1304—1332），武宗次子，长于江南，通汉学。致和元年（1328）泰定帝崩，燕铁木儿自大都拥立图帖睦尔即位，改元天历，与上都天顺帝开两都之战，旋胜。

天历二年（1329）文宗让位长兄和世㻋（[[yuan-ming-zong|明宗]]），明宗即位于和林道中，然八月即暴崩于王忽察都，文宗复位于上都。明宗之暴崩，史多疑为燕铁木儿毒杀，文宗难逃干系，为元季一大疑案。

文宗在位约四年：建奎章阁，聚虞集、揭傒斯等文士，编《经世大典》，文治可观。至顺三年（1332）文宗崩，临终悔让位之局，遗命传位明宗之子，侄懿璘质班（[[yuan-ning-zong|宁宗]]）即位，旋亦崩。

bio_parts_en.value:
Borjigin Tugh Temur (1304-1332), second son of Wuzong, was raised in the south and learned the Chinese letters. When Taiding died in 1328, El Temur raised him at Dadu, era Tianli; the Two-Capital War followed and Dadu won.

In 1329 Wenzong yielded the throne to his elder brother Khuslen (

), enthroned on the road to Karakorum - only for Mingzong to die suddenly that August at Wanghuchadu, Wenzong resuming the throne at Shangdu. The death was widely charged to El Temur's poison, with Wenzong's knowledge or hand - one of the great mysteries of the Yuan.

His reign of about four years founded the Kuizhang Pavilion, gathered scholars such as Yu Ji and Jie Xisi, and compiled the State Compendium - a genuine culture of letters. He died in 1332, having decreed that the throne return to Mingzong's line; his nephew Irinchibal (
) followed and soon died.

emperors.summary_en: Eldest son of Wuzong, exiled to the west, he was enthroned on the road to Karakorum when Wenzong yielded; he died suddenly half a year later, widely suspected poisoned by El Temür.

# 元明宗和世㻋 · 主要事迹

孛儿只斤和世㻋（1300—1329），武宗长子。武宗崩后，按「兄终弟及」之约本应传位于和世㻋，然仁宗背约传子，和世㻋被迫流亡西域，居察合台汗国多年。

天历二年（1329）文宗让位，和世㻋即位于和林道中，封文宗为皇太子。然同年八月，和世㻋宴于王忽察都，暴崩，年三十。史多疑为燕铁木儿奉文宗密令毒杀，事无可考。

明宗在位半年而崩，其子妥欢帖睦尔（[[yuan-hui-zong|惠宗]]）后得即位，元祚复延三十余年。

bio_parts_en.value:
Borjigin Khuslen (1300-1329), eldest son of Wuzong. By the brother-succession pact he should have followed his father, but Renzong broke the pact and passed the throne to his own son; Khuslen fled west and lived years in the Chagatai khanate.

In 1329 Wenzong abdicated in his favor; Khuslen was enthroned on the road to Karakorum and made Wenzong heir. That August, at a banquet at Wanghuchadu, he died suddenly at thirty - widely believed poisoned by El Temur on Wenzong's behalf, though nothing was ever proved.

A reign of half a year. His son Toghon Temur (
) later took the throne and stretched the Yuan's life another three decades.

# 元宁宗懿璘质班 · 主要事迹

孛儿只斤懿璘质班（1326—1332），明宗次子。至顺三年（1332）文宗崩，临终遗命传位明宗之子；燕铁木儿先立明宗次子懿璘质班，即位于大都。

宁宗即位仅四十余日而崩，未及改元，仍用至顺年号。其崩后，燕铁木儿复欲立文宗之子，因文宗遗言而罢，终迎明宗长子妥欢帖睦尔于广西，是为[[yuan-hui-zong|惠宗]]。

宁宗以幼冲即位、旋崩，为天历政变余波中的一瞬。
